items.title: Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026
items.summary: This paper examined the emergence and early spread of the SARS-CoV-2 variant BA.3.2, which was first identified in South Africa in late 2024 and carries a substantial number of mutations in the spike protein relative to the antigens used in current vaccines. Using a multimodal genomic surveillance strategy that incorporated traveler-based screening, clinical specimen testing, airplane wastewater analysis, and community wastewater monitoring, the authors tracked the variant's introduction and domestic spread within the United States and globally. Detection in the United States occurred first through a traveler arriving from Europe, followed by clinical detections and widespread signals in wastewater samples spanning numerous states, with the variant also reported across more than two dozen countries. The spike protein mutations in BA.3.2 raise concern that the variant may reduce the protection conferred by prior infection or vaccination. The authors conclude that continued and robust genomic surveillance is essential to monitor the variant's evolution and assess its potential public health impact.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Mila Shakya, Kevin C. Ma, Laura J. Hughes et al.. Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.
items.summary: This study examined the global research landscape at the intersection of metagenomics, wastewater systems, antimicrobial resistance, and pathogen surveillance, a field that has grown rapidly following the COVID-19 pandemic and increasing adoption of the One Health framework. The authors retrieved over a thousand publications from a major scientific database and applied bibliometric analysis software to map knowledge structures, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution across roughly fifteen years of literature. Publication output grew dramatically over the study period, with the majority of total output concentrated in the most recent years, and China led in volume while Australia and Sweden played more central roles as research intermediaries. Thematic analysis revealed a progression from basic detection of resistance genes in activated sludge toward broader questions of dissemination mechanisms and public health surveillance integration, though co-citation analysis indicated that environmental monitoring and public health literatures remain poorly connected. The authors conclude that the field must prioritize standardizing analytical methods, developing artificial intelligence tools for resistome analysis, improving participation from underrepresented regions, and operationalizing One Health surveillance to translate wastewater metagenomic data into actionable public health interventions.
items.citation: Zheng Y, Ma N, Zhao B et al.. Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.
items.summary: This study investigated whether an existing quantitative PCR assay developed for clinical *Candida auris* colonization screening could be adapted for detecting this multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen in wastewater samples. The researchers validated the qPCR workflow using a wastewater matrix, evaluating its amplification efficiency, sensitivity, and reproducibility. The assay demonstrated high amplification efficiency, excellent sensitivity at very low pathogen concentrations, and strong reproducibility across tests. These findings indicate that the clinical qPCR assay can be reliably repurposed for wastewater surveillance, offering a more cost-effective means of monitoring *C. auris* prevalence across entire healthcare systems without relying solely on direct patient screening.
items.citation: Rodríguez Stewart RM, Litvintseva AP, Chavez J et al.. Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the utility of wastewater-based epidemiology for detecting gastrointestinal and respiratory pathogens in Africa, with particular attention to rapidly urbanizing settings such as Kigali, Rwanda. The authors conducted a narrative systematic review drawing on peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and surveillance studies published over more than two decades, searching major databases and ultimately including studies that provided pathogen-specific wastewater data with clear public health relevance. The review found that wastewater-based epidemiology offers a non-invasive and cost-effective means of capturing both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, addressing the chronic underreporting that plagues traditional clinical surveillance in low- and middle-income countries. Key challenges identified include variability in sampling methods, environmental conditions that accelerate pathogen decay, and inconsistent laboratory workflows across settings. The authors conclude that integrating wastewater surveillance into existing public health systems, supported by standardized protocols, expanded laboratory capacity, and multisector collaboration, could substantially improve epidemic preparedness, outbreak response, and resource allocation across Africa.
items.citation: Bambara S, Isingizwe MC, Adegboyega TT et al.. A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the role of wastewater surveillance as an early warning tool for infectious disease outbreaks, with a focus on its alignment with One Health principles that integrate human, animal, and environmental health. The authors searched multiple major databases and screened hundreds of articles, ultimately synthesizing findings from studies that met their inclusion criteria. The evidence showed a consistent positive association between pathogen detection in wastewater and clinical case counts in communities, with seasonal patterns observed in pathogen circulation and sampling in socially vulnerable areas proving particularly useful for early outbreak warning. Most pathogens identified were linked to respiratory and gastrointestinal infections, but few studies had explicitly operationalized a One Health framework, revealing a gap in truly integrated surveillance approaches. The review concludes that wastewater surveillance is a promising complementary strategy for public health monitoring, while calling for standardized methodologies and stronger integration across human, animal, and environmental surveillance systems.
items.citation: Panigrahi S, Pattnaik M, Pradhan R et al.. Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament
items.summary: This study investigated whether multi-pathogen wastewater-based surveillance could serve as a practical public health tool during a major mass gathering in a low- and middle-income country. Researchers deployed Moore swabs across dozens of manholes at a national stadium in Uganda during a football tournament, collecting and analyzing hundreds of wastewater samples for a broad panel of enteric and respiratory pathogens, including mpox, using quantitative PCR. The vast majority of samples tested positive for at least one pathogen, with enteric pathogens such as Shigella, Rotavirus A, and Enterovirus detected most frequently, while mpox was found in a notable share of samples and respiratory pathogens appeared at lower levels. Multiple pathogens were often co-detected within the same samples, and the surveillance findings directly informed real-time public health responses including sanitation reinforcement, hygiene promotion, and enhanced food safety assessments. The authors conclude that integrating multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance into mass-gathering preparedness frameworks is operationally feasible in low-resource settings and can provide actionable, population-level outbreak intelligence to guide timely interventions.
items.citation: Nsawotebba A, Morunyanga I, Nakintu V et al.. Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament. 2026

items.title: Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.
items.summary: Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a powerful surveillance tool that captures population-level infectious disease data beyond what traditional clinical reporting systems detect. This review examines how analyzing wastewater can identify underreported, novel, and emerging pathogens—including enteric, respiratory, and neglected agents—that are frequently missed by healthcare-based monitoring. Sequencing approaches applied to wastewater have revealed extensive diversity within the human virome and show that multiple viral taxa are often co-detected, suggesting that co-infections may shape viral evolution and disease dynamics. The approach has demonstrated the ability to detect both known and novel pathogens before they are clinically recognized, despite ongoing methodological challenges in quantification and biological validation. The authors argue that advances in long-read sequencing, bioinformatics, and global data integration will cement wastewater genomics as a cornerstone of early-warning and One Health surveillance, offering a scalable strategy for pathogen discovery and public health preparedness worldwide.
items.citation: Greaves JC, Rodriguez RA. Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.. Environmental monitoring and assessment. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission dynamics of co-circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors developed a statistical method that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts and genetic sequencing data to infer variant-specific effective reproduction numbers alongside variant frequencies, going beyond approaches that rely on sequence proportions alone. The method was applied to data from states across the United States over a period spanning early 2021 to early 2022, encompassing multiple variants of concern and interest. By incorporating structured relationships between reproduction numbers across time series, the framework can estimate fixed growth advantages for specific variants that remain consistent across geographic locations. The approach demonstrates that combining case and sequencing data provides richer epidemiological insight into variant transmission than sequencing data alone.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race
items.summary: This review examines the co-evolutionary conflict between bacteria and bacteriophages, focusing on the diverse defense mechanisms bacteria have developed at each stage of the phage infection cycle. The paper systematically surveys surface-level defenses such as receptor modification, capsule production, and biofilm formation, as well as intracellular strategies including restriction-modification systems, abortive infection, and CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity. The authors also address how bacteriophages counteract these defenses through mechanisms such as anti-CRISPR proteins, receptor mimicry, and enzymatic degradation of capsules and biofilms. The review concludes that understanding these dynamic bacterial-phage interactions provides a foundation for developing novel antimicrobial strategies, including engineered phages and combination therapies aimed at combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.citation: Rafwana Ibrahim, Jesil Mathew Aranjani. Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture
items.summary: This review examines the problem of pesticide contamination in agricultural soils and evaluates microbial-based strategies for remediating these compounds in a sustainable manner. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how pesticides negatively affect crop physiology, soil fertility, human health, and broader ecosystem function, while noting that conventional physical and chemical remediation approaches are often inadequate. The review explores how microorganisms can degrade pesticides by utilizing them as metabolic substrates through diverse enzymatic pathways, with particular attention to the enhanced performance achieved through microbial consortia that exploit functional diversity and synergistic interactions among community members. It also examines advances in microbiome engineering, including targeted manipulation of microbial communities and genetic modification approaches such as protoplast fusion, as well as the integration of plant growth–promoting microorganisms in the rhizosphere to simultaneously improve pesticide breakdown and crop productivity. The authors conclude that consortia-based and engineering-driven bioremediation approaches represent a promising and integrative pathway toward resilient agroecosystems, and they highlight emerging technologies, environmental and economic benefits, and recent patentable innovations relevant to sustainable agriculture and ecological restoration.
items.citation: S. Sangeeta Srivastava Srivastava, Rakeeb Ahmad Mir, Sofi Javed Hussain et al.. Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update
items.summary: This paper developed a comprehensive One Health governance index to evaluate how well countries are managing antimicrobial resistance through their national action plans. Using a structured expert consultation process, the researchers integrated hundreds of policy documents, weighted indicators, and multinational surveillance datasets to score governance across all United Nations member states over a five-year period. They applied difference-in-differences and joinpoint regression analyses to examine the relationships between governance quality and antimicrobial use, resistance prevalence, and related mortality. The findings showed that while global governance scores improved substantially over the study period, implementation and monitoring consistently fell behind policy design, especially in animal and environmental sectors, and meaningful reductions in resistance prevalence only became detectable five or more years after national action plan adoption. The study concludes that multisector engagement and robust antimicrobial use surveillance are the factors most strongly associated with improved resistance outcomes, and that sustained financing alongside integrated environmental and agricultural surveillance will be critical as the global community prepares to update its action plan.
items.citation: Weiye Chen, Yige Zeng, Jinxin Zheng et al.. Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies
items.summary: This review examines the central role of mobile genetic elements in driving the global spread of antimicrobial resistance, encompassing plasmids, integrons, transposons, insertion sequences, integrative and conjugative elements, and prophages. The authors conducted a critical synthesis of recent genomic, epidemiological, and ecological research, including case studies of clinically significant resistance outbreaks, to consolidate current understanding of how these elements disseminate antibiotic resistance genes across bacterial species and environments. The review finds that mobile genetic elements act as hubs for the capture, recombination, and stabilization of resistance genes, facilitating the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant pathogens. Ecological pressures such as antibiotics, heavy metals, and biocides are identified as important drivers of this process, and the work traces transmission pathways through a One Health framework spanning human, animal, and environmental contexts. The authors connect these molecular insights to applied control strategies, including genomic surveillance, mobile genetic element-targeted inhibitors, phage therapy, and CRISPR-based interventions, arguing that understanding these elements is essential for mitigating the antimicrobial resistance crisis.
items.citation: Hemayet Hossain, Md. Hasan Ali, Tanvir Ahmad et al.. Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme infrared colors. The authors tested the alternative hypothesis that the source is a very cool brown dwarf by exploiting new medium-band NIRCam imaging obtained roughly three and a half years after the original discovery data, performing careful astrometric analysis using point-spread-function fitting and a robust local reference frame. They detected a clear proper motion of the source over the observational baseline, ruling out any extragalactic origin at very high statistical significance. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identifies it as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K, placing it at a distance of several hundred parsecs and making it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The result highlights the power of multi-epoch JWST imaging for identifying cool substellar objects that can mimic extreme high-redshift galaxy candidates through their photometric colors alone.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Analysis of Architectural and Operational Dynamics of Phishkits in the Wild
items.summary: This paper investigated the architecture, evasion strategies, communication methods, and data exfiltration behaviors of modern phishkits—pre-packaged tools used to create and deploy phishing pages. The researchers collected and analyzed over a thousand phishkits spanning several years, examining their source code, dynamic redirection mechanisms, and the messaging services used to transmit stolen credentials to attackers. They found that while phishkits vary in implementation details, their core functional components are remarkably consistent or even identical across different kits, indicating widespread code reuse. A substantial portion of the phishkits analyzed lacked any evasion mechanisms, and only a small fraction incorporated advanced functionalities. The authors conclude that this predictability and reliance on known techniques makes large-scale automated detection of phishing operations more tractable.
items.citation: Behzad Ousat, Mohammad Ali Tofighi, Estefan Schafir et al.. An Analysis of Architectural and Operational Dynamics of Phishkits in the Wild. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules
items.summary: This paper reports the experimental observation of weakly-bound ultralong-range Rydberg molecules with Π-symmetry formed from rubidium Rydberg atoms paired with ground-state rubidium atoms. The molecules were detected spectroscopically across a range of principal quantum numbers, and their Π-state character was confirmed through the multiplet structure arising from spin-spin coupling between the Rydberg and valence electrons, which splits the magnetic sublevels of the ground-state atom analogously to the Zeeman effect. The molecular binding energy was found to decrease rapidly with a strong power-law dependence on the effective quantum number, indicating that lower principal quantum numbers are best suited for studying these Π-symmetry states. Theoretical calculations based on a Green's function approach reproduced the observations well for the higher principal quantum numbers studied, but showed poorer agreement at the lowest value examined, suggesting that the Fermi pseudopotential approximation begins to break down at low principal quantum numbers.
items.citation: Matthew T. Eiles, Aleksandr Zaitsev, Dominik Dorer et al.. Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Active Control of Extreme Ultraviolet Photon Flux and Resolution with a Plane Ruled Reflection Grating Spectrometer that Measures Diverging High-Harmonics
items.summary: This paper addresses a practical challenge in extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy where intensity modulations inherent to high harmonic generation sources distort measured absorption spectra. The researchers developed a broadband extreme ultraviolet spectrometer based on a plane ruled reflection grating that uses a motorized iris aperture at the entrance slit to actively control the divergence of the incoming beam before dispersive detection. By tuning the effective beam divergence, the instrument can be dynamically adjusted to favor either higher spectral resolution or greater photon flux, with the trade-off between signal-to-noise ratio and resolution mapped through a volcano plot analysis. The design was validated against ray tracing simulations and demonstrated on thin film metallic samples, achieving spectral coverage exceeding thirty electron volts with resolution up to five hundred millielectronvolts. This approach provides an on-demand means to optimize measurement conditions for near-edge absorption spectroscopy, particularly for strongly correlated materials where both resolution and sensitivity are critical.
items.citation: Caleb H. DeWitt, Nnamdi C. Okey, Griffin W. Hancock et al.. Active Control of Extreme Ultraviolet Photon Flux and Resolution with a Plane Ruled Reflection Grating Spectrometer that Measures Diverging High-Harmonics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QMIMO: Circuit Based Quantum MIMO Design with Variational Receiver
items.summary: This paper studied a quantum analogue of classical Multiple-Input Multiple-Output communication systems, replacing the conventional linear channel model with a parameterized multi-qubit unitary transformation in which interference is modeled through coherent quantum interactions rather than additive signal coupling. To recover transmitted information, the authors developed a Variational Quantum Circuit receiver that learns an approximate inverse of the channel transformation via supervised variational optimization. The system was evaluated under realistic noisy intermediate-scale quantum conditions, including depolarizing noise, thermal relaxation, and measurement imperfections, and was benchmarked against standard classical detection methods. The results revealed a performance trade-off: classical detectors achieved substantially lower bit-error rates across most of the tested parameter space but suffered pronounced degradation for specific channel configurations, while the variational quantum receiver maintained a more uniform error profile as channel complexity increased, albeit at a higher average error rate. The authors conclude that variational quantum receivers are best understood as a complementary rather than replacement approach, potentially offering greater performance stability in scenarios involving strong coupling and complex interference patterns.
items.citation: Sayeda Bipanchi Ahmed, Bikash K. Behera, Mandar Thatte et al.. QMIMO: Circuit Based Quantum MIMO Design with Variational Receiver. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tokens: How Vision Language Models Cut AI Energy Costs While Improving Accuracy
items.summary: This paper investigated whether Vision-Language Models (VLMs) could reduce the energy cost and improve the accuracy of large language model inference for numerical time-series data analysis in telecommunications networks. The researchers encoded multivariate key performance indicator data from cellular network sites as two-dimensional plots rather than sequences of floating-point tokens, then evaluated this visual approach across multiple large model architectures on both proprietary telecom anomaly detection tasks and public benchmarks. They found that the visual representation achieved substantial reductions in input token count, which translated directly into measured reductions in inference energy consumption, with estimated meaningful energy savings at edge deployments monitoring many cells continuously. Beyond efficiency, the visual modality also improved accuracy dramatically over text-only counterparts and classical baselines such as LSTM and ARIMA on anomaly detection tasks. The study further demonstrated a practical feasibility advantage, as high-dimensional time-series data can exceed the context window limits of most production language models when represented as text, whereas visual encoding remains within standard limits, establishing VLMs as both a more efficient and more capable modality for this class of workloads.
items.citation: Bhavika Jalli, Nikhil Korati Prasanna, Jayanta Choudhury. A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tokens: How Vision Language Models Cut AI Energy Costs While Improving Accuracy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities
items.summary: This paper reviews the current state and future potential of point-of-care molecular diagnostic technologies in the context of neglected infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance. The authors examine a range of emerging technologies, including isothermal nucleic acid amplification, rapid polymerase chain reaction, CRISPR-based detection, nanomaterial biosensors, and microfluidic platforms capable of delivering near-laboratory accuracy within clinically relevant timeframes without dependence on centralized laboratories. The review also explores how artificial intelligence and cloud-based digital health systems can support automated result interpretation, real-time surveillance, and antimicrobial stewardship. The authors highlight the particular value of these platforms for elucidating drug-resistance mechanisms in tuberculosis, malaria, and bacterial infections, while acknowledging persistent barriers such as clinical validation, cost, scalability, and equitable access. They conclude that the convergence of molecular diagnostics, nanotechnology, and AI-driven analytics presents transformative opportunities for precision therapy, resistance surveillance, and infectious disease preparedness in low-resource settings.
items.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
items.citation: Qi Zhang, Xiajun Zhang, Jie Yang et al.. Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infections in freshwater snails, which serve as intermediate hosts, as a strategy to support schistosomiasis control and elimination. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimizing it for a straightforward single-temperature reaction, and evaluated its performance against conventional parasitological methods, standard PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two African countries. The new assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory conditions, outperforming microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR, with microscopy failing to identify any positive samples at all. The findings indicate that this LAMP-based diagnostic is sensitive, specific, and suitable for field deployment, offering a practical tool for routine surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission through snail host monitoring.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated the use of machine learning to automate the interpretation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostic results, which are typically subject to subjective and error-prone visual assessment. The researchers trained a YOLOv8 object detection model on digital images of LAMP reaction tubes to automatically locate and classify each tube as either positive or negative. The trained model achieved high overall accuracy in classifying test images, with strong precision and recall for both positive and negative cases. The findings demonstrate that this approach is suitable for real-time LAMP diagnostics, offering a rapid, consistent, and automated alternative to manual result interpretation.
items.citation: Mezgebo B, Chaffee R, Castellanos LR et al.. You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated nucleic acid amplification methods that can function across a wide range of temperatures rather than requiring precise thermal control. The researchers developed a LAMP-based amplification approach using a Bst polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability, enabling DNA synthesis across a temperature range spanning from near-body temperature to temperatures typical of standard isothermal assays. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at both high and low starting temperatures and sustained even under dynamically changing temperature conditions. The system was successfully validated for detecting SARS-CoV-2 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic DNA. The authors propose this platform as a promising tool for point-of-care diagnostics and field deployment scenarios where maintaining strict temperature control is impractical.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a novel protein detection method called DISCO-LAMP that combines proximity ligation assay with loop-mediated isothermal amplification, eliminating the need for temperature cycling required by conventional PCR-based proximity ligation approaches. The key challenge addressed was achieving a careful balance between efficient amplification of the correctly ligated full-length DNA product and minimal background signal from the individual unligated DNA fragments, which required extensive template and primer design optimization. The optimized assay achieved femtomolar-level detection limits for both synthetic DNA targets and protein analytes, and was successfully applied to detect Shiga toxin 2 as well as both Wuhan-1 and Omicron variants of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein using an engineered Designed Ankyrin Repeat Protein targeting a conserved epitope. The authors conclude that DISCO-LAMP is a versatile, wash-free isothermal detection platform adaptable to diverse protein targets through pairing with appropriate affinity reagents.
items.citation: Thomas BM, Simeon RA, Yan KL et al.. DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.. Sensors & diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.
items.summary: This review examines isothermal amplification technologies as diagnostic tools for detecting pathogens in both livestock and companion animals. The authors synthesize recent advances in these methods, which amplify nucleic acids at a constant temperature and therefore do not require the thermocycling equipment central to conventional PCR-based approaches. By removing the need for expensive instrumentation, specialized laboratory infrastructure, and highly trained personnel, isothermal techniques offer rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly alternatives suited to field and resource-limited settings. The review covers innovations in assay design, improvements in analytical performance, and the integration of these methods into portable, field-deployable detection platforms. It also addresses remaining challenges and outlines future directions for incorporating isothermal amplification into routine veterinary diagnostics and broader animal disease surveillance programs.
items.citation: Tooryan F, Enyertornye B, Choudhury FJ et al.. Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only bibliographic and administrative information about a report with no scientific content describing the study, methods, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies for detecting high-priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, which remain persistent threats to global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, with particular attention to how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, which enables intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing, effectively transforming conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically identifies key challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, and discusses mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular multipathogen panels, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward robust, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes
items.summary: This review examines neurocysticercosis, the most common helminthic parasitic infection of the human central nervous system, which presents with highly variable clinical manifestations and is encountered both in endemic regions and among immigrant populations in industrialized countries. The authors synthesize advances from the past decade across multiple domains, including improved diagnostic tools such as more specific antigen and antibody detection methods and more sensitive magnetic resonance imaging sequences, as well as updated treatment strategies involving combined anti-parasitic drugs, refined approaches to managing treatment-associated inflammation, and new surgical techniques. The review also incorporates findings from new animal models and emerging data on transmission control. Despite these advances, the authors note that diagnostic challenges remain and that treatment approaches can vary depending on disease type, creating ongoing complexities in clinical practice. The work is intended as a comprehensive and practical reference for clinicians in both endemic and non-endemic settings to guide optimal diagnosis and management.
authors: for The Cysticercosis Working Group in Peru (CWGP)
items.citation: Javier A. Bustos, Christina M. Coyle, Kiran T. Thakur et al.. Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control
items.summary: This review examines antimicrobial resistance as a public health threat transmitted through the food chain, adopting a One Health framework that connects animals, the environment, and humans. The authors analyzed the major drivers of resistance dissemination across animal agriculture, aquaculture, and food processing, while evaluating both established and emerging detection methodologies. They contrast traditional culture-based phenotypic testing with advanced molecular approaches such as whole genome sequencing, metagenomics, and CRISPR-based diagnostics, noting that despite the speed and resolution these tools offer, significant technical challenges persist, including matrix interference, the viable but non-culturable bacterial state, and disconnects between genotype and phenotype. The review also describes integrated mitigation strategies spanning antimicrobial stewardship on farms, biofilm control innovations, and consumer hygiene practices. The authors conclude that bridging technical and regulatory gaps in surveillance is essential for developing effective interventions and ensuring food system safety.
items.citation: Emílio Gomes, Tomás Gonçalves Mesquita, Patrícia Serra et al.. Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci (VRE) in Nosocomial Infections: A Systematic Review of Resistance, Pathogenesis, and Clinical Management
items.summary: This systematic review examined the epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, clinical manifestations, and management strategies for two major healthcare-associated pathogens, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant enterococci, which are associated with high mortality, prolonged hospitalisation, and substantial healthcare costs. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors qualitatively synthesised findings from over a hundred records published between the early and mid-2020s, drawn from multiple bibliographic databases. The review found that both pathogens cause severe infections including ventilator-associated pneumonia, endocarditis, and bacteraemia, with resistance driven primarily by the mecA, vanA, and vanB genes, while biofilm formation independently promotes antibiotic tolerance and persistence beyond classical genetic resistance. Effective therapeutic options identified include ceftaroline for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and linezolid or daptomycin for vancomycin-resistant enterococci, alongside active screening, infection prevention and control measures, and antimicrobial stewardship programmes, though implementation is frequently hampered by institutional barriers, resource limitations, and inadequate staff training. The authors conclude that a coordinated, multidisciplinary approach integrating rapid diagnostics, stringent prevention measures, and sustained institutional investment is essential to reduce the clinical and economic burden of these infections.
items.citation: Peptine Lucian-Daniel, Zaharia Andreea-Eliza, Maftei Nicoleta-Maricica et al.. Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci (VRE) in Nosocomial Infections: A Systematic Review of Resistance, Pathogenesis, and Clinical Management. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the validation of a uranium-based fission chamber detector system designed to monitor neutron output across an exceptionally wide dynamic range during high-performance fusion plasma operations on the SPARC tokamak. The detector employs a parallel-plate geometry paired with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Experimental testing with both types of neutron generators confirmed vendor-specified detection efficiencies and demonstrated strong linearity in count rates, with results agreeing well with Monte Carlo neutronics simulations. The study further assessed the detector's performance under practical deployment conditions, finding it robust against stray magnetic fields and signal degradation from long cable runs. The authors conclude that, when combined with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height discrimination, this fission chamber provides a reliable diagnostic for fusion power measurements.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper addresses how large language model agents can improve their performance on recurring tasks by refining reusable procedural knowledge artifacts called skills, which are stored as text and loaded into the agent's context without modifying model weights. The authors identify two key weaknesses in prior skill refinement approaches: the absence of explicit feedback linking diagnoses to task outcomes, and the treatment of skill deletion as a generic editing operation rather than a principled consolidation mechanism. To address these gaps, they propose SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient optimization that combines a forward stage—which re-executes diagnosis-driven skill edits on the same task batch and rolls back regressions—with a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimates each unit's contribution through leave-one-out utility auditing, and applies gated consolidation or removal. Evaluated across multiple backbone language models on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy, with ablation studies confirming that the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components each contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: This paper investigates how band topology and quantum geometry influence magnetic domain wall stability in two-dimensional ferromagnets with time-reversal-conjugate Chern bands. The authors show theoretically that smooth magnetic textures in such systems can carry a dipole density transverse to the domain wall, characterized by a dimensionless geometric coefficient related to a moment of the second Chern form in mixed momentum and order-parameter space. Because this geometric dipole coefficient is generally nonzero even though the net charge response vanishes, dipolar repulsion can stabilize chiral domain walls against collapse, rendering them metastable even under finite reverse magnetic fields. Applying this framework to a realistic model of twisted molybdenum ditelluride, the authors find that the geometric dipole coefficient drops sharply at a phase boundary within the valley-polarized phase where the Chern number changes, which naturally accounts for recent pump-probe experiments observing a long-lived excitation that survives large reverse fields but abruptly disappears at an intermediate displacement field. The work establishes metastable magnetic textures as a sensitive probe of band quantum geometry and identifies them as an intrinsic obstacle to fast optical switching of moiré ferromagnets.
items.citation: Nisarg Chadha, Qiang Gao, Eslam Khalaf et al.. A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Harnessing bound states in the continuum for quantum and nonlinear photonics in silicon nitride microresonators
items.summary: This paper theoretically and experimentally investigates how bound states in the continuum (BICs) can be exploited in integrated nonlinear photonics, specifically within silicon nitride microresonators. The researchers realized electrically tunable Friedrich-Wintgen BICs in an interferometrically coupled microresonator architecture, where one mode participating in spontaneous four-wave mixing is tuned to the BIC condition, effectively suppressing its radiative loss. Although the BIC mode cannot be directly excited by linear coupling, it is populated through the nonlinear four-wave mixing process and read out via its radiative photon partner. In the low-gain quantum regime, this configuration produces photon pairs with distinctive signal-idler correlations and a signal coherence time approaching the intrinsic-loss-limited lifetime of the dark idler mode. In the high-gain classical regime, making one mode a BIC substantially enhances parametric gain and lowers the oscillation threshold, establishing BICs as a versatile tool for mode-selective lifetime engineering in both quantum photon-pair generation and integrated parametric oscillator devices.
items.citation: Eduardo C. Lima, Marco Clementi, Alice Viola et al.. Harnessing bound states in the continuum for quantum and nonlinear photonics in silicon nitride microresonators. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments
items.summary: This paper investigated whether reinforcement learning in simulated clinical environments could improve the sequential decision-making capabilities of AI agents in medical contexts, drawing an analogy to physician residency training. The researchers developed ResidencyRL, a framework that trains a language model policy agent through multi-turn simulated patient encounters featuring adversarial simulator behaviors, with structured rewards spanning diagnostic accuracy, management quality, communication, documentation, and safety. Under adversarial evaluation conditions, the trained agent substantially improved diagnostic accuracy and reduced rates of missed clinical red flags compared to a baseline model, with blind expert clinicians strongly preferring the trained agent in head-to-head comparisons. The approach also demonstrated generalization, with the agent outperforming the base model across multiple independent clinical benchmarks. The authors conclude that complex clinical reasoning can be effectively learned through simulated multi-turn reinforcement learning, though they note that prospective validation in real-world clinical workflows is still required to establish practical utility.
items.citation: Valentin Liévin, Samuel Schmidgall, Tim Strother et al.. ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Extreme least singular values of random row submatrices with bounded-density subgaussian entries
items.summary: This paper studies the minimum singular value of square submatrices formed by selecting rows from a tall random matrix with independent, centered, subgaussian entries that have a bounded Lebesgue density. The authors characterize the exponential-scale behavior of the minimum over all possible row subsets of size equal to the number of columns, identifying the precise exponential rate as a function of the aspect ratio. To establish the upper tail bound—the more challenging direction—they develop a novel argument combining a local central limit theorem for delocalized directions, an averaged delocalization estimate for hyperplane normals, a bound controlling nearly parallel pairs, and an amplification strategy using independent probe rows, thereby avoiding the need for uniform control over exponentially many random hyperplanes. The resulting deviation probability decays faster than any exponential in the dimension, and under a canonical coupling of the entire infinite array, the exponential law holds almost surely and uniformly over compact ranges of aspect ratios. As a notable application, at the phase-retrieval threshold where the number of measurements is just under twice the ambient dimension, the Balan–Wang stability parameter is shown to have a specific exponential base both in probability and almost surely.
items.citation: Xiufan Yang, Shu Wen, Yitzchak Shmalo. Extreme least singular values of random row submatrices with bounded-density subgaussian entries. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of cystatin C as a biomarker for early detection of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury. The authors systematically searched electronic databases, assessed study quality using an established diagnostic accuracy tool, and pooled results from seventeen eligible studies using a random-effects model, constructing a summary receiver operating characteristic curve to characterize overall performance. Cystatin C demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with the area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity all indicating meaningful discriminatory ability for identifying acute kidney injury in septic patients. Subgroup analyses suggested that studies applying Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria achieved higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with less heterogeneity, and combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further improved accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising candidate for early clinical diagnosis of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, though heterogeneity across the included studies warrants cautious interpretation.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the utility of pancreatic stone protein as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for sepsis in paediatric populations, with particular focus on distinguishing early infection from postoperative sterile inflammation. A structured literature search across two major databases identified studies from a defined recent period, ultimately analysing over fifty publications meeting inclusion criteria. The review found that pancreatic stone protein levels rose significantly in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation and were associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. Its diagnostic performance was comparable to or superior to conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, with particularly encouraging results in neonatal and other high-risk groups. The authors conclude that while pancreatic stone protein is a promising early biomarker for paediatric sepsis, study heterogeneity necessitates larger multicentre prospective trials and integration into multimarker diagnostic frameworks before routine clinical adoption.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the immature platelet fraction—a marker of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity—for the early identification of sepsis. The authors searched two major databases and identified a small number of studies meeting inclusion criteria, then pooled their data to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio, with a subgroup analysis focused on adult patients. The meta-analysis found that the immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy for sepsis, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around the low-to-mid seventies percent range and a combined diagnostic odds ratio indicating a meaningful but limited discriminatory ability. Moderate heterogeneity was observed across the included studies, and the overall evidence base was notably small. The authors conclude that the immature platelet fraction may serve as a complementary rather than standalone biomarker for sepsis, and that standardized prospective research is needed before its clinical utility can be firmly established.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, addressing inconsistencies in prior clinical studies. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched multiple major databases spanning nearly three decades and included controlled studies involving neonates, analyzing pooled sensitivity, specificity, and summary receiver operating characteristic curves. The results showed that IL-27 outperformed CRP on all diagnostic metrics, achieving higher pooled sensitivity, specificity, and a greater area under the curve. The authors conclude that IL-27 demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared to CRP for identifying neonatal sepsis and may serve as a more reliable biomarker to support early and accurate clinical diagnosis.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.
items.summary: This paper examined the current state of diagnostics for neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries, where the condition remains a major driver of infant death and illness despite limited diagnostic progress. The authors synthesized evidence across a range of existing and emerging diagnostic approaches, including clinical algorithms, host-response biomarkers, haematological parameters, continuous monitoring systems, and artificial intelligence-based digital platforms, evaluating each against the WHO Target Product Profile for neonatal sepsis triage. They assessed these strategies not only for diagnostic performance but also for operational feasibility in resource-constrained settings, including suitability for use outside hospital environments. The analysis identified host-response biomarkers with greater accuracy than those currently in use, as well as affordable technologies capable of enhancing existing predictive algorithms. The authors conclude that an integrated approach combining point-of-care testing, routine clinical data, and digital decision support tools—aligned with WHO target criteria—holds the greatest promise for improving early detection, rationalizing antibiotic use, and ultimately reducing neonatal mortality in these settings.
items.citation: Gleeson B, Blumel B, Ibarz Pavon AB et al.. Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.
items.summary: The study investigated whether calprotectin, a neutrophil activation marker measured in plasma, could serve as a useful diagnostic biomarker for sepsis and for identifying the source of infection in patients presenting to an emergency department. Researchers prospectively enrolled patients with suspected sepsis at a university hospital and measured calprotectin levels at admission, analyzing its discriminatory ability alone and in combination with C-reactive protein (CRP). Calprotectin showed modest ability to distinguish sepsis from non-infectious systemic inflammatory response syndrome but was not an independent predictor when CRP was included in the model. However, calprotectin demonstrated value in differentiating lower respiratory tract infections from both upper respiratory tract infections and urinary tract infections, and adding calprotectin to CRP significantly improved discriminatory performance for these comparisons. The authors conclude that calprotectin may enhance identification of lower respiratory tract infection as the source of sepsis in the emergency setting, though further research is needed to confirm its value beyond standard clinical assessment.
items.citation: Wollmer M, Wessman T, Melander O et al.. Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 update to the Surviving Sepsis Campaign international clinical practice guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adults. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse, multidisciplinary committee using the GRADE methodology to synthesize evidence across clinical domains including screening, infection management, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals of care, with structured input from a patient and family advisory panel. The committee evaluated prioritized patient-centered outcomes for each clinical question and applied an Evidence to Decision framework that incorporated balance of effects, certainty of evidence, patient values, resource availability, equity, and cost-effectiveness. The resulting guidelines provide a comprehensive set of graded recommendations and other evidence-informed statements intended to support clinicians in hospital, prehospital, and immediate post-hospital settings, with particular attention to antimicrobial stewardship and applicability across diverse resource settings including low- and middle-income countries. The guidelines aim to translate a large body of research into actionable guidance to improve early identification, treatment, and outcomes for the millions of patients affected by sepsis globally each year.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, containing only background epidemiological context about sepsis and a brief statement on the importance of early identification and treatment, with no description of the guideline methodology, specific recommendations, or findings from the 2026 update.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review paper examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and its dysregulation across a range of diseases. The authors survey the history of lipid metabolism research and synthesize knowledge on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways regulate the behavior of immune cells, including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, in both innate and adaptive immunity. The review explores how specific lipid metabolites influence immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation, and details multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control. The authors further discuss how disrupted lipid metabolism contributes to autoimmune diseases, cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, aging, and metabolic disorders. Finally, the paper outlines current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, including lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches supported by ongoing clinical trials.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026
