items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), a family of immune cell receptors central to inflammatory signalling that has been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was the sole intervention in human participants, categorising the literature by exercise modality and duration into acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training. The review found that acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise showed a more neutral or downregulatory effect, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs were associated predominantly with unchanged or reduced TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change in expression. The authors conclude that exercise and TLR signalling are interrelated in a manner dependent on exercise type, but highlight substantial heterogeneity across study designs and call for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological significance.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities
items.summary: This review examines the NLRP3 inflammasome, a central signaling platform of the innate immune system that detects a wide range of microbial, metabolic, and environmental danger signals. Upon activation, the complex recruits ASC and caspase-1 to drive maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin-1β and interleukin-18 and to execute pyroptotic cell death. The authors provide an updated synthesis of the molecular mechanisms underlying NLRP3 activation, including ion flux, mitochondrial damage, lysosomal rupture, reactive oxygen species, and post-translational modifications, as well as the negative regulatory pathways that maintain inflammasome homeostasis. Aberrant NLRP3 activity is linked to a broad range of diseases spanning autoinflammatory syndromes, metabolic and cardiovascular conditions, neurodegeneration, and cancer. The review concludes by surveying emerging therapeutic strategies—including direct inhibitors, allosteric modulators, biologics, and repurposed drugs—and their potential for clinical translation in inflammatory and immune-related diseases.
items.citation: Chan Zou, Shilong Jiang, Hui Li et al.. The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the validation and characterization of a uranium-based fission chamber designed to monitor neutron emission from high-performance deuterium-tritium plasma operations in the SPARC tokamak across a very wide dynamic range of neutron yield rates. The detector employs a parallel-plate geometry with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons, and its performance was tested experimentally using both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium neutron generators. Measured count rates agreed well with vendor-specified efficiencies and with neutronics simulations performed using the OpenMC code, confirming excellent detector linearity. Additional testing demonstrated that the detector remains robust under SPARC-relevant environmental conditions, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation risks associated with long cable runs. The authors conclude that the fission chamber, when combined with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height thresholds, provides a reliable solution for fusion power measurements within the SPARC neutron diagnostics suite.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme infrared colors. To test whether it might instead be a cool brown dwarf within the Milky Way, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST imaging roughly three and a half years after the original observations and performed precise relative astrometry using a carefully constructed local reference frame and injection-recovery analysis. They detected a clear proper motion, ruling out any extragalactic interpretation at high statistical significance. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identified it as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K, placing it at a distance consistent with the outer scale-height of the Galactic disc and making it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The study underscores the power of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing cold substellar objects from genuine high-redshift extragalactic candidates.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics
items.summary: This paper investigated the sensitivity of next-generation cosmic microwave background experiments to neutrinos and other light relics from the early universe, as characterized by the effective number of relativistic species. Using Fisher-matrix forecasting methods, the authors evaluated multiple survey configurations under consideration for the CMB-S4 experiment, assessing how precisely each could measure this parameter over their respective observing periods. The conceptual design configuration is projected to achieve a measurement precision below a threshold that would constitute a percent-level test of the Standard Model and probe new physics such as light thermal relics and big bang nucleosynthesis. A cosmic-variance-limited forecast was also computed to establish the ultimate ceiling for improvement beyond instrumental constraints. The analysis was carried out with a publicly released end-to-end pipeline tool that handles foreground separation, delensing, and parameter sensitivity forecasting, making it applicable to other future survey designs.
items.citation: Cynthia Trendafilova, Srinivasan Raghunathan, Benjamin Wallisch et al.. Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation
items.summary: The paper investigates the active Cahn-Hilliard equation, a model describing phase separation in systems driven out of equilibrium by activity, addressing both its mathematical well-posedness and the dynamics by which coarsening patterns evolve. Using a novel approach based on heteroclinic trajectories in the phase plane, the authors characterize static kink profiles and spherical droplet states, and develop a theory explaining how activity and local interface curvature modify surface tension to produce a shift in the coarsening power law for the characteristic domain length. This theoretical analysis predicts a transient regime before phase-separated domains reach a finite saturation length, with the coarsening exponent shifting from the classical value to a slower one induced by activity. To complement the analytical results, the authors design and analyze a finite-element numerical scheme, proving its well-posedness and stability for both regular polynomial and singular logarithmic potentials, and establishing local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in two and three dimensions with singular potential, as well as global well-posedness in one dimension under a smallness condition on the activity parameter. Numerical simulations confirm that the scheme correctly reproduces phase separation dynamics and the theoretically predicted power-law shift in coarsening behavior prior to late-time length saturation.
items.citation: Abramo Agosti, Andrea Giorgini. Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language model agents can improve their procedural skills through iterative self-refinement without updating model weights. The authors identify two key limitations in existing skill-refinement frameworks: the absence of explicit feedback linking diagnoses to outcomes, and the treatment of deletion as a generic edit rather than a principled consolidation mechanism. To address these gaps, they introduce SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that combines a forward stage performing closed-loop diagnostic evolution with regression rollback, and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units and applies utility-based consolidation or removal. Evaluated across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks with multiple backbone language models, SkillProx achieves meaningful accuracy gains over the strongest gradient-based baseline, with ablations confirming that both the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.summary: This paper examined the fragmented landscape of open-source tools designed to mitigate risks associated with large language models in enterprise deployments, where manual harm identification struggles to keep pace with production-scale adoption. The researchers developed a structured, taxonomy-driven protocol that maps the capabilities of a set of prominent open-source evaluation and security tools onto the subcategories of an extended AI risk mitigation taxonomy, using a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to automatically extract tool capabilities from source code and documentation. Independent reviewers assessed the reliability of the automated mapping, yielding moderate inter-rater agreement, and majority voting among reviewers produced a solid overall classification performance. The analysis revealed a strongly skewed distribution of tool coverage, with existing tools clustering heavily around technical and operational controls while governance, legal and regulatory, and financial and market risk categories remain largely unaddressed by available tooling. The authors conclude that effective enterprise AI risk mitigation requires a layered architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes, and they offer their mapping framework as a practical guide for identifying gaps in both open-source and proprietary solutions.
items.citation: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj et al.. Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging innovations in diagnostic technologies for urinary tract infections, a globally prevalent bacterial infection complicated by high recurrence rates, polymicrobial contributions, biofilm formation, and rapidly spreading antimicrobial resistance. The authors argue that traditional culture-based diagnostics are inadequate due to slow turnaround times and limited resolution of resistance and virulence factors, which drives inappropriate empirical antibiotic prescribing. The review surveys molecular diagnostic approaches including nucleic acid amplification techniques, biosensor-based platforms, microfluidic lab-on-chip systems, and omics-based methods, with particular attention to their integration with artificial intelligence and machine learning to accelerate and improve diagnostic accuracy. The authors highlight translational applications of these combined technologies for enabling targeted antimicrobial therapy and supporting antimicrobial resistance surveillance, while also addressing ethical, regulatory, and implementation challenges. They conclude that the convergence of next-generation molecular tools and AI-assisted diagnostics represents a transformative approach to improving antibiotic stewardship and clinical management of urinary tract infections.
items.citation: Goyal S, Sharma P, Aggarwal D et al.. Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.. Molecular biology reports. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for faster antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) for *Escherichia coli*, given that conventional culture-based methods require up to a full day and can miss resistance due to intrasample heterogeneity. The researchers developed AI MedLab MS, a diagnostic platform that combines longitudinal MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry spectral analysis with a dynamic relative growth algorithm and machine learning to track how bacterial populations respond to levofloxacin over time, rather than relying on a single static measurement. The platform was developed using a set of clinical *E. coli* isolates and then prospectively validated on an independent cohort. The system delivered susceptibility results within two hours, achieving an overall accuracy of around eighty percent and notably high precision for identifying resistant isolates. By modeling the dynamic trajectory of the entire bacterial population's spectral profile rather than analyzing individual colonies at a fixed timepoint, the approach improves classification of complex resistance phenotypes and could support faster, more targeted clinical treatment decisions.
items.citation: Liu Y, Xie N, Hu W et al.. Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.
items.summary: This paper presents a state-of-the-science statement from two major European professional societies examining the role of rapid diagnostic tests in community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections, developed in the context of an EU-funded project aimed at combatting antimicrobial resistance. The authors reviewed existing literature and current clinical practice to assess how rapid diagnostic tests can support antibiotic stewardship by enabling more accurate and timely aetiological diagnosis. The review evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of these tests, the utility of biomarkers and clinical decision algorithms, and how the introduction of rapid diagnostics changes the understood microbiological landscape of these infections. Overall, the statement concludes that rapid diagnostic tests have the potential to optimize antibiotic use in community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections, thereby improving clinical outcomes and helping to reduce the emergence of multidrug-resistant organisms.
items.citation: Polverino E, De Nardo P, Gentilotti E et al.. ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.. The European respiratory journal. 2026

items.title: Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.
items.summary: This review paper examined emerging rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing technologies and their role in addressing the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the landscape of these novel diagnostic approaches, focusing on growth-based methods and their clinical and operational implications. The review found that rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing can deliver actionable results significantly faster than conventional methods, enabling earlier optimization of antibiotic therapy in severe infections such as sepsis where treatment delays worsen outcomes. However, the authors note that implementation is hampered by variability in test performance, absence of standardized protocols, and cost-benefit concerns. Overall, the review positions rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing as a pivotal advancement capable of bridging diagnostic gaps and supporting antimicrobial stewardship programs.
items.citation: Glover JS, Humphries R. Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.. Clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing (mNGS) for Detecting Pathogens and Antimicrobial Resistance Genes (ARGs), and Guiding Antimicrobial Therapy in Cancer Patients from Southwest China.
items.summary: This study investigated the clinical utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for detecting pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes in cancer patients, and evaluated whether mNGS-guided therapy improved outcomes compared to empirical treatment. Researchers retrospectively collected two years of mNGS results and clinical data from cancer patients at a single institution in Southwest China, analyzing diagnostic performance and comparing mortality and mechanical ventilation duration between treatment groups. The most frequently identified pathogens included common bacterial, fungal, and viral organisms, with extended-spectrum beta-lactamases and aminoglycoside resistance genes predominating among antimicrobial resistance genes detected. mNGS demonstrated high sensitivity for pathogen identification but only moderate sensitivity for resistance gene detection, while mNGS-guided therapy showed trends toward lower mortality and shorter mechanical ventilation without reaching statistical significance. The authors identified older age and recent antibiotic exposure as independent risk factors for multidrug-resistant organism infections, and immunodeficiency as a predictor for opportunistic fungal infections, but concluded that prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the clinical value of mNGS in guiding antimicrobial therapy for cancer patients.
items.citation: Qian Z, Qian W, Si-Wei W et al.. Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing (mNGS) for Detecting Pathogens and Antimicrobial Resistance Genes (ARGs), and Guiding Antimicrobial Therapy in Cancer Patients from Southwest China.. Journal of global antimicrobial resistance. 2026

items.title: Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multiplex molecular panel for identifying pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from positive blood cultures. Researchers compared the panel's results against conventional culture-based methods, mass spectrometry identification, and automated susceptibility testing in samples collected from a university hospital, with resistance gene findings confirmed by polymerase chain reaction. The panel successfully detected at least one microorganism in the vast majority of samples, demonstrating strong agreement with conventional methods overall, including complete concordance for certain bacterial species such as *Escherichia coli* and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. Resistance genes identified by the panel correlated well with phenotypic susceptibility results, though interpretation was limited by the absence of clinical correlation data and repeat culture information, particularly for coagulase-negative staphylococci. The authors conclude that the panel provides rapid and reliable identification of bloodstream pathogens and resistance markers, making it a valuable complement to conventional diagnostics when used alongside clinical context.
items.citation: Çinar C, Çayci YT, Atakcan Z et al.. Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.. Polish journal of microbiology. 2026

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent a comprehensive international update to evidence-based recommendations for the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, incorporating evidence published through mid-2025. Developed using GRADE methodology with broad multisociety endorsement and no industry funding, the guidelines encompass statements across domains including screening, infection management, hemodynamic support, respiratory care, adjunctive therapies, and long-term outcomes. Notable new recommendations include prehospital sepsis screening and antibiotic administration for patients with prolonged transport times, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance settings, tailoring anaerobic antibiotic coverage to individual risk factors, and active fluid removal following the acute resuscitation phase. Key changes from the prior guidelines include a shift away from routine empiric antifungal therapy, updated guidance permitting either invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring in septic shock, and a recommendation favoring crystalloids alone over albumin supplementation for fluid resuscitation. Several prior recommendations were strengthened, including prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antibiotic de-escalation, while others such as norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor were downgraded from strong to conditional recommendations based on updated evidence certainty.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between lipid metabolism and cellular homeostasis, with a particular focus on how lipid metabolic processes govern immune cell function in both health and disease. The authors synthesize the historical progression of lipid metabolism research and detail how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways regulate the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review addresses multilevel regulatory mechanisms—spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control—that connect lipid metabolism to innate and adaptive immune responses. Dysregulation of these processes is explored in the context of numerous diseases, including autoimmune conditions, cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, and metabolic diseases. The authors conclude by surveying therapeutic strategies that target lipid metabolism, current clinical trial progress, and emerging opportunities such as lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms
items.summary: This review examines the green synthesis of nanoparticles using biological entities—including plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and yeast—as an environmentally sustainable alternative to conventional physical and chemical fabrication methods. The authors surveyed literature from major scientific databases to critically assess advances in plant-mediated and microorganism-assisted nanoparticle production, covering the underlying formation mechanisms, the influence of biological constituents on particle size, morphology, and stability, and standard characterization approaches. The review evaluates the functional applications of these biologically synthesized nanoparticles across biomedical, agricultural, catalytic, and environmental domains, with particular attention to their photocatalytic and pollutant degradation capabilities for environmental remediation. The authors identify persistent challenges surrounding reproducibility, standardization, and scalability that currently hinder translation from laboratory-scale studies to industrial application. Ultimately, the review aims to provide a structured critical framework to guide future efforts in making green nanotechnology practically viable.
items.citation: Shoaeb Mohammad Syed, Shivam Kulkarni, Mayur Patil et al.. A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms. Discover Green Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a versatile and sustainable platform for addressing challenges in energy, environmental remediation, and healthcare. The authors survey its synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies, highlighting how its layered structure enables tunable surface functionalization, adjustable band gap, high surface area, and configurable dimensionality from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers a broad range of applications, including photocatalytic degradation of micro- and nanoplastics, toxic substances and volatile organic compounds, carbon dioxide photoreduction, hydrogen production, battery technologies, and ultrasensitive biosensing through surface-enhanced Raman scattering. The authors argue that graphene oxide can function effectively as a standalone material across these diverse domains, distinguishing it from composites that rely on additional components to achieve performance. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and proposes directions for overcoming these limitations to enable sustainable industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that allow these devices to integrate seamlessly with the body over extended periods, as well as multimodal sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The integration of artificial intelligence for signal processing and predictive health insights is also assessed alongside the device architectures that enable these capabilities. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of AI-generated outputs. Overall, the work consolidates progress in materials science, device design, and AI-assisted strategies as a roadmap for next-generation biosensing systems.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the validation of a uranium-238 fission chamber designed to monitor neutron emissions from high-performance deuterium-tritium plasma operations in the SPARC tokamak across an exceptionally wide dynamic range of neutron yield rates. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both DD and DT reactions. Experimental testing with DD and DT neutron generators confirmed vendor-specified detection efficiencies and demonstrated excellent linearity, with measured count rates agreeing well with OpenMC neutronics simulations. Additional characterization showed the detector remains robust under SPARC-relevant environmental conditions, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation risks from long cable runs. The results establish that this fission chamber, when paired with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height thresholds, constitutes a reliable diagnostic for fusion power measurements in the SPARC neutron diagnostics suite.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language model agents can more effectively accumulate and refine procedural knowledge in the form of reusable textual skills, without modifying model weights. The authors identify two shortcomings in existing skill-refinement frameworks: the absence of explicit feedback coupling diagnosis to measured outcomes, and the treatment of skill deletion as a generic editing operation rather than a principled knowledge management mechanism. To address these gaps, they propose SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient optimization that combines a forward stage of closed-loop diagnostic evolution with regression rollback, and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units and selectively consolidates, demotes, or removes them based on leave-one-out utility estimates. Evaluated across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks using multiple backbone language models, SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy. Ablation studies confirm that the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components each contribute complementary benefits to the overall performance gains.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules
items.summary: This paper reports the experimental observation of weakly-bound, Π-symmetry electronic states in ultralong-range Rydberg molecules formed from rubidium atoms, where one atom is excited to a Rydberg P-state and the other remains in its ground state. The Π-state character was confirmed through the observed multiplet structure arising from spin-spin coupling between the Rydberg and valence electrons, which splits the magnetic sublevels of the ground-state atom analogously to the Zeeman effect. The study examined a range of low principal quantum numbers and found that the molecular binding energy decreases rapidly with a strong power-law dependence on the effective quantum number, suggesting that the low-n regime is particularly favorable for studying such molecules. Experimental results were compared against Green's function-based theoretical calculations and showed good agreement across most of the studied range, though deviations at the lowest principal quantum number examined suggest the Fermi pseudopotential approximation begins to break down in that limit.
items.citation: Matthew T. Eiles, Aleksandr Zaitsev, Dominik Dorer et al.. Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.summary: This paper examined the fragmented landscape of open-source tools designed to mitigate risks associated with large language models in enterprise deployments, where scaling manual harm identification has become increasingly difficult. The researchers developed a structured, taxonomy-driven protocol that used a large language model-assisted retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to analyze the source code and documentation of prominent open-source tools, mapping their capabilities onto subcategories drawn from an extended AI risk mitigation taxonomy. Independent reviewer assessment of the mapping protocol showed moderate inter-rater agreement, and majority voting yielded a reasonable F1 score, lending credibility to the automated extraction approach. The analysis revealed a heavily skewed coverage landscape in which existing tools concentrate on technical and operational controls while governance, legal and regulatory, and financial and market risk categories remain largely unaddressed by current open-source offerings. Based on these findings, the authors propose a layered risk-mitigation architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes, and they identify areas where human oversight remains indispensable.
items.citation: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj et al.. Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: This paper investigates how band topology and quantum geometry influence the stability of magnetic domain walls in ferromagnetic systems with conjugate Chern bands related by time-reversal symmetry. The authors show theoretically that smooth magnetic textures in such systems can carry a dipole density transverse to a domain wall, even when the net charge response vanishes, with the strength of this response governed by a dimensionless geometric coefficient related to the second Chern form in mixed momentum and order-parameter space. Because this geometric dipole coefficient is generally nonzero, dipolar repulsion can compete with surface tension to render chiral domain walls metastable at finite size, even under an applied Zeeman field. Applying this framework to a realistic model of twisted molybdenum ditelluride, the authors find that the geometric coefficient drops sharply at a transition between topologically distinct ferromagnetic phases within the valley-polarized state, explaining recent pump-probe experiments in which a long-lived excitation persists under large reverse fields but abruptly disappears at an intermediate displacement field with little change in conventional magnetic signals. The work establishes metastable spin textures as sensitive probes of quantum geometry and identifies them as an intrinsic bottleneck for ultrafast optical switching of moiré ferromagnets.
items.citation: Nisarg Chadha, Qiang Gao, Eslam Khalaf et al.. A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Active Control of Extreme Ultraviolet Photon Flux and Resolution with a Plane Ruled Reflection Grating Spectrometer that Measures Diverging High-Harmonics
items.summary: This paper addresses a practical challenge in extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy, where intensity modulations from high harmonic generation sources can distort measured absorption spectra. The researchers developed a broadband XUV spectrometer using a plane ruled reflection grating, in which a motorized iris aperture at the entrance slit actively controls the divergence of the incoming XUV beam before dispersive detection. By tuning the effective beam divergence across a wide range, the instrument allows on-demand adjustment of the trade-off between spectral resolution and signal-to-noise ratio, a relationship they mapped using a volcano plot. They validated the design by measuring near-edge absorption spectra of thin metallic films deposited on membranes, achieving spectral coverage exceeding the target range with sub-electron-volt resolution, in agreement with ray tracing simulations. The work demonstrates a flexible, rapidly reconfigurable spectrometer particularly suited to studying ultrafast dynamics in strongly correlated and other solid-state thin film materials.
items.citation: Caleb H. DeWitt, Nnamdi C. Okey, Griffin W. Hancock et al.. Active Control of Extreme Ultraviolet Photon Flux and Resolution with a Plane Ruled Reflection Grating Spectrometer that Measures Diverging High-Harmonics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with a focus on their relevance to both food safety and clinical diagnostics. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, evaluating how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic systems. The review critically identifies persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability constraints, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI frameworks, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular multi-pathogen panels, blockchain-enabled data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as the foundation for next-generation, regulation-ready food safety monitoring platforms.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Multimodal SERS Biosensing Platforms: Emerging Opportunities for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection and Intelligent Diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines multimodal surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) biosensing platforms designed to overcome the inherent limitations of single-modality SERS, such as signal fluctuations, matrix interference, and poor quantitative robustness in complex biological environments. The authors systematically survey the fundamental design principles, nanomaterial engineering strategies, and approaches for coupling SERS with complementary detection modalities including colorimetric, fluorescence, and electrochemical transduction. Rather than treating multimodality as mere signal addition, the review critically analyzes how different modality combinations provide complementary or synergistic analytical information depending on the biomarker type and clinical context. The work also discusses integrated devices, microfluidic platforms, and data-driven analysis as enabling tools for converting complex multimodal outputs into actionable diagnostic information, with reported systems reorganized by disease-relevant biomarker classes. The authors conclude by identifying key challenges in material standardization, device integration, data interoperability, and clinical translation, offering guidance for rationally designing next-generation multimodal SERS platforms.
items.citation: Cunming Hu, Ming Guan, Fang Mi et al.. Multimodal SERS Biosensing Platforms: Emerging Opportunities for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection and Intelligent Diagnostics. ACS Sensors. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the integration of recombinase polymerase amplification with microfluidic and paper-based platforms for decentralized molecular diagnostics. RPA is highlighted as particularly suited for field use because it amplifies nucleic acids rapidly at mild temperatures without the intensive thermal cycling required by conventional PCR, making it compatible with compact, low-power device formats. The authors survey recent advances across a broad range of application domains, including biomedical diagnostics, food safety, environmental monitoring, and One Health biosurveillance, with attention to device architectures such as centrifugal chips, capillary-driven systems, electrochemical biosensors, CRISPR-coupled assays, and sample-to-answer cartridges. Emerging trends toward smartphone-based readout, artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation, digital partitioning, and cloud connectivity are identified as pushing these platforms toward greater portability and analytical intelligence. The review concludes that while the field is advancing rapidly, challenges remain in sample preparation, multiplexing, quantitative reliability, reagent storage, scalable manufacturing, and regulatory validation before widespread deployment can be realized.
items.citation: Wang HM, Lee SZ, Fu LM. Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.. Micromachines. 2026

items.title: A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.
items.summary: This paper developed a rapid quantitative test for measuring creatinine in urine, targeting its dual clinical role as a kidney impairment biomarker and a normalizer for urine dilution. The assay exploits creatinine's ability to inhibit hydroxyl radicals generated by Fenton's reaction, which otherwise cleave an oligonucleotide linker connecting magnetic and polystyrene microparticles. By measuring how much creatinine is present through the degree of microparticle binding preserved, and then using magnetic separation on a self-driven microfluidic chip to translate this into a visible bar length, the method produces a direct visual readout. The approach demonstrated a clinically relevant detection limit, broad tolerance to interfering substances and pH variation, and strong concordance with a standard reference method when tested on clinical urine samples, supporting its potential for practical diagnostic use.
items.citation: Hartanto H, Li J, Szeto CC et al.. A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system
items.summary: This paper addressed the fabrication challenges of pyrolytic carbon microelectrodes derived from SU-8 photoresist, which conventionally suffer from adhesion problems, geometric distortion, and limited surface area when produced via two-step pyrolysis in low-aspect-ratio planar designs. The researchers developed a three-step pyrolysis protocol to improve structural integrity and surface morphology of these electrodes while maintaining planar geometries compatible with standard microfabrication. The resulting carbon electrodes were integrated into a polydimethylsiloxane-based microfluidic device and evaluated for hematocrit detection by measuring electrical current responses from red blood cells suspended in phosphate-buffered saline. Surface characterization revealed substantially greater roughness and thickness compared to platinum electrodes, yielding increased electroactive surface area that reduced overpotentials and improved electrochemical performance. The device demonstrated precision and accuracy for hematocrit determination comparable to previously reported platinum-based systems, establishing the approach as a viable low-cost alternative to noble metal electrodes for integrated diagnostic microdevices.
items.citation: Lee HY, Rogers J, Kendrick C et al.. Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and stable integration with the body, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. It also addresses how artificial intelligence is being applied to enhance signal processing and generate predictive health insights from biosensor data. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of AI-derived outputs. Overall, the paper synthesizes progress in materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies as they collectively shape the future of continuous health monitoring.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a major cause of hospital-acquired bloodstream infections characterized by high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of the condition, while critically evaluating the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods that contribute to harmful delays in treatment. The review assesses emerging diagnostic technologies alongside therapeutic strategies ranging from empiric to susceptibility-guided regimens, with particular attention to antifungal resistance and the role of combination therapy in overcoming it. Advances in drug development are surveyed, including pipeline agents targeting novel fungal pathways, and future directions are outlined encompassing artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches. The authors frame this synthesis as a resource for clinicians and researchers navigating the evolving complexities of candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Smart biomaterials for skeletal aging repair and regeneration
items.summary: This paper reviewed the role of smart biomaterials in addressing bone repair and regeneration challenges associated with skeletal aging, a growing global problem driven by demographic shifts and lifestyle factors. The authors framed skeletal aging as a progressive continuum from peak bone mass through pathophysiological decline, characterizing it through the lenses of cellular, matrix, and microenvironmental changes as well as macrostructural and mechanical properties. They examined two primary categories of smart materials: stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems that undergo conformational or phase changes to release therapeutics in a time- and site-specific manner, and smart scaffolds engineered to respond to endogenous disease microenvironments or external physical triggers to release bioactive factors and support tissue regeneration. The paper also surveyed manufacturing techniques for these materials and discussed their potential for personalized and targeted therapies. Key challenges and future directions for clinical translation were outlined, positioning smart biomaterials as promising tools for overcoming the limitations of current degenerative bone treatment strategies.
items.citation: Dingfa Liang, Hufei Wang, Yu Jiang et al.. Smart biomaterials for skeletal aging repair and regeneration. Bone Research. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the characterization of a prototype uranium-238 fission chamber designed to monitor neutron yields across the wide dynamic range expected during high-performance deuterium-tritium plasma operations on the SPARC tokamak. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons, and was tested using both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium neutron generators. Experimental measurements confirmed vendor-specified detection efficiencies and demonstrated excellent linearity, with results showing strong agreement with neutronics simulations performed using OpenMC. The study further assessed the detector's resilience to practical deployment challenges, including exposure to stray magnetic fields and signal degradation from long cable runs, finding the design to be robust under these conditions. The results establish the fission chamber as a reliable component of the planned SPARC neutron diagnostic suite, capable of supporting fusion power measurements when combined with appropriate shielding and pulse height discrimination.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language model agents can improve their performance on recurring tasks by refining reusable procedural knowledge artifacts called skills. The authors developed SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that combines a forward stage of closed-loop diagnostic evolution—where diagnosis-driven edits are re-executed on the same task batch with regression rollback—and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimates their utility through leave-one-out auditing, and applies validation-gated consolidation or removal. The approach is motivated by a composite objective that balances task performance against skill complexity, addressing limitations in prior methods that lacked explicit diagnosis-outcome feedback loops and treated deletion as a generic edit rather than a principled consolidation mechanism. Experiments across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks using multiple backbone language models showed that SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy, with ablations confirming that the two stages contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: This paper investigates how band topology and quantum geometry influence the stability of magnetic domain structures in two-dimensional ferromagnets with conjugate Chern bands related by time-reversal symmetry. The authors show that smooth magnetic textures in such systems can carry a nonzero electric dipole density transverse to domain walls, even though the net charge response vanishes, with the strength of this effect characterized by a dimensionless geometric coefficient related to a moment of the second Chern form in mixed momentum and order-parameter space. Because this dipole decoration generates repulsive interactions, domain walls can become metastable at finite radius even under an applied Zeeman field, representing a purely quantum-geometric mechanism for metastability. Applying this framework to a realistic model of twisted molybdenum ditelluride, the authors find that the geometric coefficient drops sharply at a transition between topologically distinct ferromagnetic phases within the valley-polarized state, explaining recent pump-probe experiments in which a long-lived magnetic excitation persists under large reverse fields but abruptly disappears at an intermediate displacement field with little change in conventional magnetic observables. The work establishes metastable spin textures as sensitive probes of band quantum geometry and identifies them as an intrinsic obstacle to fast optical switching of moiré ferromagnets.
items.citation: Nisarg Chadha, Qiang Gao, Eslam Khalaf et al.. A quantum geometric mechanism for chiral domain wall metastability: Application to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Designer Codes from GALA: Compact, Self-Dual, and Rate-1/2 QEC on Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of implementing quantum error correction on near-term reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays, which are limited to hundreds of qubits and constrained hardware connectivity from a small number of acousto-optic deflectors. The authors introduce GALA codes, a family constructed via group-action lifts over product groups combining a small non-abelian factor for achieving rate-one-half with above-weight distance and a large abelian factor that naturally yields hardware-compatible gate schedules. By treating hardware compatibility and logical gate capability as design inputs rather than post-hoc properties, GALA codes function as genuinely designer quantum low-density parity-check codes. The construction encompasses previously known rate-one-half codes while providing simpler parameter bounds and explicit transversal Clifford gate implementations compatible with the folded-transversal approach. The search produces several compact, self-dual codes achieving very low logical error rates at practical physical error rates, including codes that break previously known rate-one-half size barriers while maintaining hardware-compatible cycle times.
items.citation: Willers Yang, Casey Duckering, Arpit Dua. Designer Codes from GALA: Compact, Self-Dual, and Rate-1/2 QEC on Reconfigurable Atom Arrays. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Harnessing bound states in the continuum for quantum and nonlinear photonics in silicon nitride microresonators
items.summary: This paper investigates how bound states in the continuum can be exploited to engineer nonlinear optical processes in integrated photonic devices, specifically within silicon nitride microresonators. The researchers theoretically and experimentally realized electrically tunable Friedrich-Wintgen bound states in the continuum by interferometrically coupling microresonators, achieving extremely high quality factors while keeping the structure reconfigurable. A key finding is that tuning only the idler mode to the bound state in the continuum condition—making it effectively dark to linear excitation—profoundly alters the nonlinear dynamics of spontaneous four-wave mixing, since the bound state can still be populated and read out through the nonlinear interaction with its radiative partner mode. In the low-gain quantum regime, this configuration produces photon pairs with distinctive spectral and correlation signatures, with the extracted signal exhibiting a coherence time approaching the intrinsic-loss-limited lifetime of the dark idler. In the high-gain classical regime, the bound state in the continuum substantially enhances parametric gain and reduces the oscillation threshold, establishing this approach as a powerful method for mode-selective lifetime engineering in integrated nonlinear and quantum photonic devices.
items.citation: Eduardo C. Lima, Marco Clementi, Alice Viola et al.. Harnessing bound states in the continuum for quantum and nonlinear photonics in silicon nitride microresonators. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cloud-Boosted Low-Compute Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of running high-quality speech enhancement on wearable devices, where real-time and low-compute constraints limit what can be achieved on-device alone. The authors propose a collaborative framework in which a capable cloud-based server assists a lightweight edge model through three mechanisms: using delayed server outputs as supplementary input, transferring intermediate feature representations from the server to guide edge inference, and combining covariance matrices from both models to improve multichannel beamforming via a collaborative Wiener filtering approach. This builds on prior Knowledge Boosting work, which had shown limited gains specifically for speech enhancement tasks. The proposed framework is shown to substantially outperform an edge-only baseline while incurring minimal additional computational cost on the device.
items.citation: Xulin Fan, Juan Azcarreta, Ashutosh Pandey et al.. Cloud-Boosted Low-Compute Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform with broad applicability across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The paper surveys the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies that underpin graphene oxide's tuneable characteristics, including its adjustable band gap, high surface area, structural flexibility, and capacity for surface functionalization across dimensional configurations ranging from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers applications in environmental remediation such as adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of plastics, pathogens, and toxic compounds, as well as energy-related uses including photocatalytic hydrogen production, carbon dioxide reduction, and battery technologies. Additional coverage extends to sensing platforms, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for ultrasensitive molecular detection and gas sensing, alongside healthcare applications. The authors also identify persistent challenges facing graphene oxide, namely scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, and propose possible solutions toward sustainable and industrially viable deployment of the material.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026
