items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which remain significant threats to global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, with particular attention to how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically evaluates biosensor design principles, signal transduction mechanisms, and performance validation across diverse food environments, while identifying persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, along with mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing and explainable AI. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular multiplexed pathogen panels, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a major cause of hospital-acquired bloodstream infections that carries high mortality and significant healthcare costs. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside an evaluation of both conventional and emerging diagnostic technologies and their respective limitations. Therapeutic strategies are analyzed comprehensively, encompassing empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to the potential of combination therapy. The review also surveys advances in antifungal drug development, including agents in clinical trials and compounds directed at novel fungal pathways. Looking ahead, the authors identify artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment strategies as promising future directions for improving candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.
items.summary: This paper developed biosensors to detect viral protease activity within living cells and to screen antiviral drug candidates more accurately than existing methods. The researchers engineered two modular biosensors based on split ascorbate peroxidase (APEX) fragments, designed so that cleavage of a target recognition sequence by a viral protease triggers reassembly of the enzyme, restores its activity, and produces an amplified fluorescent signal. Using the coronavirus main protease as a model system, one sensor achieved an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio for enzymatic detection, while the other successfully avoided false positives arising from non-specific conformational interference that plagues traditional fluorescent protein and FRET-based assays, correctly identifying known potent inhibitors. Because the protease recognition sequence within the biosensors can be swapped out, the platform is modular and was adapted to detect proteases from multiple coronaviruses and other viruses including Enterovirus 71, Epstein-Barr virus, and Hepatitis A virus. The authors conclude that this intracellular screening platform offers a reliable and broadly applicable tool for evaluating antiviral compounds and accelerating the development of broad-spectrum therapeutics.
items.citation: Li B, Dong B, Chen Y et al.. A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.. Virologica Sinica. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a rapid molecular diagnostic assay for detecting *Escherichia coli* in neonates with suspected sepsis or bacterial meningitis, addressing limitations of conventional culture methods including slow turnaround time and poor sensitivity. The researchers designed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay paired with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using a multi-primer set optimized for isothermal amplification, with the entire workflow completable in approximately one hour. The assay achieved femtogram-level sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* organisms, and when evaluated on clinical sterile body fluid specimens from neonates, it showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR while detecting a substantially higher proportion of positive samples than conventional culture. These findings suggest the MCDA-LFB assay offers a sensitive, rapid, and operationally simple approach to *E. coli* detection that is well-suited to point-of-care and resource-limited settings for early neonatal sepsis diagnosis.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major cause of foodborne illness, by developing a biosensor that integrates multiple signal amplification strategies. The platform combines DNAzyme-catalyzed cleavage, which generates single-stranded DNA to trigger hybridization chain reaction amplification using three DNA hairpin structures, followed by CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated cleavage of the resulting DNA nanowires to restore a quenched fluorescence signal. This cascade converts a low-abundance bacterial target into a highly enriched detectable signal, achieving an exceptionally low limit of detection in a broad linear range spanning several orders of magnitude in colony-forming units. The biosensor demonstrated straightforward operation, rapid response, and high sensitivity under optimized conditions. The authors also propose that the platform is adaptable to detecting other foodborne pathogens by substituting the recognition module and primer sequences.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a major foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor capable of simultaneously targeting two key genetic markers that define its serotype. The approach exploited the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins to establish dual fluorescence channels, integrating gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing into a single reaction tube. This design eliminated the need for complex equipment, reduced contamination risk, and achieved high sensitivity at a low detection limit using fecal samples from a mouse infection model, with results consistent with standard PCR. Compared to conventional CRISPR diagnostics, the dual-channel strategy improved serotype discrimination and specificity while remaining simple and field-deployable. The authors conclude that this biosensor offers a promising platform for food safety monitoring, clinical diagnostics, and infectious-disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor platform designed to rapidly detect antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets at the point of care. The researchers used disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which were immobilized through π-π stacking to preserve the electrode's electronic properties and high surface area without requiring on-surface chemical reactions. A key advance was a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduced sensor preparation time from many hours to just minutes while maintaining detection performance, enabling amplification-free and label-free identification of both the colistin resistance gene and, through simple probe swapping, a carbapenem resistance gene. The biosensor showed strong discrimination between complementary and non-complementary sequences and achieved low detection limits for both synthetic DNA and bacterial plasmids. The platform demonstrated reproducible performance across independently fabricated sensors, positioning it as a scalable approach for decentralized diagnostics targeting antimicrobial resistance and pandemic preparedness.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.
items.summary: This review examines biosensor technologies developed for detecting two major foodborne pathogens, *Salmonella* spp. and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which are among the leading causes of foodborne illness and death globally. Rather than surveying biosensing broadly across many pathogens, the authors provide a pathogen-specific comparison of bioreceptor development and transducer choices tailored to these two organisms. The review also addresses, for the first time, how artificial intelligence tools can be applied to accelerate biosensor design, optimization, and decision-making specifically for these pathogens. A central focus is bridging the gap between laboratory-scale research and practical implementation by critically evaluating which strategies hold genuine potential for scalability, portability, and routine deployment in the food industry. The authors present the review as a practical roadmap intended to direct future research toward field-ready, industry-relevant biosensing solutions.
items.citation: Gumush SE, Al-Attar R, Sandbecker E et al.. Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.. Food chemistry. Molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual nature of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they serve as essential signaling molecules at physiological concentrations but drive disease when produced in excess or dysregulated. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the major types, sources, and normal physiological functions of reactive oxygen species, as well as the molecular pathways through which redox imbalance causes cellular damage and signaling dysfunction. The review evaluates both established and emerging methods for detecting and quantifying oxidative stress in clinical and preclinical settings, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. The contribution of oxidative stress to the pathophysiology of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders is surveyed. The authors conclude by outlining future directions in precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based therapeutic and diagnostic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and translational barriers of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, which have attracted interest due to their biocompatibility, cargo-carrying capacity, and ability to traverse biological barriers. The authors systematically identify the core obstacles preventing most EV therapies from advancing beyond preclinical stages, including difficulties in isolation, storage stability, characterization, biosafety evaluation, and quality control. They then survey emerging technologies intended to address these bottlenecks, such as advanced bioreactors for scalable production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis tools to handle population heterogeneity, and machine learning approaches to improve standardization and clinical decision support. The review concludes by outlining future directions centered on harmonizing production standards, strengthening safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the authors argue that tackling these interconnected technical and regulatory challenges is essential to bring EV-based therapies into routine clinical use.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.
items.summary: This study examined the diagnostic performance and economic implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR panels used to detect pathogens in acute infections across four clinical syndromes at a southern Italian hospital over nearly two years. The researchers retrospectively analyzed all tests run using panels targeting central nervous system, upper respiratory, lower respiratory, and gastrointestinal infections, removing duplicate determinations so each unit of analysis represented a distinct diagnostic episode. They found that nearly three-fifths of all determinations returned entirely negative results, with striking variation by panel type: the meningitis/encephalitis panel was negative in the vast majority of cases while the pneumonia panel showed far higher positivity rates, highlighting highly uneven diagnostic appropriateness across syndromes. Key pathogen findings included viral predominance in central nervous system infections, rhinovirus/enterovirus dominance in respiratory specimens, resistance marker clustering in Enterobacterales co-infections on the pneumonia panel, and diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes as the leading gastrointestinal agents. Based on these findings, the authors advocate for clinical gating criteria before ordering certain panels, tiered respiratory testing algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A specimens to close a surveillance gap for novel or zoonotic strains.
items.citation: Chirizzi D, Spedicato A, Bianco G et al.. Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the epidemiology of respiratory pathogens in children presenting with fever or respiratory symptoms at a hospital in Guangzhou, China. Using a consistent multiplex PCR panel applied to nasopharyngeal swabs, researchers retrospectively compared pathogen detection patterns in a season-matched design, contrasting the same months before and after restrictions were lifted. Following the lifting of restrictions, detection rates of Influenza A, RSV, and human rhinovirus increased substantially, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined markedly. The post-restriction period also featured a younger patient composition and higher proportions of wheezing and lower respiratory tract diagnoses among tested children. The authors conclude that pediatric respiratory pathogen activity shifted meaningfully after restrictions were relaxed, while cautioning that causal attribution is limited by residual confounding from seasonality, ongoing SARS-CoV-2 circulation, and changes in healthcare-seeking behavior.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adult inpatients at a regional hospital in Chiang Mai using multiplex real-time PCR capable of detecting a broad panel of respiratory pathogens. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus being the most commonly identified agents, and co-infections occurring in a notable proportion of cases. Seasonal patterns were observed, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated throughout the study period. The authors conclude that expanded and rapid molecular diagnostics are needed given the high rate of empiric antibiotic use and the substantial proportion of cases that remained unexplained, possibly due to untested bacterial or fungal pathogens.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper addresses the bioinformatics bottleneck in real-time pathogen detection using Oxford Nanopore sequencing technologies for syndromic surveillance. The authors developed a visualization tool adapted from existing RAMPART software that integrates multiplex PCR amplicon panels with long-read nanopore sequencing to enable rapid taxonomic assignment of pathogens from raw sequencing data within minutes. The tool provides a dynamic interface for tracking sequencing runs and amplicon coverage in real time, supporting diagnostic workflows in clinical or field settings. Validation using complex clinical and environmental samples demonstrated that the system reliably identified all pathogens present, confirming its accuracy for syndromic surveillance applications. The authors present this as an accessible, user-friendly solution for genomic pathogen monitoring relevant to outbreak response and the surveillance of emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.
items.citation: Lechat P, Kwasiborski A, Vincent R et al.. VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England). 2026

items.title: Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the BioFire FilmArray RP2.1 plus, a multiplex PCR panel capable of detecting twenty respiratory pathogens, and explored whether its cycle threshold values could serve as a semi-quantitative measure of pathogen load. Using a retrospective design, the researchers tested clinical specimens on the BioFire platform and compared results against established comparator assays, including Cepheid Xpert/Xpress and in-house real-time PCR methods, generating several hundred PCR results across both qualitative and quantitative analyses. The BioFire panel showed excellent overall qualitative agreement with comparator methods, with most discordant results occurring in samples containing low pathogen loads, and a small number of specimens were detected by BioFire but missed by comparator assays. Exploratory quantitative analyses revealed strong correlations between BioFire-derived cycle threshold values and those from reference platforms, suggesting a reproducible relationship that could support semi-quantitative interpretation. The authors caution that the quantitative findings are preliminary given the exploratory study design and the inherent challenges of comparing cycle threshold values across different PCR platforms.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Vitale A, Mahler Z, Loup V et al.. Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.
items.summary: This study addressed the diagnostic challenge of bovine respiratory disease in Brazil, where prior molecular investigations relied solely on single-pathogen assays, by developing and validating a multiplex quantitative real-time PCR platform capable of simultaneously detecting ten viral and bacterial pathogens associated with the disease. The researchers standardized the assay system across multiple multiplex configurations, evaluated its analytical performance through standard curve analysis and repeatability testing, and applied it to nasal swab samples collected from dairy cattle in southern Brazil. The platform demonstrated robust sensitivity and efficiency across all targeted pathogens, with performance comparable between singleplex and multiplex formats. Field application revealed that the majority of sampled cattle were positive for at least one pathogen, with bacterial agents being most prevalent, and that pathogen detection patterns were significantly influenced by animal age, season, and farm-level factors. The authors present this as the first validated multiplex quantitative PCR system for bovine respiratory disease diagnostics in Brazil, offering a cost-effective tool for advancing understanding of the disease's pathogenesis and epidemiology in the region.
items.citation: Rodriguez MC, Silva IV, Perotta JH et al.. Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America
items.summary: This study investigated the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 into Antarctica, focusing on outbreaks observed across two consecutive austral summers in the South Shetland Islands. The researchers performed whole-genome sequencing, mutational profiling, and phylogenetic analysis on viral samples collected from carcasses of eight species, including multiple seabirds and marine mammals. Their analyses revealed that the viruses detected did not stem from a single introduction but instead represented multiple independent incursion events from South America. One viral cluster linked gulls, skuas, fur seals, and other hosts to H5N1 strains circulating in South American marine mammals, while a second cluster connected petrels, shags, and skuas to strains previously identified in South Georgia. These findings demonstrate extensive epidemiological connectivity between South America and Antarctica, with South Georgia acting as an intermediate hub facilitating the southward movement of the virus.
items.citation: Maria Ogrzewalska, Ralph Eric Thijl Vanstreels, Elisa Cavalcante Pereira et al.. Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: This paper examines the genus *Enterococcus*, commensal bacteria found in the gastrointestinal tracts of humans and animals, diverse food sources, and environmental settings, focusing on their dual role as potentially beneficial microorganisms and sources of safety concern. The authors reviewed evidence for how certain enterococcal strains function as probiotics, protective cultures, and antibiotic alternatives, contributing to pathogen control, microbiome modulation, food fermentation, and the production of bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins. At the same time, the review addresses the risks posed by these organisms, particularly their involvement in healthcare-associated infections and their capacity to harbor and disseminate antimicrobial resistance determinants. The paper synthesizes this evidence into a comprehensive overview intended to guide future research, inform regulatory assessments, and support responsible application of enterococci in both agrifood and clinical contexts. The authors argue that rigorous safety evaluations are essential before enterococci can be widely adopted in any of these roles.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci (VRE) in Nosocomial Infections: A Systematic Review of Resistance, Pathogenesis, and Clinical Management
items.summary: This systematic review examined the epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, clinical manifestations, and management strategies for two major healthcare-associated pathogens, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant enterococci, which impose substantial burdens of mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and healthcare costs globally. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors qualitatively synthesized data from over a hundred records published between recent years, drawn from multiple bibliographic databases. The review found that both pathogens are implicated in severe infections including ventilator-associated pneumonia, endocarditis, and bacteraemia, with resistance driven by key genes such as mecA, vanA, and vanB, while biofilm formation adds further complexity by promoting antibiotic tolerance and persistence distinct from genetic resistance mechanisms. Effective management was identified as requiring appropriate antimicrobial agents, active screening, infection prevention and control measures, and stewardship programmes, though implementation is frequently hampered by institutional barriers, resource limitations, and inadequate staff training. The authors conclude that a coordinated, multidisciplinary approach integrating rapid diagnostics, stringent infection control, and sustained institutional investment is essential to reduce the clinical and economic burden of these pathogens.
items.citation: Peptine Lucian-Daniel, Zaharia Andreea-Eliza, Maftei Nicoleta-Maricica et al.. Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci (VRE) in Nosocomial Infections: A Systematic Review of Resistance, Pathogenesis, and Clinical Management. Microorganisms. 2026

items.citation: Rory P. Mulloy, Danyel Evseev, Noga Sharlin et al.. Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses. PLoS Biology. 2026

items.title: Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of secondary mucormycosis arising after respiratory viral infections, particularly those caused by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses. A multidisciplinary group of international experts was convened to develop a formal consensus document aimed at preventing this serious fungal complication. The resulting consensus identifies high-risk patient populations and provides a set of preventive recommendations organized around four domains: education and training, personal protection, early diagnosis and treatment, and infection control. The document also acknowledges areas where evidence remains limited or contested, and it outlines priorities for future research to strengthen the evidence base. Overall, the consensus seeks to offer systematic, clinically actionable guidance to improve awareness and optimize prevention strategies for mucormycosis in the context of respiratory viral infections.
items.citation: Junyan Qu, Xinyao Liu, Min Quan et al.. Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections. iFungi. 2026

items.title: A Dual-Hue Recognizable Lateral Flow Immunoassay Corresponding to Distinct Sensitivity Ranges for Timely and Quantitative Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This paper developed a lateral flow immunoassay platform designed to improve the early detection of prostate cancer by simultaneously measuring two biomarkers with high accuracy and simple operation. The system employs dual-ratiometric fluorescence transitions that produce two distinct color-change pathways governed by the inner filter effect, each calibrated to different sensitivity ranges for detecting total and free prostate-specific antigen. This design allows clinicians to visually identify samples falling within the diagnostically ambiguous gray zone using the naked eye, while a smartphone performs tonal analysis to calculate the free-to-total antigen ratio for precise cancer risk stratification. When validated against clinical serum samples, the platform achieved diagnostic accuracy comparable to established chemiluminescent assays while being substantially faster and easier to use. The authors propose this dual-hue ratiometric framework as a generalizable approach for multiplexed point-of-care diagnostics applicable beyond prostate cancer.
items.citation: Rong Hu, Xi Zhang, Liang Huang et al.. A Dual-Hue Recognizable Lateral Flow Immunoassay Corresponding to Distinct Sensitivity Ranges for Timely and Quantitative Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer. ACS Nano. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable serological assay for detecting Usutu virus (USUV) and West Nile virus (WNV) antibodies in wild birds, addressing a gap in on-site surveillance tools amid rising arbovirus incidence in the Netherlands. The researchers applied a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay (LMIA) capable of simultaneously detecting antibodies against both viruses' non-structural proteins to blood samples from wild birds captured at ringing sites, comparing results against a gold-standard neutralization test. The LMIA demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for USUV detection relative to the reference method, and successfully identified seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird that was confirmed by the gold-standard test. Performance of the assay was also evaluated against the WHO REASSURED framework for point-of-care diagnostics, where it achieved a high proportion of the maximum possible score. The authors conclude that the LMIA is a feasible, rapid, and equipment-light tool for on-site arbovirus serological screening in wild bird populations, with potential applicability in both structured surveillance programs and resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation on gold nanoparticles affects the performance of lateral flow immunoassays used in point-of-care diagnostics. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature synthesis method capable of producing phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles at large scale in a short time, overcoming the limitations of conventional citrate-capped nanoparticles that require high-temperature reflux and yield randomly oriented antibodies. The phenylboronic acid surface chemistry enables oriented antibody immobilization by selectively binding to carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments, ensuring that antigen-binding sites remain accessible. When tested for fecal occult blood detection, these functionalized nanoparticles demonstrated dramatically improved sensitivity compared to conventional citrate-capped gold nanoparticle probes. The authors conclude that this scalable nanoplatform offers strong potential for clinical translation in high-sensitivity lateral flow diagnostics.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.
items.summary: This paper addressed the limited sensitivity of conventional lateral flow immunoassays, which stems from weak optical signals, randomly oriented antibodies, and inconsistent nanoprobe fabrication. The researchers developed a dual-enhancement approach combining gold-decorated ferritin nanocages with SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry, where engineered ferritin displaying SpyTag peptides served as a template for controlled gold nanocluster growth while retaining functional sites for subsequent antibody attachment. The gold deposition produced highly uniform core-shell nanostructures with amplified optical signals, and conjugation of SpyCatcher-fused antibodies via spontaneous isopeptide bond formation ensured site-specific, covalently oriented antibody immobilization. Using human chorionic gonadotropin as a model target, the optimized assay achieved a dramatically lower detection limit compared to commercial gold nanoparticle-based strips, with oriented conjugation alone improving antigen-binding capacity approximately eightfold over random adsorption. The platform demonstrated reliable performance in urine samples with acceptable spike-recovery rates, suggesting broad applicability for improving sensitivity in point-of-care diagnostic settings.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Yuan X, Zhu X, Xu Y et al.. Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Ag-rich Ag-Au nanoshells based lateral flow immunoassay for rapid and sensitive detection of bovine viral diarrhea virus.
items.citation: Ding Y, Zhang W, Huang Y et al.. Ag-rich Ag-Au nanoshells based lateral flow immunoassay for rapid and sensitive detection of bovine viral diarrhea virus.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Mannan immunoassay for diagnosis of invasive mucormycosis: assay development, preclinical testing and evaluation in an animal model.
items.summary: This study investigated whether Mucorales mannan, a fungal cell wall component, could serve as a non-invasive biomarker for diagnosing invasive mucormycosis in blood and respiratory fluid samples. The researchers developed a lateral flow immunoassay using a monoclonal antibody specific to Mucorales mannan, incorporating europium nanoparticles as the detection reagent, and tested it for analytical performance, in a pulmonary mouse model, and in a small cohort of patients with probable or proven mucormycosis. The assay detected mannan from four of five major disease-causing Mucorales species without cross-reacting with mannans from other clinically important fungi such as Aspergillus, Candida, and Fusarium. In the animal model, mannan was detectable in both serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and rose progressively with infection, while in the patient cohort, positive results were more frequent among those not receiving amphotericin B therapy, and one patient showed elevated mannan levels a week before meeting formal diagnostic criteria. The authors conclude that mannan represents a promising diagnostic biomarker for mucormycosis and that mannan-targeted assays warrant further clinical investigation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Burnham-Marusich AR, Pandit V, Alkhazraji S et al.. Mannan immunoassay for diagnosis of invasive mucormycosis: assay development, preclinical testing and evaluation in an animal model.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of low sensitivity in lateral-flow immunoassays, which are widely used for rapid point-of-care diagnostics. The researchers explored using a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system based on poly(ethylene glycol) and dextran to preconcentrate small hydrophilic protein targets before applying the sample to a lateral-flow immunoassay, a strategy previously blocked by the high viscosity of the dextran-rich phase that impedes fluid flow on paper. To overcome this barrier, they incorporated the enzyme dextranase to degrade dextran and reduce viscosity, optimizing enzymatic and fluid-flow conditions through systematic studies. The integrated system improved the limit of detection for a model protein target in artificial saliva by tenfold compared to a conventional lateral-flow immunoassay, and this improvement was maintained when dextranase was dehydrated directly onto the paper strip to simplify liquid handling. This work represents the first successful coupling of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system with a lateral-flow immunoassay, expanding the toolkit of preconcentration strategies available for point-of-care diagnostics.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Nicklen FD, Hadeed CH, Zhang F et al.. First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.. items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines advanced biosensing technologies designed to rapidly and accurately detect major foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, with particular attention to how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically assesses practical challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Analysis of the antimicrobial activity of zinc oxide nanoparticles against drug-resistant bacteria and their applications in the disinfection process
items.summary: This study investigated the antimicrobial potential of zinc oxide nanoparticles synthesized using an eco-friendly, plant-based method employing Phoenix dactylifera root extract as a reducing agent. The nanoparticles were characterized and tested against a broad range of bacterial and fungal isolates, including multidrug-resistant strains, using multiple assays, and their disinfection efficacy was evaluated on water samples, surfaces, and acid-fast bacilli isolates. The nanoparticles demonstrated potent activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with Gram-positive organisms showing greater susceptibility, and MRSA producing the largest inhibition zone. Disinfection testing showed that the nanoparticles could achieve complete bacterial elimination on laboratory surfaces within a short contact period, and bactericidal effects were also observed against acid-fast bacilli. The authors conclude that these green-synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles represent a promising broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent suitable for clinical and environmental disinfection applications, with future investigation into synergistic use alongside conventional antimicrobials recommended.
items.citation: Dalia Alqaffaf, Ali M. Atoom, Rana Abu Huwaij et al.. Analysis of the antimicrobial activity of zinc oxide nanoparticles against drug-resistant bacteria and their applications in the disinfection process. PLoS ONE. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual nature of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they act as essential signaling molecules at physiological concentrations but drive disease pathology when produced excessively or in a dysregulated manner. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the major types, sources, and physiological functions of reactive oxygen species alongside the molecular pathways through which oxidative stress damages cells and disrupts signaling. The review also critically evaluates contemporary and emerging methods for detecting and quantifying oxidative stress, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging techniques. The contribution of redox imbalance to major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders is examined in an integrated framework. The authors conclude by outlining future directions in precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine
items.summary: Spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) are nanoconstructs comprising a nanoparticle core densely coated with radially oriented oligonucleotide strands, first created as gold nanoparticle–DNA conjugates in the mid-1990s. This review traces three decades of their development, covering advances in synthesis that have produced dozens of SNA classes, the discovery of emergent properties arising from their dense nucleic acid shell architecture, and their translation into biomedical and materials applications. The dense shell architecture confers enhanced binding affinity to complementary DNA, resistance to enzymatic degradation, reduced immune activation, and efficient cellular uptake without transfection agents, establishing SNAs as a chemically distinct materials class. These properties have been exploited across intracellular and extracellular probing, gene regulation, vaccine development, and CRISPR-based gene editing platforms. In parallel, sequence-specific DNA interactions between SNAs have been used to assemble programmable colloidal crystals with diverse lattice symmetries and compositions, yielding metamaterials with unusual optical and mechanical properties such as negative refractive indices and shape memory, illustrating how synthetic mastery and fundamental discovery together drive broad interdisciplinary innovation.
items.citation: Connor M. Forsyth, Rachel R. Chan, Tanner D. Fink et al.. Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine. Accounts of Chemical Research. 2026
