items.title: Efficient three-dimensional variational data assimilation of multi-plane PIV data
items.summary: This paper investigated three-dimensional variational data assimilation of sparse stereoscopic particle image velocimetry measurements taken across multiple cross-stream planes in the turbulent wake of a vehicle-like bluff body at high Reynolds number. The authors employed a discrete adjoint approach to optimize time-averaged momentum equations and introduced a novel technique called adjoint localization, which restricts the control variable space to a user-defined subdomain to reduce the memory demands of the method. Confining the control variable to a small fraction of the full control space achieved a large reduction in peak memory usage while preserving the fidelity of the assimilated velocity and momentum forcing fields. The assimilated results improved upon a baseline turbulence model by recovering the correct asymmetric topology of the three-dimensional recirculation bubble, yielding physically consistent mean pressure and Reynolds shear stress fields. A data efficiency study further revealed that measurement planes must extend at least to the end of the primary recirculation bubble to adequately constrain near-wake dynamics, underscoring the practical utility of adjoint localization for industrial-scale separated flow problems.
items.citation: Uttam Cadambi Padmanaban, Samaresh Midya, Ping He et al.. Efficient three-dimensional variational data assimilation of multi-plane PIV data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: SimWAM is a world-action model for end-to-end autonomous driving that addresses the computational inefficiency of existing approaches, which require generating future video frames at inference time. The method co-trains a pretrained video generation expert and a lightweight action expert using joint flow matching, with an isolated attention mask ensuring that action prediction remains independent of future frames so the video branch can be entirely discarded after training. This design allows the video generation process to serve purely as a training signal, transferring video dynamics priors to the action expert without imposing any generation cost during deployment. Reinforcement learning is additionally applied to optimize a compositional driving reward that goes beyond simple trajectory imitation. The resulting system achieves competitive trajectory planning performance on the NAVSIM benchmark, outperforms state-of-the-art world-action model planners at substantially lower latency, and generalizes zero-shot to a separate dataset.
items.citation: Zongchuang Zhao, Xin Zhou, Tianyang Xu et al.. SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum de Sitter and Analytically Continued Chern Simons Theory
items.summary: This paper investigates the quantum wavefunction of de Sitter space using the mathematical framework of Lefschetz thimbles applied to Chern-Simons theory in Lorentzian self-dual gravity with a positive cosmological constant. The authors redefine the Chern-Simons-Kodama wavefunctional by replacing the conditionally convergent real integration contour with an absolutely convergent Lefschetz thimble attached to the self-dual de Sitter saddle point, following Witten's analytic continuation prescription, which enables a controlled semiclassical expansion. In the simplest homogeneous isotropic reduction, this construction reproduces the known Hartle-Hawking Airy wavefunction, and in the more general Bianchi IX truncation, the analysis reveals that the symmetric configuration is the unique critical point for positive cosmological constant. The resulting wavefunction on the Lefschetz thimble takes the form of the Airy factor from the isotropic sector multiplied by a real Gaussian damping in the anisotropic shear directions, yielding a finite and well-defined Bianchi IX wavefunction. The authors conclude that the characteristic Airy behavior is not merely an artifact of restricting to one-dimensional minisuperspace but is a genuine feature of the wavefunction on the appropriate integration cycle.
items.citation: Stephon Alexander, Kenneth Blakey. Quantum de Sitter and Analytically Continued Chern Simons Theory. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the experimental validation of a uranium-based fission chamber detector designed to monitor neutron output across the wide dynamic range expected during high-performance plasma operations on the SPARC tokamak. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Testing with both types of neutron generators confirmed that the detector's efficiency matched vendor specifications and that its response was highly linear, with measured count rates agreeing well with neutronics simulations. Additional characterization demonstrated the detector's resilience to operationally relevant environmental conditions, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation risks associated with long cable runs. The authors conclude that this fission chamber design, when combined with appropriate shielding and pulse height thresholds, constitutes a reliable neutron diagnostic for measuring fusion power on SPARC.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme near-infrared colors. To test whether the source might instead be a cool brown dwarf within the Milky Way, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST imaging roughly three and a half years after the discovery data and performed precise relative astrometry using point-spread-function fitting and a local reference frame of compact sources. They detected a clear proper motion over the observational baseline, ruling out any extragalactic origin at high statistical confidence. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identified it as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K, placing it at a distance that makes it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The study highlights the power of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing cold substellar objects from genuine extreme high-redshift candidates in deep extragalactic survey fields.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of helping large language model agents accumulate and refine procedural knowledge in the form of reusable textual skills for recurring tasks. The authors identify two key limitations in existing skill refinement frameworks: the absence of explicit diagnosis-outcome feedback loops and the treatment of deletion as a generic editing operation rather than a principled consolidation mechanism. To address these gaps, they introduce SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that combines a forward stage performing closed-loop diagnostic evolution with rollback capabilities and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimating each unit's contribution through a leave-one-out utility audit before applying validation-gated consolidation or removal. Evaluated across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks with multiple backbone language models, SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy, with ablation studies confirming that the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components each contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study describes the design and enrollment procedures for a prospective longitudinal mixed-methods investigation evaluating point-of-care nucleic acid tests for HIV detection and viral load monitoring across clinical and community settings in the United States. The researchers enrolled participants seeking HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, or post-exposure prophylaxis at a hospital-based clinic and an LGBTQ+ community center, administering a qualitative whole blood point-of-care nucleic acid test alongside standard laboratory testing, while people already living with HIV were enrolled in a randomized clinical trial comparing standard care with the addition of a semiquantitative point-of-care test. The study also collected acceptability surveys and conducted in-depth interviews with subsets of participants, and performed time-and-motion observations to assess the impact of point-of-care testing on clinic visit timing. The abstract reports only enrollment and procedural outcomes, as the primary analyses examining test performance, acceptability, feasibility, and clinical impact on viral suppression have not yet been completed and are anticipated in future publications. Overall, the paper establishes the protocol and feasibility of conducting such an evaluation rather than reporting substantive findings on test performance or clinical outcomes.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study examined whether pharmacologic measures of tenofovir adherence could predict future HIV viremia among people with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy in South Africa. Researchers compared three adherence metrics — a point-of-care urine tenofovir assay, quantitative urine tenofovir concentrations via liquid-chromatography-mass-spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and assessed their associations with current and subsequent viral load outcomes at approximately six months. Tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots were significantly and negatively associated with viremia at the later timepoint, suggesting this measure can help predict future treatment failure, while the urine-based measures did not show significant associations with subsequent viral load. Participants with undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir results were more likely to be viremic at enrollment and to have lower CD4 counts, patterns consistent with recent antiretroviral therapy initiation rather than established adherence. The findings support dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate as a useful tool for identifying patients at risk of future viremia who might benefit from targeted interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation
items.summary: This qualitative study examined perceptions of integrating a point-of-care triage test measuring IP-10, a chemokine correlated with HIV viral load, into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique. Researchers conducted multiple rounds of interviews with people living with HIV who underwent IP-10 testing, as well as healthcare providers and programme stakeholders, nested within a clinical evaluation at two primary healthcare facilities. Participants across all groups found the IP-10 triage test broadly acceptable, with same-day results perceived to reduce patient anxiety, support treatment adherence, and facilitate timely clinical decisions. The test was seen as potentially improving monitoring efficiency by prioritising those who require confirmatory viral load testing while reducing unnecessary testing among virally suppressed clients, though concerns about test accuracy and the necessity of maintaining confirmatory testing were noted. The authors conclude that successful implementation would depend on adequate training, workflow integration, quality assurance, and clear patient communication to maximise the test's contribution to differentiated HIV care approaches.
items.citation: Myburgh H, Saura-Lázaro A, van den Bogaart E et al.. Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation. 2026

items.title: Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.
items.summary: This qualitative study examined the barriers and facilitators encountered by healthcare workers when implementing near point-of-care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people living with HIV in Tanzania. Researchers conducted clinic observations and in-depth interviews with healthcare workers at multiple time points across Tanzanian sites participating in a larger cluster-randomised controlled trial, using a thematic framework analysis guided by the Measurement Instrument for Determinants of Innovations. The findings showed that near point-of-care testing improved result turnaround times and enabled same-day counselling, which motivated both staff and patients, and was further supported by compatibility with existing workflows, teamwork, and management commitment. However, significant implementation bottlenecks included lengthy patient waiting times, shortages of physical resources such as rooms and electricity, staff shortages, and delays caused by sample transport to nearby laboratories. The authors conclude that investment in staff training, infrastructure, sample handling procedures, and guideline alignment is necessary to fully realise the benefits of this approach for the target population.
items.citation: Msoka P, Mtenga A, Maro R et al.. Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines the contested question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The authors structured opposing arguments around several issues, including whether high-performance athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity apart from confounding factors such as sleep disruption, anxiety, travel, nutritional deficits, and environmental stress, and whether commonly used biomarkers and study designs are adequate to draw firm conclusions. Moderate-intensity exercise of relatively short duration is broadly accepted as beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, whereas arduous exercise typical of elite athletes and military personnel has long been thought to suppress immunity. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in nature, but the central question of whether exercise per se causally increases infection risk remains unresolved. The authors call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the independent contribution of exercise from the many other factors that converge on immune pathways in high-performance populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and its dysregulation across a range of diseases, with particular emphasis on how lipid metabolic processes govern immune cell function. The authors synthesize the historical development of lipid metabolism research and detail the functions, transport mechanisms, and signaling pathways central to lipid biology. A major focus is placed on how lipid metabolites regulate the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, spanning both innate and adaptive immunity. The review further explores multilevel regulatory mechanisms—genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational—that link lipid metabolism to immune cell behavior in conditions such as autoimmune diseases, cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic disorders. The authors conclude by surveying therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical efforts, and emerging opportunities involving lipid-derived biomarkers and novel interventions.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines exosomes — nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by shuttling bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids — with a focus on the molecular mechanisms governing their biogenesis, cargo loading, and functional heterogeneity. The authors synthesize current understanding of the regulatory machinery involved, including ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications, while surveying advanced omics platforms and machine learning tools used to decode exosomal content. The clinical utility of exosomes is assessed across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, particularly in the context of liquid biopsies and their diagnostic performance. The review also covers the therapeutic landscape, including native and engineered exosomes for drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, alongside insights from ongoing clinical trials. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as protocol standardization and targeting specificity, and propose that emerging approaches including synthetic exosome mimetics and artificial intelligence-driven diagnostics will advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label randomized platform trials investigated whether the antiviral treatment nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces severe outcomes in higher-risk outpatients with COVID-19 who were predominantly vaccinated or had prior natural immunity, a population in whom the drug's effectiveness had not been well established. Conducted in the United Kingdom and Canada, the trials enrolled adults who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had been symptomatic for five days or fewer, randomly assigning them to receive nirmatrelvir–ritonavir plus usual care or usual care alone, with hospitalization or death within 28 days as the primary outcome. Despite the drug reducing viral load by the end of the treatment course, rates of hospitalization or death were very low in both groups across both trials, and neither trial demonstrated a statistically meaningful reduction in the primary outcome with active treatment. The authors conclude that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir did not reduce hospitalization or death among vaccinated higher-risk individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection, in contrast to earlier findings in unvaccinated high-risk populations.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of how large language model agents accumulate and refine procedural knowledge in the form of reusable textual skills that can be loaded into context without modifying model weights. The authors identify two key limitations in existing skill refinement frameworks: the absence of explicit closed-loop feedback linking diagnoses to outcomes, and the lack of a principled mechanism for consolidating accumulated knowledge beyond generic editing operations. To address these gaps, they introduce SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that combines a forward stage performing diagnosis-driven edits with regression rollback and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimates their utility via a leave-one-out audit, and applies structured consolidation or removal. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks with multiple backbone language models show that SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy, with ablation studies confirming that both the closed-loop diagnosis and the proximal refinement components contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Permutation invariant neural network prediction of vacancy formation under deformation and varying chemical environment in FCC high entropy alloys
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of predicting vacancy formation energies in face-centered cubic high-entropy alloys, where both local chemical disorder and mechanical deformation create enormous variability that makes direct atomistic calculations impractical at scale. The authors developed a permutation-invariant machine learning framework that represents local atomic environments using geometric descriptors combined with invariants of the local deformation gradient, allowing the model to simultaneously capture chemical and mechanical effects on vacancy energetics. Atomistic simulations used to train and validate the framework revealed that volumetric deformation dominates changes in average vacancy formation energy, while shear deformation plays a comparatively minor role, though significant site-to-site variability under identical loading conditions confirms that local chemical environments control the statistical spread of vacancy energetics. The trained model predicts vacancy formation energies across diverse deformation states with accuracy comparable to direct atomistic calculations but at orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost. The authors argue this approach provides an efficient pathway for incorporating stress-dependent defect energetics into multiscale models of diffusion, irradiation damage, and dynamic failure in chemically complex alloys.
items.citation: Tanvir Sohail, Swarnava Ghosh. Permutation invariant neural network prediction of vacancy formation under deformation and varying chemical environment in FCC high entropy alloys. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Do We Still Need Demand Flexibility as Batteries Become Cheaper? A Levelized Cost Perspective
items.summary: The paper investigates whether demand flexibility from industrial and data-center loads remains economically valuable as battery storage costs decline, given that both resources serve to balance power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy. The authors develop a levelized cost framework to compare energy storage technologies against load shifting in settings such as aluminum smelters and data centers, accounting for incremental costs that arise when large loads operating near full capacity must shift electricity use, including extra equipment, delayed sales, working capital, and process disruption. A key insight is that battery storage costs per shifted kilowatt-hour rise as the flexibility period lengthens and cycling frequency falls, whereas load shifting does not face the same scaling of capacity cost under a fixed avoided-hour share. The analysis finds that batteries are competitive for short-cycle shifting applications but become dramatically more expensive than load shifting for seasonal flexibility timescales. The paper concludes that the relative value of demand flexibility versus storage depends critically on the timescale of the balancing need, the specific load type, and whether the productive capacity required for flexibility is newly built or already in place.
items.citation: Ruike Lyu, Tengmu Li. Do We Still Need Demand Flexibility as Batteries Become Cheaper? A Levelized Cost Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Onset of the transitional flux-avalanche regime in bulk NbTi controlled by the thermal boundary conductance
items.summary: This paper investigated thermomagnetic avalanches in bulk NbTi superconductors, which can occur in two distinct regimes distinguished by whether the threshold magnetic field increases or decreases with temperature. The researchers manipulated the thermal boundary conductance between a bulk NbTi disk and its environment by introducing silver-filled interface layers of varying compositions, moving the system from the purely thermally limited regime toward the transitional region separating electromagnetically controlled and thermally limited behavior. With a standard nonadecane interface, the threshold field decreased monotonically with temperature, but silver-filled interfaces produced a non-monotonic dependence featuring a positive-slope interval and a maximum in threshold field, a behavior predicted theoretically but not previously observed in a bulk superconductor. The temperature at which this maximum occurs is determined by the intrinsic properties of NbTi rather than the silver loading, and the onset of the positive-slope regime coincides with a change in avalanche morphology from narrow channeled fingers to broad fronts. These findings confirm that the sign reversal of the temperature derivative of the threshold field serves as a direct experimental signature of the transitional regime, where heat removal during the magnetic instability becomes dynamically significant.
items.citation: Irina Abaloszewa, Victor V. Chabanenko, Aleksander Abaloszew. Onset of the transitional flux-avalanche regime in bulk NbTi controlled by the thermal boundary conductance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Synthesizing Voltage Ride-Through Controllers for Data Centers
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of designing controllers that allow data centers to remain connected to the power grid during voltage disturbances, as required by emerging voltage ride-through grid codes, rather than disconnecting in ways that could collectively destabilize the grid. The authors developed SolVRT, a system that uses formal methods to synthesize grid-code-compliant voltage ride-through controllers for data centers by expressing grid code requirements in Signal Temporal Logic and translating them, along with a model of the data center's power topology, into a controller synthesis problem. This approach guarantees correct-by-construction controllers when solutions exist, and when compliance is impossible, SolVRT diagnoses the root cause by identifying conflicting constraints and computing the minimal hardware or workload modifications needed to achieve compliance. The system was evaluated through closed-loop simulations of a large data center connected to a multi-bus transmission system, demonstrating its ability to synthesize compliant controllers, certify infeasibility, and pinpoint targeted remediation strategies.
items.citation: Wayne Wang, Archit Bhatnagar, Tongyuan Miao et al.. Synthesizing Voltage Ride-Through Controllers for Data Centers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A foundation-model approach to pediatric headache classification from rs-fMRI
items.summary: This paper investigated whether resting-state functional MRI combined with machine learning could support the classification of headache disorders in children, a population for whom headache represents the most common neurological complaint. The researchers applied NeuroSTORM, a foundation model pretrained on neuroimaging data, to encode rs-fMRI scans and fine-tuned it to distinguish children with headache from healthy controls and to differentiate headache subtypes, comparing this approach against traditional functional-connectivity matrix features. Using a modest dataset of scans collected across two visits, the foundation model substantially outperformed the functional-connectivity approach in binary headache detection, demonstrating strong discriminative ability without relying on predefined connectivity features. In multiclass classification across healthy controls, chronic migraine, and other headache subtypes, the model achieved moderate performance and showed particular ability to identify chronic migraine while struggling to separate other headache subtypes from one another. The authors conclude that foundation model representations of rs-fMRI data offer a promising proof-of-concept for neuroimaging-based pediatric headache classification, even under data-limited conditions, with potential implications for subtype identification and personalized treatment.
items.citation: Guilherme S. Imai Aldeia, Clara Moon, Julie Shulman et al.. A foundation-model approach to pediatric headache classification from rs-fMRI. arXiv. 2026

items.title: New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.
items.summary: This paper investigated how to distinguish people newly entering HIV care from those transferring from previous care within United States clinical cohort studies, a distinction that has important implications for research accuracy. The researchers examined the availability of five types of historical HIV data — prior antiretroviral therapy prescriptions, historical CD4 counts, historical viral loads, suppressed viral load at enrollment, and prior AIDS-defining conditions — across cohorts participating in a large North American collaboration spanning two decades. Using these data types, participants were classified into categories reflecting their prior care experience, including those new to care, those transferring without a care gap, and those re-engaging after a gap. The study found that the proportion of participants transferring into cohorts grew substantially over the study period while those truly new to care declined, and that historical antiretroviral prescriptions and suppressed viral load at enrollment became increasingly useful identifiers of prior care experience, particularly after treatment guidelines expanded. The authors recommend that HIV cohorts systematically collect all five data types and apply a standardized classification algorithm to improve the identification of participants who are genuinely new to HIV care.
items.citation: Haw NJL, Hogan B, Humes E et al.. New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.. American journal of epidemiology. 2026

items.title: The Impact of the Common Elements Treatment Approach on HIV Treatment Outcomes Among Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence in South Africa: A Randomized Trial.
items.summary: This randomized controlled trial examined whether the Common Elements Treatment Approach (CETA), a cognitive-behavioural-therapy-based intervention delivered by lay healthcare workers, could improve HIV treatment outcomes among women experiencing intimate partner violence in South Africa. Women living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy who had recent intimate partner violence exposure and either unsuppressed viral loads or poor medication adherence were randomly assigned to receive either eight to twelve CETA counselling sessions or weekly safety text messages, with viral suppression and retention in care at twelve months as the primary outcome. The trial found no meaningful overall difference in viral suppression or retention between the CETA and control groups. However, among women who completed the full CETA intervention, there was a modest improvement in viral suppression compared to controls, suggesting that intervention completion may be an important factor. The authors conclude that future research should investigate strategies to improve CETA completion rates to determine whether the intervention can meaningfully benefit HIV outcomes in this population.
items.venue: Journal of the International AIDS Society
items.citation: Fox MP, Kane JC, Mngadi-Ncube S et al.. The Impact of the Common Elements Treatment Approach on HIV Treatment Outcomes Among Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence in South Africa: A Randomized Trial.. Journal of the International AIDS Society. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of Southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are compromised by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and tested blood samples using the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT, conventional RDT, expert microscopy, and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and near-perfect agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity dropped considerably when qPCR was used as the reference standard, revealing that submicroscopic, low-density infections were frequently missed. Malaria prevalence was highest by qPCR, which also detected more mixed infections than either microscopy or the RDT, underscoring the limitations of antigen-based tests at low parasitemia. The findings support the multi-antigen RDT as a clinically useful tool for routine diagnosis but highlight the need for more sensitive methods in malaria surveillance and control programmes in endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti during a period when security concerns had disrupted conventional surveillance efforts. Researchers extracted nucleic acids from discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients at health centers across two Haitian departments, then screened the material using a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus, followed by next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Dengue virus serotype three was identified as the sole arbovirus detected, with all positive samples coming from collections made in a single year, and phylogenetic analysis placed these sequences within a cluster circulating across the Caribbean during the same period. No evidence of alphavirus or Oropouche virus infection was found in the subset tested. The findings validate discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests as a practical surveillance tool in resource-limited or politically unstable settings, capable of detecting and genetically characterizing arboviruses without dedicated specimen collection infrastructure.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper presents an integrated wireless health monitoring framework combining IoT sensors, ZigBee communication, and cloud-based artificial intelligence to enable real-time remote health surveillance, particularly for elderly and chronically ill patients. The system uses IoT sensors to continuously track heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels, transmitting data via the low-power ZigBee protocol to a centralized processing unit where machine learning algorithms—including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression—analyze the data for health anomalies. Testing in a real-world care facility evaluated the system's performance in terms of detection accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency. The random forest model demonstrated particularly strong detection performance, and the overall system achieved very low transmission latency and minimal power consumption, making it suitable for long-term deployment. The authors claim their modular, scalable architecture addresses key shortcomings of existing telehealth systems, such as high delays and excessive false alarms, while reducing the monitoring burden on healthcare providers.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis
items.summary: This paper investigated why chronic joint inflammation persists in rheumatoid arthritis despite the presence of macrophages that are normally associated with tissue repair. The researchers found that patient-derived pro-repair macrophages in the inflamed joint produce the complement protein C1q and simultaneously express its receptor, creating an autocrine signaling loop. When these macrophages were stimulated with C1q, the mitochondrial enzyme SARM1 was activated, catalyzing the breakdown of NAD into cyclic ADP ribose, which drove metabolic exhaustion and a form of inflammatory cell death called PANoptosis. In vivo experiments confirmed that C1q worsened synovial inflammation, while inhibiting SARM1 provided therapeutic benefit. The study concludes that SARM1-mediated metabolic collapse of macrophages is a key driver of pathogenic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and represents a potential therapeutic target.
items.citation: Tao Huang, Yoshinori Takashima, Jitendra Kumar et al.. Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis. Immunity. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This study evaluated the safety of a large language model embedded within an electronic medical record system to support clinical decision-making at primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed patient encounter records to assess hallucination rates, guideline alignment, and the safety of model-generated recommendations. The system rarely hallucinated and its guidance aligned with local clinical guidelines in nearly all cases, demonstrating strong baseline performance. However, clinicians disproportionately adopted harmful model recommendations while failing to incorporate beneficial ones, and a meaningful proportion of encounters contained actively harmful outputs that appeared in final documentation. The findings suggest the tool holds promise for quality improvement in African primary healthcare settings but that usability optimization, locally tailored safeguards, and prospective trials are needed before patient-level benefit can be confirmed.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: Public health and urban resilience implications of sustainable sanitary waste management
items.summary: This paper examines the public health and environmental challenges posed by sanitary waste from absorbent hygiene products in rapidly urbanizing cities, with a focus on Chennai, India. The authors conducted a review that maps regulatory gaps and infrastructure deficiencies across local, national, and international contexts, identifying how monsoon flooding exacerbates the leakage of spent diapers and similar products into waterways and drainage systems. The review highlights shortcomings in regulatory enforcement, public participation, and infrastructure, while drawing on global examples to identify best practices. The authors propose an integrated management framework emphasizing source segregation, dedicated sealed collection, audited routing to authorized treatment facilities, and governance tied to measurable performance indicators funded through Extended Producer Responsibility mechanisms. The proposed scenario targets substantial reductions in drain leakage and disease risk by 2030, positioning coordinated action among communities, industries, and governments as a pathway to more resilient urban sanitation systems.
items.citation: Pachaiyappan Murugan, Meivelu Moovendhan. Public health and urban resilience implications of sustainable sanitary waste management. Discover Public Health. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the development and experimental validation of a uranium-based fission chamber designed to monitor neutron emission across an exceptionally wide dynamic range during deuterium-tritium plasma operations on the SPARC tokamak. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Experimental tests using both types of neutron generators confirmed that the detector's efficiency matched vendor specifications and that its response was highly linear, with results in good agreement with neutronics simulations. Additional testing demonstrated that the detector remains robust under conditions relevant to the SPARC environment, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation risks associated with long cable runs. The authors conclude that this fission chamber, combined with appropriate shielding and signal threshold settings, provides a reliable diagnostic solution for fusion power measurements on SPARC.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme near-infrared colors. To test whether it might instead be a cold brown dwarf within the Milky Way, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST imaging taken roughly three and a half years after the discovery data and performed precise relative astrometry using point-spread-function fitting and a carefully constructed local reference frame. They detected a clear proper motion over the observational baseline, ruling out any extragalactic origin at very high statistical confidence. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identifies it as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K, placing it at a distance of several hundred parsecs and making it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The study highlights the power of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing cold substellar objects from genuine high-redshift galaxy candidates.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics
items.summary: This paper investigates how next-generation cosmic microwave background experiments can constrain the effective number of relativistic species in the early universe, a parameter that encodes information about neutrinos and other light relics. The authors used Fisher-matrix forecasting methods, implemented in a publicly released end-to-end analysis pipeline called DRAFT, to evaluate the projected sensitivity of multiple CMB-S4 survey configurations across their design phase. The pipeline spans simulated foreground maps and component separation through to delensing and final parameter sensitivity estimates. The conceptual CMB-S4 design is forecast to achieve sub-percent precision on the effective number of relativistic species within its primary observing period, with a revised configuration reaching comparable precision over a longer timescale, and a cosmic-variance-limited survey establishes the ultimate accessible improvement. The paper also discusses the broad implications of such precise measurements for big bang nucleosynthesis, light thermal relics, and early-universe physics beyond the Standard Model.
items.citation: Cynthia Trendafilova, Srinivasan Raghunathan, Benjamin Wallisch et al.. Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation
items.summary: The paper investigates the active Cahn-Hilliard equation, a model for phase separation in active matter systems, focusing on both its mathematical well-posedness and its coarsening dynamics. Using a novel approach based on heteroclinic trajectories in the phase plane, the authors characterize static kink profiles and spherical droplet states, and develop a theory of surface tension modifications driven by activity and local interface curvature. This theory explains a previously conjectured shift in the coarsening power law for characteristic domain length, transitioning from an exponent corresponding to classical Cahn-Hilliard dynamics to a slower one induced by activity, before the system reaches a finite saturation length. The authors also construct a finite element numerical scheme, proving its well-posedness and stability for both regular polynomial and singular logarithmic potentials, and establish local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in two and three dimensions, as well as global-in-time well-posedness in one dimension under a smallness condition on the activity parameter. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions, reproducing the expected phase separation dynamics and the power-law shift in coarsening behavior at late times.
items.citation: Abramo Agosti, Andrea Giorgini. Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language model agents can improve their performance on recurring tasks by refining reusable procedural knowledge, called skills, stored as textual artifacts in the agent's context. The authors identify two key limitations in existing skill-refinement approaches: the absence of explicit closed-loop feedback linking diagnoses to measured outcomes, and the treatment of skill deletion as a generic edit rather than a principled consolidation mechanism. To address these gaps, they introduce SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that combines a forward stage performing diagnosis-driven edits with rollback mechanisms and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimates each unit's contribution via a leave-one-out utility audit, and applies gated consolidation or removal. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks with multiple backbone language models show that SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline, with ablations confirming that the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components each contribute independently to the improvement.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules
items.summary: This paper reports the experimental observation of weakly-bound ultralong-range Rydberg molecules with Π-symmetry electronic states, formed from a rubidium atom in a Rydberg P-state paired with a ground-state rubidium atom. The molecules were detected through spectroscopy across a range of principal quantum numbers, and their Π-state character was confirmed by the observed multiplet structure arising from spin-spin coupling between the Rydberg and valence electrons, which splits the magnetic sublevels of the ground-state atom analogously to the Zeeman effect. The molecular binding energy was found to decrease rapidly with a dependence on the effective principal quantum number to the negative eleventh power, suggesting that lower principal quantum numbers are most favorable for studying such Π-symmetry states. Experimental results were compared against Green's function-based theoretical calculations and showed good agreement across most of the studied range, though deviations at the lowest principal quantum number examined indicate that the Fermi pseudopotential approximation begins to break down in that regime.
items.citation: Matthew T. Eiles, Aleksandr Zaitsev, Dominik Dorer et al.. Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period and how these advances have shaped updated WHO policy guidance. The review covers developments across screening, diagnosis, and drug-resistance testing, encompassing new molecular platforms, novel specimen types, and emerging biomarkers. Key findings include the establishment of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a core screening tool, the expanded role of decentralised nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types, and the recognition of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Innovations such as tongue swabs and sputum pooling have improved diagnostic access in children and other populations unable to produce sputum, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer benefit specifically in people with HIV and advanced disease. Despite these advances, no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis, and significant performance, implementation, and equity gaps remain.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from 1990 to the present, focusing on the particular challenges posed by co-infection. People with HIV present diagnostic difficulties because they tend to have lower bacillary loads in sputum, higher rates of extrapulmonary or disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, all of which demand rapid diagnosis given the speed of disease progression in advanced HIV. The review traces the limitations of smear microscopy as the sole rapid test prior to the introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assays, noting that poor diagnostic algorithms historically caused both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis with serious consequences for patient outcomes. The advent of antiretroviral therapy and these novel diagnostics has substantially reduced tuberculosis incidence and mortality, yet screening algorithms perform less well in people already on antiretroviral therapy and no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity. The authors conclude that only one affordable point-of-care option exists, and that further development of accurate, low-cost point-of-care diagnostics remains an urgent priority.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, a disease caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* that continues to pose a major global public health burden. The authors focus on serological methods, which have gained increasing attention due to their simplicity, rapid turnaround, and cost-effectiveness compared to conventional sputum culture and molecular assays. The review is particularly motivated by the diagnostic challenges posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis and cases that yield negative results with standard testing approaches. The authors survey current biomarkers employed in tuberculosis serodiagnosis, discuss how advanced diagnostic technologies can be integrated with these biomarkers, and assess the potential of such approaches to enhance diagnostic accuracy across varied clinical settings.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests, Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance among presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis patients in India, while also evaluating their operational feasibility and costs. In a prospective design, paired sputum specimens from over six hundred patients were tested on both platforms, with mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing serving as reference standards. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for tuberculosis detection compared to Truenat MTB Plus, and also produced substantially fewer invalid and indeterminate results, particularly for rifampicin resistance testing. However, Truenat MTB Plus was considerably less expensive per test and carries operational advantages suited to decentralized settings, though its higher rates of invalid and indeterminate results increase the burden of repeat testing. The authors conclude that a tiered diagnostic approach utilizing both platforms according to setting and resource availability could help expand molecular testing access and advance tuberculosis elimination goals.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.
items.summary: This study investigated the real-world feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing — a method that combines samples from multiple individuals into a single molecular assay — as a cost-saving approach to improve tuberculosis diagnosis in high-burden, resource-constrained settings. Using a multicountry qualitative design, the researchers conducted key informant interviews and focus group discussions with a diverse range of stakeholders, including national tuberculosis programme representatives, laboratory technicians, people with tuberculosis, and international experts across seven high-burden countries. Analysis using established feasibility and acceptability frameworks revealed that pooled testing was broadly considered feasible and acceptable in both facility and community settings, with greater confidence expressed in countries that had prior implementation experience. Feasibility was contingent on compatibility with existing diagnostic algorithms and laboratory workflows, appropriate biosafety measures, staff training, and clear standard operating procedures, while acceptability required early engagement of healthcare providers and transparent communication with patients. The authors conclude that pooled testing represents a pragmatic strategy to expand molecular tuberculosis testing, though readiness varied considerably across countries, with some requiring infrastructure strengthening before scale-up could be pursued.
items.citation: Iem V, Vo LNQ, Codlin AJ et al.. Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.. BMJ open. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swab samples could serve as accurate, nonsputum-based diagnostics for pulmonary tuberculosis. Researchers conducted a nested case-control study within a prospective cohort of adults and children undergoing tuberculosis evaluation at primary care centers in Colombia, testing paired saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra against a reference standard of sputum liquid mycobacterial culture. Both sample types demonstrated strong diagnostic performance, with saliva achieving notably higher sensitivity than oral swabs, and saliva sensitivity surpassing the World Health Organization's target threshold for a low-complexity nonsputum tuberculosis diagnostic test. Specificity was high for both collection methods and did not differ significantly between them, while the vast majority of participants found both collection procedures acceptable. These findings support saliva and oral swabs as promising nonsputum alternatives that could help close gaps in tuberculosis detection, particularly in settings where sputum collection is difficult.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and its dysregulation across a range of diseases. The authors synthesize the research history of lipid metabolism and focus particularly on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways regulate immune cell behavior, including the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review explores multilevel regulatory mechanisms—spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control—that shape immune cell function through lipid metabolites. The authors connect these mechanisms to disease contexts including autoimmune conditions, cancer, neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, aging, and metabolic disorders. The review concludes by surveying therapeutic strategies that target lipid metabolism, current clinical trial progress, and emerging directions such as lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: The paper examined the implementation and outcomes of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over its first five years of operation. The programme offered low-dose computed tomography to ever-smokers aged within a defined range who met risk thresholds determined by multivariable models, delivered through a regionally federated clinical infrastructure guided by national strategic and economic frameworks. Having invited over two million people, the programme diagnosed thousands of lung cancers, with the majority detected at an early stage, representing a marked increase in early-stage diagnoses across England and particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions. The authors conclude that large-scale, rapid implementation is achievable through centralised protocols and effective project management, and that the programme has demonstrated feasibility in reaching high-risk and underserved populations, though inequalities in participation remain a challenge. These findings are presented as supporting broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the UK and internationally, with practical tools offered for adaptation elsewhere.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review paper examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with the goal of identifying more effective therapeutic targets. The authors analyzed how disease progression is driven by interconnected organelle dysfunctions, specifically mitochondrial dysfunction with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization caused by hydroxyapatite digestion, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress from compensatory protein overproduction, alongside inflammatory cytokine activity and pathological changes in bone and cartilage. The review also maps the nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system to explain the mechanisms of osteoarthritis-associated pain. Based on these mechanistic insights, the authors outline emerging pharmacological strategies that simultaneously target inflammatory cascades, restore organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and reduce pain signaling. They further highlight advanced organelle-targeted drug delivery systems intended to improve therapeutic efficacy, collectively proposing a multimodal treatment framework to address both the structural and symptomatic dimensions of the disease.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms and durations of exercise affect Toll-like receptor expression in humans, given the established links between sedentary behaviour, chronic low-grade inflammation, and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple major databases for studies in which exercise was used as an isolated intervention and categorised the resulting literature by exercise modality and duration, including acute resistance exercise, acute aerobic exercise, resistance training programmes, aerobic training programmes, combined training programmes, and chronic exercise not otherwise classifiable. They found that acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise was more likely to produce neutral or downregulatory responses, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes were associated predominantly with unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic exercise yielded mixed results with most measurements showing no change in expression. The authors concluded that exercise modulates TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight that substantial heterogeneity across study designs limits firm conclusions and that further mechanistic research is needed.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, focusing on how light-activated nanoparticles can be engineered to treat a broad spectrum of diseases with greater precision than conventional approaches. The authors survey the core components and classification of these systems, including gold nanoparticles and hybrid constructs used in photothermal and photodynamic therapies, as well as delivery platforms such as liposomes and dendrimers that control biodistribution and drug release. At the molecular level, the review dissects how light-triggered interventions generate reactive oxygen species, induce localized heating, promote oxidative stress, and activate apoptotic, autophagic, and immune-modulatory pathways relevant not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors further evaluate regulatory-approved agents and insights from recent clinical trials, identifying key barriers to clinical translation including nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery to target tissues, and regulatory challenges. Overall, the review positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative, noninvasive therapeutic strategy with the potential to reshape treatment paradigms across a wide range of chronic and malignant diseases.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026
