The authors introduce SkillProx, a framework inspired by proximal gradient descent that operates through a forward stage—which re-executes diagnosis-driven edits, rolls back regressions, and feeds measured outcomes into subsequent diagnoses—and a backward stage that decomposes skills into auditable knowledge units, estimates their utility via a leave-one-out audit, and applies validation-gated consolidation or removal. This design addresses limitations in prior skill refinement methods, which lacked explicit diagnostic feedback loops and treated deletion as a generic editing operation rather than a principled mechanism for knowledge consolidation. Experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks across multiple backbone language models show that SkillProx outperforms the strongest gradient-based baseline in average accuracy, with ablations confirming that the closed-loop diagnosis and proximal refinement components each contribute complementary benefits.
items.citation: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.. SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules
items.summary: This paper reports the experimental observation of weakly-bound ultralong-range Rydberg molecules with Π-symmetry electronic states, formed from rubidium Rydberg atoms paired with ground-state rubidium atoms. The molecules were detected spectroscopically across a range of low principal quantum numbers, and their Π-state character was confirmed through a distinctive multiplet structure arising from spin-spin coupling between the Rydberg and valence electrons, which splits the magnetic sublevels of the ground-state atom analogously to the Zeeman effect. The molecular binding energy was found to decrease rapidly with a scaling consistent with an inverse power of the effective principal quantum number, suggesting that low principal quantum numbers are particularly favorable for studying this class of molecules. Theoretical calculations based on a Green's function approach reproduced the experimental observations well across most of the observed range, but agreement deteriorated at the lowest principal quantum number examined, pointing to a breakdown of the Fermi pseudopotential approximation in that regime.
items.citation: Matthew T. Eiles, Aleksandr Zaitsev, Dominik Dorer et al.. Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a community clinic in Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to sexual health. Using a cross-sectional design over several months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and gathered data through an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese and Syrian men, among whom a notable proportion were living with HIV, and high levels of STI awareness paradoxically coexisted with condomless sex and recreational drug use. HIV-related stigma and perceived community attitudes emerged as significant barriers to testing-seeking behavior. The findings support integrating point-of-care testing into community sexual health services, as it enabled same-day counselling and swift linkage to confirmatory testing and care for those with positive results.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the cost of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, where such infections are associated with adverse birth outcomes but cost data have been lacking. Researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare and used a combination of study records, staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and secondary sources to estimate economic costs from a health system perspective, comparing point-of-care testing against syndromic management as a modelled standard of care. Because high-volume clinic settings proved operationally infeasible, costs were modelled for a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. The composite prevalence of the targeted infections was substantial among pregnant attendees, and the dominant cost drivers were test kits and personnel, which together accounted for the majority of total expenditure. The authors conclude that reducing the price of point-of-care diagnostics is essential to making antenatal STI screening cost-feasible in this context.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote Australian First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is disproportionately high among young people. Using a decision analytic model with a government payer perspective over a ten-year horizon, researchers compared point-of-care testing against standard laboratory-based testing in terms of costs and quality-adjusted life years gained. The programme was found to be cost-effective relative to the willingness-to-pay threshold used, generating an incremental cost per quality-adjusted life year well below that threshold. The model also predicted meaningful reductions in pelvic inflammatory disease diagnoses and preterm or low birth weight births among those with infections. The findings support sustained and scaled implementation of point-of-care testing in remote primary care settings as a strategy likely to improve reproductive health outcomes for this population.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.
items.summary: This review examines the epidemiology, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnosis, and prevention of anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections, focusing primarily on chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis. The authors synthesize current understanding of why these infections are frequently asymptomatic, attributing this to bacterial adaptation to rectal tissue and dampened local immune responses that do not reach symptom thresholds, a phenomenon especially pronounced among men who have sex with men where anorectal infections often surpass urogenital ones in prevalence. Molecular diagnostics have improved detection, but challenges remain in distinguishing viable from non-viable organisms, expanding point-of-care testing, and managing antimicrobial stewardship alongside rising antimicrobial resistance, particularly in gonorrhoea. The review highlights doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis as a promising preventive strategy that substantially reduces chlamydia and syphilis incidence, alongside emerging artificial intelligence applications, though widespread clinical implementation remains constrained. The authors conclude by identifying key knowledge gaps and proposing research priorities to strengthen control of these infections globally.
items.citation: Latt PM, Kong FYS, Khosropour CM et al.. Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.. Nature reviews. Gastroenterology & hepatology. 2026

items.title: Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.
items.summary: This study examined the implementation of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in non-clinical, community outreach settings in an urban environment. Researchers conducted a program evaluation and retrospective data review of individuals who received sexually transmitted infection testing, using statistical tests to explore whether demographic characteristics or symptom presence were associated with positive test results. The testing platform delivered results within thirty minutes, and all diagnosed cases were referred for treatment within one day, demonstrating the feasibility of rapid diagnosis outside clinical settings. No statistically significant associations were found between test positivity and demographic or symptom variables, though the small sample size limited the power of these analyses. The authors conclude that point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing shows promise for community outreach contexts but that further evaluation of scalability, cost, and treatment completion is needed.
items.citation: Blanchard HL, Gonzalez E, Chow J. Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.. Sexual health. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective
items.summary: This paper examines how digitalization and technologization intersect with gender dynamics, asking whether digital transformation constitutes a paradigmatic shift in how gender identities are constructed, performed, and contested. Through a systematic literature review of recent high-impact research, the study draws on feminist theory, sociology, communication studies, health informatics, and STEM education to assess both the promises and pitfalls of digital culture for gender equality. The analysis finds that while digital technologies offer emancipatory potential through anonymity, accessibility, and expanded public participation, they simultaneously replicate and intensify patriarchal structures via cyberviolence, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, and women's underrepresentation in STEM. The review also identifies geographic and disciplinary disparities in how these issues are studied, and concludes that digital spaces function as contested terrains where power relations are renegotiated rather than neutralized. The authors argue that intersectional, gender-sensitive policies and multi-stakeholder collaborations are urgently needed to prevent the re-inscription of masculine dominance and to build genuinely equitable technological ecosystems.
items.venue: Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics
items.citation: Şevki Işıklı, Esra Fatma FAZLIOĞLU. Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective. Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
items.summary: This narrative review examined compulsive sexual behavior disorder and problematic pornography use, two widely studied but contested constructs related to dysregulated sexual behavior that carry substantial implications for mental health and well-being. Drawing on contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized current empirical and theoretical knowledge across eleven key domains, including historical context, conceptualization, assessment, epidemiology, co-occurring conditions, etiology, potential harms, and treatment approaches. The review also addressed underrepresented groups such as adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors. The authors identify persistent controversies and methodological limitations in the existing literature, including debates over classification and measurement. The review concludes by calling for greater interdisciplinary collaboration, more rigorous research methods, and better integration of findings into clinical practice and public health policy.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis examined epidemiological approaches to controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with a focus on identifying asymptomatic individuals through contact tracing and screening. The research evaluated contact tracing routines, compared characteristics of chlamydia-infected women from different clinical settings, and assessed whether contact tracing data could inform models of partner choice and disease spread. Key findings included that contact tracing effectively controlled a gonorrhoea outbreak and identified previously undiagnosed individuals among HIV-infected patients, while chlamydia screening in family planning clinics revealed meaningful prevalence with specific risk factors including young age, short relationship duration, and non-use of condoms. Comparisons between chlamydia cases detected through screening versus those presenting at sexually transmitted disease clinics showed only minor differences in partner numbers and infection rates, suggesting equivalent levels of effort in partner management are warranted across both settings. Partner choice data indicated that steady partner selection was restricted while casual partner selection was more random, failing to support a purely random mixing model for disease transmission.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks
items.summary: This paper investigated the relationship between housing instability and drug overdose risk among young people who inject drugs, arguing that existing research has insufficiently captured the complexity of housing instability by relying on single-dimension measures. The researchers developed a multi-dimensional housing instability risk index composed of five dichotomous variables and applied it to baseline data from a network-based longitudinal study of young people who inject drugs and their social networks in metropolitan Chicago. Using negative binomial regression and adjusting for multiple covariates, they found a significant positive association between higher housing instability risk scores and greater lifetime overdose counts. The findings support the value of a holistic, multi-dimensional approach to measuring housing instability as a predictor of overdose, and the authors argue this framework should inform the design of interventions targeting this vulnerable population.
items.citation: Kathleen Kristensen, Leslie D. Williams, Charlie Kaplan et al.. A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks. Journal of Urban Health. 2026

items.title: Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads
items.summary: This paper developed an enzyme-free platform for ultrasensitive protein detection called efMOSAIC, designed to make advanced diagnostic assays accessible in resource-limited settings including low- and middle-income countries and point-of-care environments. The approach uses hybridization chain reaction to generate signal amplifiers on magnetic beads, replacing the enzyme-dependent steps required by existing digital protein detection methods such as Simoa and MOSAIC. The platform achieves detection limits comparable to Simoa for most proteins while using simpler assay workflows, and the signal amplifier reagents remain stable when stored at room temperature for up to six months. The researchers validated the system for detecting cytokines from human plasma and demonstrated its capacity for multiplexed biomarker detection. By combining ultrasensitive performance with temperature-stable reagents and simplified workflows, the platform is proposed as a means of extending next-generation protein diagnostics to settings that currently lack access to specialized instrumentation and stable cold-chain supply chains.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Karan Malhotra, Louise L. Hansen, Samuel Han et al.. Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the development and experimental validation of a uranium-based fission chamber designed to monitor neutron output from the SPARC tokamak across an extremely wide dynamic range of neutron yield rates. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Testing with both types of neutron generators confirmed that the detector's efficiency matched vendor specifications and that its response remained highly linear, with measured count rates agreeing well with neutronics simulations performed using OpenMC. Additional characterization demonstrated that the detector maintains reliable performance under conditions relevant to the SPARC environment, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation associated with long cable runs. The authors conclude that this fission chamber, combined with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height thresholds, represents a viable solution for fusion power measurements in the SPARC neutron diagnostics system.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme infrared colors. The authors obtained new medium-band NIRCam imaging taken roughly three and a half years after the original observations and performed precise relative astrometry using point-spread-function fitting and a robust local reference frame. They detected a clear proper motion, ruling out any extragalactic origin at very high statistical significance, and found that the source's spectral energy distribution is best matched by a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K located within the Milky Way's stellar disc. Capotauro is thus identified as one of the most distant Y dwarfs known, serendipitously discovered in a deep extragalactic survey field. The study highlights the power of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing cool Galactic substellar objects from genuine high-redshift galaxy candidates.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics
items.summary: This paper investigates the ability of next-generation cosmic microwave background experiments, particularly CMB-S4, to measure the effective number of relativistic species in the early universe, a parameter that encodes the energy density contributed by neutrinos and other light relics. The authors performed Fisher-matrix forecasts across multiple proposed CMB-S4 survey configurations to project their sensitivity to this parameter. They find that the conceptual design can achieve sub-percent precision on this parameter within its planned observing period, with the revised configuration reaching comparable precision over a longer timescale, and that a cosmic-variance-limited survey defines the ultimate frontier of improvement. The work also discusses the broader physics implications of such precise measurements for big bang nucleosynthesis, light thermal relics, and early-universe particle physics beyond the Standard Model. To support these analyses and future studies, the authors publicly released a pipeline tool that handles the full forecasting process from simulated foreground maps through component separation and delensing to parameter sensitivity projections.
items.citation: Cynthia Trendafilova, Srinivasan Raghunathan, Benjamin Wallisch et al.. Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation
items.summary: This paper investigates the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation, a model for phase separation in active matter systems, focusing on both its mathematical well-posedness and its coarsening dynamics. The authors develop analytical tools, including a method based on heteroclinic trajectories in the phase plane, to characterize static kink profiles, spherical droplet states, and surface tension modifications driven by activity and interface curvature. A central theoretical contribution is an explanation for the conjectured shift in the power-law growth exponent of the characteristic domain length from the classical value to a slower one induced by activity, revealing this as a transitory regime before the system reaches a finite saturation length. On the numerical side, the authors construct a finite element scheme and prove its well-posedness, stability, and, for singular potentials, convergence to weak solutions satisfying the physical boundedness constraint, with global well-posedness established in one dimension under a smallness condition on the activity parameter. Numerical simulations across multiple test cases confirm the theoretically predicted coarsening dynamics, including the power-law shift and eventual length saturation at late times.
items.citation: Abramo Agosti, Andrea Giorgini. Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.summary: This paper examined the fragmented landscape of open-source tools designed to mitigate risks associated with large language models in enterprise deployments, where manual harm identification has become difficult to scale. The researchers developed a structured, taxonomy-driven protocol that used a large language model-assisted retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to analyze the source code and documentation of prominent open-source tools, mapping their capabilities to subcategories of an extended AI risk mitigation taxonomy. Independent reviewer assessment indicated moderate agreement among raters, and the mapping protocol achieved a reasonable level of classification accuracy after majority voting. The analysis revealed a heavily skewed tooling landscape in which existing solutions cluster around technical and operational controls while governance, legal and regulatory, and financial and market risk categories remain largely unaddressed by available tools. The authors conclude that effective enterprise AI risk management requires a layered architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes, and they offer their mapping framework as applicable to both open-source and proprietary contexts.
items.citation: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj et al.. Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Blast Radius
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of excessive token consumption and context overflow in agentic coding systems by introducing a predictive memory management layer called Blast Radius. The system estimates how far an incoming prompt will reach across both conversational context and code, using two mechanisms: NECROPHORESIS for reversible eviction of dead context through verbatim archiving, and Recurring Dead Matter for identifying and suppressing repeatedly occurring transcripts. The authors formalize this approach over a Polish context space, connecting context entropy to the probability that evicted material will need to be recalled. Testing across multiple language models, Blast Radius substantially reduced token consumption, achieved the lowest context overflow rate among compared policies, and maintained perfect reversibility with no evicted content ever needing to be recalled. The work is positioned as a contribution to making large language model–based agentic coding more efficient and sustainable.
items.citation: MY Pitsane, Hope Mogale. Blast Radius. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a CRISPR-Cas12a-based diagnostic assay for the rapid detection of *Shigella flexneri* 2a, the serotype most commonly responsible for shigellosis in developing countries. The researchers designed two guide RNAs targeting serotype-specific genes and coupled recombinase polymerase amplification with Cas12a-mediated collateral cleavage, allowing detection via fluorescence or lateral flow without specialized equipment. The assay achieved a detection limit of ten copies per microliter, completed the isothermal reaction within one hour at room temperature, and showed complete analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity against other bacteria. Clinical validation using a large cohort of stool specimens demonstrated diagnostic sensitivity and specificity comparable to conventional PCR. The authors conclude that the assay's speed, simplicity, and accuracy make it well suited for clinical diagnostics and field-based surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for simultaneous point-of-care detection of multiple respiratory pathogens. The system combines a polymethyl methacrylate disc pre-loaded with lyophilized CRISPR/Cas13a reagents, a portable fluorescence analyzer, and a resin-based nucleic acid purification method to enable automated, multiplexed detection from throat swab samples following a single sample-loading step. The platform can screen six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples within a short timeframe, achieving single-copy analytical sensitivity without cross-reactivity between targets. Clinical validation using retrospective patient samples demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity, supporting the platform's accuracy for decentralized use. The authors conclude that iCARD offers a robust, high-throughput solution suitable for molecular screening and epidemiological surveillance outside of centralized laboratory settings.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examines a decade of progress in applying CRISPR-Cas systems to infectious disease management, covering diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine development within a unified framework. The authors surveyed translational advances across these three domains, highlighting platforms such as DETECTR and SHERLOCK for rapid pathogen detection, CRISPR-Cas9 strategies for targeting viral genomes and countering antimicrobial resistance, and the use of CRISPR tools to engineer live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. The review finds that CRISPR-based diagnostics have advanced furthest toward clinical evaluation, having moved from proof-of-concept to preclinical application, while therapeutic genome editing and personalized neoantigen vaccines remain at earlier, more exploratory stages due to delivery limitations and safety concerns. The authors identify delivery efficiency, off-target effects, and ethical and regulatory barriers as the principal obstacles that must be resolved before safe and equitable clinical translation can be achieved. They conclude that CRISPR-Cas holds transformative potential for infectious disease management but that realizing this potential will require systematic attention to both technical and governance challenges.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors systematically organized their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluate approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing designs that are simplified, rugged, and equipment-free. For amplification, they compare established and modified techniques such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP, highlighting adaptations that enable rapid, low-power, and portable operation. On the detection side, the review spans from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensor platforms leveraging CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.
items.summary: This paper investigated a previously unrecognized topological property of λ exonuclease, finding that duplex substrates with five-prime phosphates at both ends undergo self-sustained cyclic cleavage and reforming without requiring external amplification. Through biochemical and structural analyses, the researchers elucidated this topology-gated mechanism and engineered a dumbbell-shaped probe that sequesters these phosphate termini within dual RNA hairpin loops until target recognition occurs. Upon detection of a target RNA, CRISPR/Cas13 cleaves the hairpin loops to expose the hidden phosphates, activating the cyclic enzymatic reaction in a cascade called Topo-CRISPR. This system achieves attomolar sensitivity within a short timeframe and was validated on clinical samples for detection of enterovirus RNA and two microRNA/circular RNA targets, performing comparably to standard quantitative PCR methods. The platform was further extended to non-nucleic-acid targets through aptamer-based conformational control, establishing λ exonuclease as a general cyclic signal transducer for amplification-free ultrasensitive diagnostics.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Feng H, Wang Y, Zhao J et al.. Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies for bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on their role in addressing the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors conducted a structured comparative analysis of major platforms, including various forms of polymerase chain reaction, isothermal amplification, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and digital PCR, evaluating each across parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, speed, and multiplexing capability. The review also critically assessed how artificial intelligence and machine learning are being integrated into diagnostic workflows to support resistance prediction and clinical decision-making. Additionally, the translational potential of these technologies for point-of-care deployment was discussed alongside considerations of clinical validation and real-world operational constraints. The authors conclude that advancing culture-independent bacteriological diagnostics requires carefully balancing analytical performance with clinical interpretability, and they outline key challenges and future directions for the field.
items.citation: Cotelici AM, Bălășoiu AT, Boldeanu MV et al.. Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future trajectory of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, with a particular focus on electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic detection modalities applicable to both food safety and clinical settings. The authors surveyed advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies that have collectively improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-enabled traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review examines the diverse cell death programs relevant to cancer biology and their therapeutic implications. The paper surveys the major modalities of programmed cell death—including apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis—and synthesizes their roles in cancer development, progression, and treatment response. The authors present a unified conceptual framework, emphasizing that while apoptosis remains the predominant pathway triggered by conventional radiation and chemotherapy, non-apoptotic programs can drive inflammatory responses and shape interactions between tumor cells, stromal tissue, and the immune system, thereby influencing immunotherapy outcomes. Particular attention is given to ferroptosis, characterized as an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven modality arising from metabolic perturbations rather than a canonical induction signal. The review also addresses mechanisms by which cancer cells evade cell death and suppress immune responses, framing restoration of cell death as a promising therapeutic strategy.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, focusing on how light-activated nanoparticles can be used to modulate cellular and molecular pathways across a broad range of diseases. The authors surveyed the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that enable photodynamic and photothermal therapeutic modalities to achieve enhanced targeting, reactive oxygen species generation, and localized heating. At the molecular level, they analyze how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic cascades, and reshape immune responses through cytokine and T-cell modulation, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The review further critically evaluates regulatory agency-approved agents and recent clinical trial findings, identifying key barriers to clinical translation such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery, and regulatory challenges. The authors conclude that integrating molecular insights with clinical advances positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative, noninvasive strategy with broad therapeutic potential.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines new approach methodologies (NAMs) as human-centered alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which has historically suffered from high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-based, organoid-based, and computational approaches, situating these within evolving regulatory frameworks from major health agencies. The review covers how NAMs are being applied across the full drug-discovery continuum, from disease modeling and drug design through to efficacy testing and even the use of NAMs themselves as therapeutic candidates. Key biological, technical, and regulatory bottlenecks that currently limit robust translational adoption are identified and discussed. The authors conclude by outlining future human-centric discovery pipelines and the translational and societal considerations necessary for responsible implementation of these methodologies.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species that carries high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors comprehensively surveyed the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges that complicate its management. A central focus is placed on the inadequacy of conventional diagnostic methods, which cause harmful delays, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with the review evaluating both existing and emerging detection technologies as well as empiric and susceptibility-guided treatment strategies. The paper also addresses therapeutic complexities including mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the promise of combination therapy, while surveying agents under clinical investigation that target novel fungal pathways. Looking forward, the review highlights artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as potential avenues for improving patient outcomes in this evolving clinical challenge.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Beyond Extracellular Vesicle (EV) Hype: Practical Solutions and Remaining Hurdles in EV Research, Manufacturing, and Clinical Translation
items.summary: This review examines the current state of extracellular vesicle research, focusing on the analytical and translational challenges that limit progress from laboratory discovery to clinical application. The authors critically synthesize advances in EV isolation, detection, and single-particle analytics, which have revealed substantial molecular and functional heterogeneity among these nanoscale intercellular communication mediators. Key obstacles identified include incomplete mechanistic understanding, absence of standardized measurement frameworks, inconsistent regulatory classification, and the difficulty of defining EV identity and activity in a rigorous and reproducible way. The review addresses evolving regulatory frameworks and updated guidelines, advocating for operational definitions based on source material, isolation method, and molecular markers, alongside orthogonal analytical approaches, co-isolate quantification, and potency assays to support quality control. The authors argue that achieving analytical rigor is essential to transition EV research from largely descriptive work into a reproducible, quantitative measurement science capable of supporting therapeutic development.
items.citation: David J. Lundy, Zoe L. Chau, Sheng‐You Chen et al.. Beyond Extracellular Vesicle (EV) Hype: Practical Solutions and Remaining Hurdles in EV Research, Manufacturing, and Clinical Translation. Advanced Science. 2026

items.title: Efficient three-dimensional variational data assimilation of multi-plane PIV data
items.summary: This paper investigates three-dimensional variational data assimilation applied to sparse multi-plane stereoscopic particle image velocimetry measurements in the wake of a vehicle-like bluff body at high Reynolds number. The authors developed a discrete adjoint approach to optimize time-averaged momentum equations and introduced a novel technique called adjoint localization, which restricts the control variable space to a user-defined subdomain to reduce the memory demands of the method. By limiting the control variable to a small fraction of the full control space, they achieved a substantial reduction in peak memory usage while maintaining assimilated field quality comparable to the full-space approach. The method successfully recovered the correct asymmetric topology of a complex three-dimensional recirculation bubble, improved upon a baseline turbulence model, and produced physically consistent mean pressure and Reynolds shear stress fields. A data efficiency analysis further revealed that measurement coverage must extend at least to the end of the primary recirculation bubble to adequately constrain near-wake dynamics, underscoring the practical value of adjoint localization for industrial-scale separated flow problems.
items.citation: Uttam Cadambi Padmanaban, Samaresh Midya, Ping He et al.. Efficient three-dimensional variational data assimilation of multi-plane PIV data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper investigates how world models can improve end-to-end autonomous driving without incurring the high computational cost of generating future video frames at inference time. The authors propose SimWAM, a framework that uses video generation solely as a training signal by co-training a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert through joint flow matching, with an isolated attention mask ensuring that action prediction remains independent of future frames. Once training is complete, the video generation branch is discarded entirely, leaving a self-contained planner that predicts trajectories directly with low latency. The system is further refined using reinforcement learning to optimize a compositional driving reward that goes beyond simple trajectory imitation. SimWAM achieves competitive performance on the NAVSIM benchmark, outperforms existing world-action-model-based planners while running faster, and generalizes zero-shot to another dataset, establishing it as an efficient and scalable baseline for autonomous driving.
items.citation: Zongchuang Zhao, Xin Zhou, Tianyang Xu et al.. SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the characterization of a prototype uranium-238 fission chamber designed for neutron diagnostics on the SPARC tokamak, which must operate reliably across many orders of magnitude in neutron yield during high-performance deuterium-tritium plasma operations. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Experimental testing with DD and DT neutron generators confirmed vendor-specified detection efficiencies and demonstrated excellent linearity, with measured count rates agreeing well with OpenMC neutronics simulations. Additional testing demonstrated the detector's robustness against environmentally relevant stray magnetic fields and potential signal degradation from long cable runs. The results establish that the fission chamber, used alongside neutron shielding and appropriate pulse height thresholds, provides a reliable approach to fusion power measurement within the SPARC neutron diagnostic system.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Maximal estimates for perturbations of the Schrödinger operator on $\mathbb{T}^d$
items.summary: The paper investigates maximal estimates of the form $L^p_x L^\infty_t$ for exponential sums associated to smooth hypersurfaces, motivated by questions about the periodic Schrödinger equation on the torus. The authors demonstrate that the conjectured maximal estimate for the periodic Schrödinger equation breaks down when the paraboloid is subjected to small perturbations, extending a previously known one-dimensional phenomenon to arbitrary higher dimensions. To establish this, the authors employ lower bounds for incidence estimates, for which they develop an alternative proof using homogeneous dynamics rather than the original approach. The failure of the conjecture is shown to be essentially sharp at the decoupling endpoint for the paraboloid, indicating that the perturbation results are tight in a precise sense.
items.citation: Inbo Gottlieb Fenves, Jiahao Tan. Maximal estimates for perturbations of the Schrödinger operator on $\mathbb{T}^d$. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MirrorWorld: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Mirror Reflection Generation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of generating physically plausible mirror reflections in video, where both the semantic content and spatial geometry of reflections must remain consistent with the surrounding scene. The authors identify two complementary sub-problems: determining what scene content should appear in a mirror and how that content should be spatially arranged within the mirror region. To address these, they propose MirrorWorld, a reflection-aware video inpainting framework incorporating two novel components: Semantic Relation Distillation, which transfers relational knowledge from a frozen visual foundation model to associate scene content with mirror regions, and Geometric Transformation Alignment, which learns spatial transformations to guide the arrangement of reflected content. They also construct a unified benchmark by repurposing existing video mirror datasets into a reflection reconstruction task. Experimental results demonstrate that MirrorWorld outperforms both image-based reflection generation methods and strong video inpainting baselines on this benchmark.
items.citation: Youjun Zhao, Alex Warren, Gary K. L. Tam et al.. MirrorWorld: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Mirror Reflection Generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme near-infrared colors. To test whether the source might instead be a nearby cool brown dwarf, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST NIRCam imaging roughly three and a half years after the discovery observations and performed precise relative astrometry using a robust local reference frame and injection-recovery analysis. They detected a clear proper motion inconsistent with any extragalactic origin at high statistical significance, ruling out the high-redshift galaxy interpretation. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identifies Capotauro as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature around 350 K, placing it at a distance that makes it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The authors conclude that multi-epoch imaging is a powerful tool for identifying cool brown dwarf contaminants among extreme photometric-redshift candidates found in deep extragalactic survey fields.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, noninvasive electronic nose could detect SARS-CoV-2 infection as an alternative to conventional diagnostic methods that are often uncomfortable and slow. The device used an array of commercially available metal-oxide gas sensors to capture and analyze volatile organic compounds in both saliva and exhaled breath, which change in composition in the presence of the virus. Several machine learning algorithms were then applied to classify samples as infected or non-infected. Detection performance was comparable across sample types, with exhaled breath yielding slightly higher accuracy than saliva, and the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm achieving the best overall discrimination. The findings support the proof-of-concept feasibility of this approach for point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 screening in real-world clinical settings.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.
items.summary: This study investigated the fungal microbiome (mycobiome) across multiple body compartments in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), a condition previously associated with bacterial dysbiosis but whose fungal alterations had not been well characterized. Using ITS1 amplicon sequencing on saliva, sputum, and stool samples from adults with CVID and healthy controls, the researchers profiled fungal communities and applied diversity analyses, multivariate modeling, and machine learning to identify distinguishing features. They found that mycobiome composition differed significantly between CVID patients and controls across all three sites, with reduced fungal richness and evenness, particularly in respiratory and oral samples. A consistent pattern of enrichment in opportunistic yeasts, especially *Candida albicans*, alongside depletion of commensal and environmental fungi, was observed in CVID regardless of whether patients had immune dysregulation or infectious-only manifestations. Machine learning models built on fungal profiles showed strong discriminatory performance in distinguishing CVID from controls, supporting the potential utility of fungal signatures as non-invasive biomarkers and suggesting a pathobiont role for *C. albicans* in this immunodeficiency.
items.citation: Cabanero-Navalon MD, Carda-Diéguez M, Mira A et al.. Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.. Frontiers in immunology. 2026

items.title: Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether tuberculosis could be diagnosed using DNA from *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* found in salivary exosomes, offering a non-sputum-based alternative to conventional diagnostic methods. The researchers developed an exosomal nucleic acid approach that integrates salivary exosome enrichment, nucleic acid extraction, and dual-target quantitative PCR melting curve analysis, then evaluated its performance in a pilot clinical study of adults with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. Salivary exosomal DNA was found to be the predominant detectable form of *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* DNA in saliva, and the method substantially reduced turnaround time compared to standard approaches while achieving a low limit of detection. The assay demonstrated moderate-to-good sensitivity and specificity against microbiological reference standards, and these diagnostic metrics were largely maintained in the clinically challenging subset of patients with negative smear microscopy, who represent paucibacillary cases. The authors conclude that this non-invasive, rapid salivary diagnostic shows promise for tuberculosis detection but requires multicenter validation in broader populations before clinical implementation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Ma J, Zheng X, He Y et al.. Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in support of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and integration with the body, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also assessed. The review concludes that while significant progress has been made in materials, device architectures, and AI-assisted strategies, persistent challenges remain in areas such as motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and clinical interpretability of sensor outputs.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Gastroduodenal Disorders
items.summary: This paper presents a classification framework for gastroduodenal disorders, organizing symptoms attributable to the gastroduodenal region into five distinct diagnostic categories. The categories encompass functional dyspepsia with its two overlapping subcategories, nausea and vomiting disorders with three subcategories including cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome, and excessive belching disorders distinguished by the anatomical origin of refluxed gas. The framework also includes the inability to belch syndrome as a newly defined category based on self-reported symptomatology, as well as rumination syndrome characterized by repetitive effortless regurgitation. The abstract is primarily taxonomic in nature, providing definitions and subcategory structures rather than reporting findings from an original empirical study.
items.citation: H. Tornblom, Florencia Carbone, William L. Hasler et al.. Gastroduodenal Disorders. Gastroenterology. 2026

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles, membrane-bound particles secreted by most cell types that mediate intercellular communication by transporting diverse molecular cargos including proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and metabolites. The paper surveys the biological origins of these vesicles, with particular attention to exosomes, which arise through the endosomal pathway via multivesicular body formation, as well as the various methods used to isolate and characterize them from biological fluids and cultured cells. A range of isolation approaches is compared, including ultracentrifugation, size-exclusion chromatography, and immunoaffinity capture, each carrying distinct trade-offs in purity, scalability, and vesicle integrity, while characterization techniques such as nanoparticle tracking analysis, electron microscopy, and flow cytometry are discussed for assessing vesicle properties. The review highlights the considerable therapeutic promise of extracellular vesicles as diagnostic biomarkers, drug delivery vehicles, cell-free therapeutics, and tools in regenerative medicine, owing to their biocompatibility and inherent targeting capabilities. The authors conclude that despite rapid progress in the field, standardization of sourcing, production, purification, and drug loading remains a critical challenge that must be addressed before clinical translation can be achieved.
items.citation: Madison Schank, Juan Zhao, L Wang et al.. Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential. Biomedicines. 2026

items.title: Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions
items.summary: This review examines the role of biomaterials in advancing personalized drug delivery, covering a broad range of material classes including polymers, metals, ceramics, and composites. The authors trace the conceptual evolution of biomaterials from inert biological interfaces to rationally engineered systems capable of controlled drug release through diffusion, degradation, or stimulus-responsive mechanisms, and survey nanostructured carriers such as liposomes, micelles, and dendrimers that improve solubility, cellular uptake, and targeted accumulation. The review synthesizes recent progress at the intersection of regenerative medicine, nanotechnology, and precision healthcare, highlighting how tunable physicochemical properties enable protection of fragile therapeutics and reduced systemic dosing frequency relative to conventional formulations. Despite these innovations, the authors identify persistent barriers to clinical translation, including immune–biomaterial interactions, manufacturing variability, unpredictable long-term biodegradation, and regulatory scalability constraints. They conclude that future progress requires precision fabrication strategies, manufacturing-practice-compatible production pipelines, and biologically informed design that accommodates patient-specific variability.
items.citation: Adna Hrapović, Nadia Islam, Asmaa Al Bourghli et al.. Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions. PeerJ. 2026

items.title: Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application
items.summary: This review examined how polymer-based biosensors perform analytically when applied to complex real-world samples across food, beverage, environmental, and clinical contexts. The authors conducted a meta-trend analysis of nearly a hundred original research articles spanning a decade, evaluating four distinct polymer classes—conductive polymers, redox-mediator polymers, hydrogels, and molecularly imprinted polymers—with respect to their ability to handle matrix interference and maintain reliable performance. Electrochemical detection was found to dominate the field, with each polymer class offering distinct advantages: conductive polymers reduce interference from electroactive species, hydrogels preserve enzyme function in protein-rich environments, and molecularly imprinted polymers excel at trace-level detection under harsh conditions. However, the review also exposed substantial validation gaps, with the vast majority of studies omitting key quantification metrics and roughly a third lacking reproducibility or precision data, undermining confidence in reported results. The authors identify maintaining calibration across varied hostile matrices as the central barrier to commercial deployment and highlight emerging architectures such as nanocapsulation, hierarchical nanocomposites, and microneedle-integrated systems as promising routes to improved fouling resistance and operational stability.
items.citation: Marcello Mascini, Sara Palmieri, Fabiola Eugelio et al.. Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review
items.summary: This systematic review examined the scope and impact of artificial intelligence integration in medical devices for personalized healthcare, analyzing both the technological innovations enabling this integration and the barriers impeding its full realization. The authors conducted a systematic review drawing on peer-reviewed literature, industry analyses, and regulatory advisories published over a seven-year period, evaluating current applications, implementation challenges, and strategies for overcoming them. The review found significant advances across diagnostics, treatment personalization, wearable health monitoring, and smart prosthetics, with AI diagnostic tools demonstrating high classification accuracy for disease detection from imaging data. Key challenges identified include data security risks, algorithmic bias, regulatory constraints, and difficulties integrating AI systems with existing healthcare infrastructure, though strategies such as improved data validation, updated regulatory frameworks, and ethical guidelines were found effective in addressing these barriers. The authors conclude that while AI-driven personalization holds transformative potential for precision medicine, successful implementation depends on resolving these technical, ethical, and regulatory challenges, with emerging technologies such as quantum computing and blockchain-based data management offering promising future directions.
items.citation: Hemanth Ponnambalath Mohanadas, A Manikandan, Ahmad Fauzi Ismail et al.. Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2026

items.title: Why Andes hantavirus is not the next SARS-CoV-2: contrasting viral shedding, transmissibility and genomic patterns.
items.summary: The paper examined whether Andes hantavirus poses a pandemic threat comparable to SARS-CoV-2, prompted by a cruise ship-associated outbreak that raised concerns about transmissibility and spread. The authors analyzed contrasting features of the two viruses, including modes of shedding, transmission dynamics, and genomic diversity patterns. They found that despite Andes virus being capable of respiratory entry and limited human-to-human spread under close contact, it differs fundamentally from SARS-CoV-2 in its rodent-borne ecology, vascular rather than respiratory pathogenesis, reliance on blood-based diagnostics, and genetic diversity driven by reservoir biology and geography rather than sustained human transmission or immune selection. The paper concludes that these characteristics collectively explain why Andes hantavirus is unlikely to become the next pandemic respiratory pathogen.
items.venue: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin
items.citation: Bal A, Sauvage V, Bouscambert-Duchamp M et al.. Why Andes hantavirus is not the next SARS-CoV-2: contrasting viral shedding, transmissibility and genomic patterns.. Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing. The authors surveyed the field by organizing it into three core operational stages: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing designs that are simple, robust, and equipment-free. They also reviewed key amplification strategies, ranging from conventional polymerase chain reaction to isothermal methods such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, all adapted for portable and low-power conditions. On the detection side, the review covers platforms from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, concluding that these emerging technologies offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition suited to point-of-care environments.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.
items.summary: The paper studied whether a commercial rapid quantitative PCR assay originally designed for throat swabs could accurately detect *Streptococcus pyogenes* from pediatric pleural fluids, a specimen type relevant to diagnosing invasive Group A streptococcal pneumonia. The researchers evaluated the Xpert Xpress Strep A assay against a composite reference standard consisting of bacterial culture and a laboratory-developed PCR targeting a separate gene, using a convenience sample of pediatric pleural fluid specimens collected over approximately two years. The Xpert assay detected all positive specimens, achieving perfect agreement with the composite reference standard and the laboratory-developed PCR, while standard bacterial culture identified only a minority of confirmed positive cases. These findings demonstrate that Xpert Xpress Strep A is substantially more sensitive than culture for detecting *S. pyogenes* in pleural fluid, likely because many patients had received antibiotics prior to sample collection. The authors conclude that the assay has strong diagnostic utility in this setting, offering rapid turnaround that can support timely clinical management and public health decision-making for close-contact chemoprophylaxis.
items.citation: Amaral G, Gadkar VJ, Almodahka A et al.. Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform for addressing challenges in energy, environment, and healthcare. The authors survey its synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies, highlighting how its layered structure enables extensive surface functionalization and tunable configurations spanning zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers a broad range of applications, including environmental remediation through adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, energy storage and conversion technologies such as hydrogen production and battery systems, and advanced sensing platforms including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for detecting biological and organic molecules. The authors present graphene oxide's tunable band gap, high surface area, and adaptable surface chemistry as properties underpinning its transformative potential across these domains. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges facing the material, including scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, and proposes possible solutions to enable sustainable real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026
