items.title: Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry
items.summary: Researchers developed and evaluated chitosan–eugenol carbon dots as a multifunctional nanomaterial for dental applications, motivated by the need for agents that simultaneously combat infection and support tissue regeneration. The carbon dots were synthesized from biocompatible chitosan and eugenol, then characterized for their physical and chemical properties using electron microscopy and elemental analysis, which confirmed spherical nanoparticles with successful incorporation of heteroatoms and surface functional groups. Antibacterial performance was assessed against Streptococcus mutans, a key pathogen in dental caries and pulp inflammation, and the material demonstrated concentration-dependent inhibition at defined minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations. Biocompatibility testing using fibroblast cells showed preserved cell viability and morphology alongside enhanced migratory activity, suggesting strong potential for wound healing. The authors conclude that combining chitosan and eugenol within a carbon dot framework yields a synergistic nanoplatform with fluorescent, antibacterial, and cytocompatible properties suited to oral infection management and tissue repair.
items.citation: N. Narayanan, Aruchamy Mohanprasanth, Natesan Thirumalaivasan. Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances
items.summary: This review examines bacterial biofilms, which are structured microbial communities encased in a self-produced extracellular polymeric substance matrix that confers protection against antimicrobial agents and host immune defenses, making them central to chronic and difficult-to-treat infections. The paper synthesizes current knowledge of biofilm biology, covering the stages of biofilm development, the composition and protective roles of the matrix, and the physiological heterogeneity that emerges during maturation. It also details the multiple overlapping resistance mechanisms that make biofilms so recalcitrant, including restricted antibiotic diffusion, enzymatic inactivation, efflux pump upregulation, persister cell formation, and horizontal gene transfer, and reviews the clinical contexts in which biofilms are implicated, such as cystic fibrosis, chronic wounds, osteomyelitis, implant-associated infections, and breast implant illness. Conventional and emerging detection strategies are discussed alongside a range of therapeutic approaches, including matrix-disrupting enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, bacteriophages, metabolic reactivators, and nanotechnology-based delivery systems, with the argument that no single modality is sufficient on its own. The authors conclude that effective management of biofilm-associated disease requires integrated detection and multifaceted treatment strategies, and that advances in multi-omics and systems-level modeling will be essential for developing next-generation interventions.
items.citation: Pranay Amruth Maroju, Angad S. Sidhu, Amogh R. Motaganahalli et al.. Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Diet and Gut Microbiota in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Clinical and Nutritional Perspective
items.summary: This paper examined the relationships between diet, gut microbiota, and inflammatory bowel disease, encompassing both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, within a clinical and nutritional framework. The authors reviewed epidemiological and interventional evidence linking dietary patterns to disease risk and progression, finding that high-fiber and healthy diets reduce susceptibility while ultra-processed and inflammatory dietary patterns increase it. Specific therapeutic nutritional strategies, including exclusive enteral nutrition, the Crohn's Disease Exclusion Diet, and the Mediterranean diet, were found capable of inducing and maintaining remission while favorably reshaping the gut microbiome by enriching butyrate-producing bacteria and reducing pathogenic taxa. The paper also highlighted that micronutrient deficiencies are highly prevalent in this patient population and that nutritional status meaningfully affects surgical outcomes and responses to biologic therapies. The authors conclude that personalized, microbiome-informed dietary strategies integrated into multidisciplinary care plans represent a promising frontier, though realizing this potential will require standardized clinical trials and precision nutrition approaches tailored to individual disease and microbial profiles.
items.citation: Luisa Bertin, Sonia Facchin, Brigida Barberio et al.. Diet and Gut Microbiota in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Clinical and Nutritional Perspective. Pharmaceuticals. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines antimicrobial resistance as a critical global public health threat, focusing on the bacterial pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these pathogens evade existing antibiotics, encompassing reduced membrane permeability, efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic discovery pipelines have largely failed to keep pace with resistance, and assesses a range of emerging therapeutic strategies including artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds, while addressing their translational and regulatory challenges. The authors also consider practical barriers such as toxicity, dosing optimization, and resistance re-emergence that complicate clinical implementation of these novel approaches. They conclude that overcoming resistance in priority pathogens will require integrated, multidisciplinary efforts spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, and public health, including robust antimicrobial stewardship and a One Health framework connecting human, animal, and environmental domains.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.
items.summary: The paper studied three synthetic peptide epitopes derived from *Streptococcus agalactiae* proteins — GroEL, enolase, and EF-Tu — as components of an ELISA-based immunodiagnostic assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women. The researchers developed prototype assays using these epitopes individually and in combination to detect IgG, IgM, and IgA antibodies in serum samples from GBS-positive and GBS-negative individuals, aiming to provide an alternative to the current culture-based gold standard, which is slow and can yield ambiguous results. All three epitopes, whether used alone or in combination, significantly distinguished between GBS-positive and GBS-negative sera, with the enolase- and EF-Tu-derived epitopes performing best as individual candidates due to their lower required concentrations and higher immunoreactivity. Combining the epitopes in various mixtures further improved immunoreactivity across all tested antibody classes. The authors conclude that this epitope-based ELISA represents a promising and potentially pioneering diagnostic approach with no comparable test currently available on the market.
items.citation: Brzychczy-Włoch M, Dobrut A, Drożdż K et al.. Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.. Applied microbiology and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a syndromic molecular panel for central nervous system infections by comparing it against conventional cerebrospinal fluid culture in a real-world clinical setting over three years. Using a large dataset of paired molecular and culture results, researchers calculated diagnostic concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values both across all pathogens and when restricted to bacterial targets covered by the panel. The syndromic panel showed moderate overall agreement with culture, with sensitivity improving substantially when analysis was limited to pathogens included within the panel's target range, and the panel achieved a very high negative predictive value for those targets. However, conventional culture identified clinically relevant organisms not covered by the syndromic panel, including several bacterial pathogens of importance, underscoring a meaningful diagnostic gap. The authors conclude that syndromic panels cannot function as standalone assays and must be systematically combined with conventional culture to ensure comprehensive pathogen detection and guide appropriate antimicrobial treatment.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Sberna G, D'Arezzo S, Valli MB et al.. Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the LIAISON PLEX Gram-Positive Blood Culture Assay, a multiplexed molecular test designed to rapidly identify gram-positive bacterial pathogens and antibiotic resistance markers directly from positive blood culture bottles. The assay was assessed across multiple sites using a combination of prospective clinical samples, pre-selected samples, and contrived specimens, along with analytical testing for inclusivity, cross-reactivity, and interference. The assay demonstrated very high overall sensitivity and specificity for detecting its panel of gram-positive bacterial targets and resistance markers, with strong performance maintained across different blood culture bottle types, in the presence of potential interfering substances, and in polymicrobial infection scenarios. Nearly all strains tested in the inclusivity study were correctly detected, and cross-reactivity with off-panel organisms was minimal. The authors conclude that the assay offers fast, accurate, and reliable identification of gram-positive organisms and their resistance genes from positive blood cultures, with potential to support timely antibiotic optimization and patient management decisions.
items.citation: Chow S-K, Stevig C, Granato P et al.. Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of Group B Streptococcus colonization in pregnant women, given its association with neonatal infections and preterm stillbirth. The researchers developed and validated an in-house diagnostic assay combining CRISPR/Cas12a technology with recombinase polymerase amplification, enabling isothermal detection without complex instrumentation. The assay was assessed for specificity against other common female reproductive tract pathogens, and its detection limit was established using serially diluted plasmid standards. Clinical validation was performed using vaginal-rectal swabs from pregnant women, with results compared against a commercial quantitative real-time PCR method, showing strong concordance. The assay completed testing within one hour and produced results interpretable by either visual inspection or fluorescence reader, demonstrating high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy suitable for clinical application.
items.venue: International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM
items.citation: Hu S, Xie J, Liu L et al.. Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.. International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM. 2026

items.title: Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the real-world diagnostic performance and clinical utility of multiplex PCR panels used to detect pathogens causing meningitis and encephalitis from cerebrospinal fluid samples over a five-year period at a tertiary care hospital. Researchers retrospectively reviewed test results alongside clinical data to determine how often positive findings led to meaningful changes in diagnosis or patient management. Viral pathogens dominated the positive detections, with human herpesvirus-6, enterovirus, and herpes simplex virus type-1 being most frequently identified, while Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most common bacterial finding. Despite the panels' capacity for rapid, broad pathogen identification, fewer than half of positive results were associated with a clinically relevant action, and repeat testing after an initial negative result offered little additional diagnostic benefit. The authors conclude that suboptimal test utilisation—including ordering panels for conditions outside their scope and insufficient clinician familiarity with panel content—limits the clinical impact of these tools, and that clearer testing criteria are needed to improve diagnostic efficiency.
items.venue: The Indian journal of medical research
items.citation: Gürler M, Karaoğlu Ç, Yurtcu EE et al.. Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.. The Indian journal of medical research. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviewed advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types. Novel specimen approaches, including tongue swabs and stool samples, have improved bacteriological confirmation particularly in children and others unable to produce sputum, while targeted next-generation sequencing has been recognised for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Urine lipoarabinomannan-based assays offer diagnostic benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease, and host blood transcriptomic signatures show promise for triage and prognosis, though various proteomic, metabolomic, and other biomarkers remain under evaluation. Despite these advances, the authors identify persistent performance, implementation, and equity gaps, and note that no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing. The authors systematically surveyed the field by organizing the diagnostic workflow into three core operational stages: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing their suitability for simplified, equipment-free use in resource-limited settings. Amplification strategies reviewed include both conventional polymerase chain reaction and isothermal alternatives such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, all of which have been adapted for portable and low-power conditions. On the detection side, the review covers a spectrum from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensor platforms exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch mechanisms, which together offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition at the point of care.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated a novel electrochemical nucleic acid amplification test that couples isothermal amplification with real-time voltammetric detection for infectious disease diagnostics. Rather than relying on optical readout methods that can introduce detection challenges, the approach monitors proton release during amplification using a pH-sensing redox compound, enabling electrochemical signal measurement. The platform was tested against multiple respiratory viral pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, and equine herpesvirus, using both purified RNA from clinical samples and an extraction-free workflow. The method achieved a limit of detection of fifty copies per reaction for influenza A virus and demonstrated high concordance with RT-qPCR across hundreds of clinical samples. The authors conclude that real-time voltammetric LAMP is feasible across diverse sample types, while acknowledging that broader validation in additional matrices and prospective cohorts is still needed.
items.citation: Munita R, Lyttleton R, Danefur E et al.. A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.. ACS omega. 2026

items.title: Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.
items.summary: This review paper examined isothermal nucleic acid amplification methods as alternatives to conventional PCR-based diagnostics. The authors compiled and synthesized information on the major isothermal techniques developed over the past two decades, including loop-mediated isothermal amplification, helicase-dependent amplification, rolling circle amplification, strand displacement amplification, nucleic acid sequence-based amplification, and recombinase polymerase amplification. Because these methods operate at a constant temperature and do not require thermal cycling equipment, they offer simplified, rapid, and cost-effective nucleic acid detection suited for resource-limited settings. The review addresses a gap in the literature by providing a unified overview of the reaction principles, product detection strategies, and disease diagnosis applications for these techniques in a single comprehensive resource. The authors also discuss the advantages of each method and offer perspectives on their future development in clinical and research contexts.
items.citation: Amare Amdiyee A, Sisay Tessema T. Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.. Practical laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.
items.summary: This study developed and evaluated a multiplex one-tube nested real-time PCR assay integrated with a point-of-care testing instrument for detecting three streptococcal pathogens responsible for cerebrospinal fluid infections. The researchers assessed sensitivity using recombinant plasmids, evaluated specificity against common CSF pathogens, and tested the system on both simulated and clinical CSF samples, comparing performance against conventional real-time PCR with manual nucleic acid extraction. The integrated point-of-care system achieved very low detection limits for all three target pathogens in simulated samples while reducing total turnaround time to approximately two hours through fully automated nucleic acid extraction. In clinical sample testing, the new assay identified additional positive cases that conventional real-time PCR had missed, demonstrating superior sensitivity. The authors conclude that this approach offers a rapid, highly sensitive, culture-free, and operationally streamlined method for diagnosing bacterial meningitis pathogens directly from cerebrospinal fluid.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Wu J, Zhao Z, Pang P et al.. A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies for bacterial infections, with particular attention to their role in improving etiological diagnosis amid growing antimicrobial resistance. The authors conducted a structured comparative analysis of major platforms including various forms of PCR, isothermal amplification, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and digital PCR, evaluating each across parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, turnaround time, and multiplexing capacity. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into diagnostic workflows for resistance prediction and clinical decision support was also critically assessed. Additionally, the review considered the translational potential of these technologies for point-of-care deployment, weighing clinical validation requirements and real-world operational constraints against analytical performance. The authors conclude that advancing culture-independent bacteriological diagnostics requires balancing analytical rigor with clinical interpretability, and they outline key challenges and future directions for the field.
items.citation: Cotelici AM, Bălășoiu AT, Boldeanu MV et al.. Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey
items.summary: This survey examines the intersection of foundation models and computational healthcare through a data-centric lens, focusing on how these AI systems can address longstanding challenges in clinical data acquisition, quality, and processing. The authors review a broad range of data-centric approaches spanning the full lifecycle of foundation models, from pre-training through inference, and assess their applicability to healthcare workflows. Key topics covered include data characterization, annotation, patient privacy, and ethical considerations that are particularly acute in medical contexts. The survey also addresses AI security, model assessment, and alignment with human values as critical dimensions for deploying foundation models responsibly in clinical settings. The authors conclude with an outlook on how foundation model-based analytics may improve patient outcomes and streamline clinical workflows as the healthcare AI landscape continues to evolve.
items.citation: Yunkun Zhang, Jin Gao, Zheling Tan et al.. Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey. ACM Computing Surveys. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with a focus on platforms suitable for clinical and field-based applications. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, evaluating how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examined candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that carries high mortality and significant healthcare costs. The authors synthesized current knowledge across the full spectrum of the condition, encompassing its epidemiology, species distribution, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies. A central focus was placed on the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods that contribute to delayed treatment, as well as the growing challenge of antifungal resistance and the role of susceptibility-guided therapy in improving outcomes. The review also evaluated emerging diagnostic technologies, novel antifungal agents in development, and combination therapy approaches targeting new fungal pathways. Looking forward, the authors highlight promising future directions including the use of artificial intelligence in diagnostics and vaccine-based prophylaxis as potential tools for improving candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the development and experimental validation of a uranium-based fission chamber intended to monitor neutron emission during high-performance plasma operations on the SPARC tokamak, which must function across many orders of magnitude in neutron yield. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation designed to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Testing with both types of neutron generators confirmed that the detector meets vendor-specified efficiencies, exhibits excellent linearity, and produces count rates consistent with Monte Carlo neutronics simulations. Additional characterization demonstrated robustness against environmental stresses relevant to the SPARC environment, including stray magnetic fields and signal degradation over long cable runs. The authors conclude that the fission chamber, when combined with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height discrimination, constitutes a reliable component of the SPARC neutron diagnostic suite for fusion power measurements.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme near-infrared colors. To test this claim, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST imaging approximately three and a half years after the original observations and performed precise relative astrometry using point-spread-function fitting and a carefully defined local reference frame. They detected a clear proper motion of the source across the observation baseline, ruling out any extragalactic explanation at high statistical significance. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates instead identifies Capotauro as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature near 350 K, located within the Milky Way disc at a distance of several hundred parsecs, making it one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. The study underscores the importance of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing cold substellar objects from genuine high-redshift galaxy candidates.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics
items.summary: This paper investigates how well next-generation cosmic microwave background experiments can constrain the effective number of relativistic species, a parameter that encodes the energy density of neutrinos and other light relics in the early universe. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, the authors evaluated multiple survey configurations under consideration for CMB-S4, assessing their projected sensitivity to this parameter. The conceptual design achieves a constraint tighter than a threshold that would enable percent-level measurements over its planned observing period, with a revised configuration reaching equivalent precision over a longer timeline. The study also benchmarks these results against a cosmic-variance-limited survey to identify the remaining room for improvement from instrumental, observational, and theoretical advances. The authors additionally discuss implications for big bang nucleosynthesis, light thermal relics, and early-universe physics more broadly, and release a public end-to-end forecasting pipeline applicable to other CMB survey designs.
items.citation: Cynthia Trendafilova, Srinivasan Raghunathan, Benjamin Wallisch et al.. Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation
items.summary: The paper investigates the active Cahn-Hilliard equation, a model describing phase separation dynamics in active matter systems, addressing both its mathematical well-posedness and the characterization of its coarsening behavior. Using a method based on heteroclinic trajectories in the phase plane, the authors analyze static kink profiles and droplet states, and develop a theory of surface tension modified by activity and interface curvature to explain how activity shifts the power-law growth of characteristic domain length. This theoretical analysis predicts a transitory change in the coarsening exponent before the system reaches a finite saturation length, rather than indefinite coarsening. On the numerical side, the authors construct and analyze a finite element scheme, proving its well-posedness and stability for both regular polynomial and singular logarithmic potentials, and establish local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in two and three dimensions, as well as global-in-time well-posedness in one dimension under a smallness condition on the activity parameter. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted power-law shift in coarsening dynamics and the eventual saturation of the domain length, validating the theoretical findings.
items.citation: Abramo Agosti, Andrea Giorgini. Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.summary: This paper examined the fragmented landscape of open-source tools designed to mitigate risks associated with large language models in enterprise deployments, where manual harm identification struggles to keep pace with rapid adoption. The researchers developed a structured, taxonomy-driven protocol that used a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation to automatically analyze the source code and documentation of prominent open-source tools, mapping their capabilities onto the subcategories of an extended AI risk mitigation taxonomy. The analysis revealed a highly skewed distribution in which available tools cluster heavily around technical and operational controls, while governance, legal and regulatory, and financial and market risk categories remain largely unaddressed by existing open-source solutions. The mapping protocol demonstrated reasonable performance after majority voting, and reliability assessment among independent reviewers showed moderate agreement. The study concludes by motivating a layered risk-mitigation architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes, and it identifies domains where human oversight remains essential rather than automatable.
items.citation: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj et al.. Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Blast Radius
items.summary: The paper addresses inefficiencies in agentic coding systems, specifically the high token consumption and context overflow that make large language model use costly and wasteful. The authors developed Blast Radius, a predictive memory management system that estimates how far an incoming prompt will reach across both conversational context and code, using a mechanism called NECROPHORESIS to reversibly archive unused context and a concept called Recurring Dead Matter to identify and remove repeatedly occurring transcripts. The approach is grounded in a formal mathematical framework over a Polish context space, linking context entropy to the probability of needing to retrieve archived material. Testing across multiple language models showed that the system substantially reduced token usage, achieved the lowest context overflow rate among compared policies, and maintained perfect reversibility, with the vast majority of archived content identified as recurring dead matter and none requiring recall. The work positions Blast Radius as a component of a broader framework for making agentic coding more sustainable and reusable.
items.citation: MY Pitsane, Hope Mogale. Blast Radius. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a lateral flow immunoassay-based rapid antigen test designed to simultaneously detect SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus from nasopharyngeal swab specimens. Archived specimens were tested in parallel with the rapid antigen test and real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, which served as the reference standard, and cross-reactivity against a panel of respiratory pathogens was also assessed. The test demonstrated high sensitivity for all four viral targets, particularly in specimens with high viral loads, and achieved perfect specificity with no observed cross-reactivity against any of the tested microbial strains. Performance was consistently strong in specimens with low cycle threshold values, indicating reliable detection when viral burden is high, but sensitivity declined in low viral load specimens. The authors conclude that the test is a useful rapid screening and initial differentiation tool for major respiratory viruses but should complement rather than replace molecular testing due to its reduced sensitivity in low viral load settings.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kang M, Yu HJ et al.. Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients
items.summary: This study investigated the burden of respiratory syncytial virus infection among adult patients presenting with acute respiratory illness at a clinic in Japan, with the aim of evaluating a rapid immunochromatographic antigen test that simultaneously detects RSV, SARS-CoV-2, and influenza viruses A and B. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from adult patients over approximately one year and tested using this rapid antigen platform. While a substantial number of patients tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A, and one for influenza B, no patients tested positive for RSV. Comparison with previous studies that used polymerase chain reaction testing revealed a statistically significantly lower RSV detection rate in the current study. The authors conclude that rapid immunochromatographic antigen testing has limited utility for diagnosing RSV infections in Japanese adults compared to PCR-based approaches.
items.citation: Kajiwara N, Tsunetoshi Y, Shiode S. No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients. 2026

items.title: Performance of an antigen test for detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus-a prospective study.
items.summary: This prospective study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multiplex rapid antigen test capable of simultaneously detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus in patients presenting with acute respiratory infections. The researchers enrolled over a thousand symptomatic patients, including children, comparing nasal swab antigen test results interpreted by emergency department staff against nasopharyngeal PCR results from a central laboratory, and additionally subjected a subset of test device media to PCR analysis. Sensitivity across all four pathogens exceeded approximately four-fifths when using a PCR cycle threshold of thirty as the reference standard, while specificity was perfect for all agents. The study also found that nasal swabs absorbed less viral RNA than nasopharyngeal swabs, a difference that reached statistical significance for influenza A in adults. The authors conclude that the test's high specificity and clinically meaningful sensitivity support its potential use as a marker of infectiousness in acute care settings across different age groups.
items.venue: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

items.title: Analytical comparison of over-the-counter multiplex tests for influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2.
items.summary: This study evaluated the analytical performance of over-the-counter lateral flow tests designed to detect influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2, comparing multiple commercially available products side by side. Researchers prepared contrived specimen panels using propagated viral stocks of several influenza strains and a SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant diluted in clinical matrix, then applied these to each test kit following manufacturer instructions, with results read by blinded evaluators. Across all eight tests and four viruses examined, the lower limits of detection fell within a fourfold dilution range, indicating broadly similar analytical sensitivity among the products. A notable finding was that at low viral concentrations, many tests appeared negative at the start of the interpretation window but converted to a positive result by the end of that window. The authors therefore recommend that users allow the full manufacturer-specified incubation time to elapse before concluding that a result is truly negative.
items.citation: Lohsen S, Hoy-Schulz Y, Taing A et al.. Analytical comparison of over-the-counter multiplex tests for influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The authors structured opposing arguments around four key issues: whether athletes experience greater infection rates than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, and anxiety, the utility of specific biomarkers for monitoring immune health in those performing arduous exercise, and the overall quality of evidence supporting claims about exercise-induced immunosuppression. There is general agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise of short duration is beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older or chronically ill individuals, while high-intensity exercise typical of elite athletes or military personnel has been associated with elevated infection burden. However, the debating groups contested whether exercise per se is causally responsible for increased infection risk, or whether the many other stressors unique to these populations account for the observed effects. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, and the authors conclude that the causal role of exercise itself remains unresolved, calling for more rigorous empirical research.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with particular focus on how exercise modulates immune responses in individuals with such injuries. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search to gather existing research on exercise immunology across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations with spinal cord injury. The paper explains that autonomic dysfunction following spinal cord injury alters resting and post-exercise catecholamine concentrations, which may directly depress immunity given that most lymphoid cells express adrenergic receptors, with individuals with tetraplegia being especially affected. However, the review also identifies exceptions to this pattern, such as preserved mucosal immunity responses to exercise and enhanced natural killer cell cytotoxicity following exercise in those with tetraplegia, suggesting compensatory mechanisms involving sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or neuroendocrine adjustments may offset some deficits. The authors conclude that exercise and rehabilitation can improve certain measures of immunity and autonomic function, positioning exercise as a potential tool to maintain or improve health in this population, while calling for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria L. Goosey‐Tolfrey, Nicolette C. Bishop. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper examines graft-versus-host disease, a serious multi-systemic complication arising when donor immune cells attack host tissues following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, with particular attention to its chronic form and the morbidity it causes. The authors reviewed the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease alongside available evidence from both animal and human studies on the potential role of exercise as an adjunct therapy. Their review suggests that exercise training shows promise for improving physical fitness and possibly immune function while reducing fatigue in patients who have undergone transplantation. However, the authors conclude that the evidence base remains insufficient, calling for more rigorously designed randomized controlled trials focused specifically on patients with graft-versus-host disease.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with the goal of identifying more effective therapeutic targets. The authors analyzed how nociceptive pathways connect the knee joint to the central nervous system, how inflammatory cytokines drive disease, and how organelle-specific dysfunctions—including mitochondrial dysfunction with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization leading to chondrocyte apoptosis, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress causing cartilage degradation—collectively promote disease progression. Building on these mechanistic insights, the review delineates emerging pharmacological strategies aimed at simultaneously addressing inflammatory cascades, restoring organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuating pain signaling. The authors also highlight advanced organelle-targeted drug delivery systems intended to improve therapeutic efficacy and stability. Together, these findings are proposed to establish a multimodal therapeutic framework capable of addressing both the structural degeneration and clinical symptoms of osteoarthritis.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: The distinct roles of ROS in tumor immunity: from mechanisms to immunotherapeutic applications
items.summary: This review examines the dual and context-dependent roles of reactive oxygen species in shaping tumor immunity, proposing a conceptual framework called the "ROS-Immune Mismatch" to describe how redox signaling differentially affects immune cell populations within the tumor microenvironment. The authors analyze how moderate ROS levels promote tumor growth and immunosuppression, while excessive ROS can trigger immunogenic cell death, with outcomes determined by the subcellular location and timing of ROS production. A central mechanistic insight is that cytotoxic T cells are preferentially exhausted by oxidative stress while immunosuppressive regulatory T cells are relatively resistant, representing a fundamental pathway of immune evasion exploited by tumors. The review surveys emerging immunotherapeutic strategies that target these redox dependencies to improve treatment efficacy, alongside translational obstacles such as off-target oxidative toxicity and redox heterogeneity across tumors. Intelligent nanomedicine and redox-reprogrammed cellular therapies are highlighted as promising future directions for precision ROS-targeted immunomodulation.
items.citation: Jiayi Li, Chen Huang, Pan Tang et al.. The distinct roles of ROS in tumor immunity: from mechanisms to immunotherapeutic applications. Journal of Hematology & Oncology. 2026

items.title: Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources
items.summary: This paper describes the experimental validation of a uranium-238-based fission chamber designed to monitor neutron output from the SPARC tokamak across an extremely wide dynamic range of neutron yield rates. The detector uses a parallel-plate geometry combined with borated polyethylene collimation to preferentially detect unscattered fusion neutrons from both deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium reactions. Testing with both types of neutron generators confirmed that the chamber meets vendor-specified detection efficiencies and exhibits excellent linearity, with measured count rates agreeing well with OpenMC neutronics simulations. The study also demonstrated that the detector remains robust under SPARC-relevant operating conditions, including exposure to stray magnetic fields and signal degradation risks from long cable runs. The authors conclude that this fission chamber, when combined with appropriate neutron shielding and pulse height thresholds, constitutes a reliable diagnostic for fusion power measurements in the SPARC neutron diagnostics suite.
items.citation: V. Hagenlocker, R. A. Tinguely, X. Wang et al.. Characterization of a prototype parallel-plate $^{238}$U fission chamber with DD and DT fusion neutron sources. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf
items.summary: The paper investigated "Capotauro," a compact red source discovered in deep JWST imaging that had been proposed as a galaxy candidate at an extraordinarily high redshift based on its extreme infrared colours, with a brown dwarf offering a competing explanation. To distinguish between these possibilities, the authors obtained new medium-band JWST NIRCam imaging roughly three and a half years after the original observations and performed precise relative astrometry using point-spread-function fitting anchored to dozens of compact reference sources. They detected a clear proper motion of the source over the observational baseline, ruling out any extragalactic origin at very high statistical confidence. Comparison of the source's photometric spectral energy distribution with empirical templates identifies Capotauro as a Y-type brown dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 350 K, located at a distance placing it among the most distant Y dwarfs known. The study highlights the power of multi-epoch imaging for identifying cool substellar objects that can masquerade as high-redshift galaxy candidates in deep extragalactic survey fields.
items.citation: F. -Y. F. Liu, D. J. McLeod, B. J. Sutlieff et al.. A clear detection of proper motion confirms that the claimed $\mathbf{z\simeq32}$ galaxy candidate, "Capotauro'', is a Y-type brown dwarf. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics
items.summary: This paper examines how next-generation cosmic microwave background surveys can constrain the effective number of relativistic species in the early universe, a parameter that encodes information about neutrinos and other light relics. Using Fisher-matrix forecasting methods, the authors evaluated several proposed survey configurations for CMB-S4 to determine their projected sensitivity to this parameter. The analysis finds that the conceptual design can achieve a measurement precision better than a threshold representing percent-level sensitivity within its planned observing period, with a revised configuration reaching comparable precision over a longer timescale. The authors also quantify an upper bound on achievable improvement by computing the cosmic-variance limit over the same angular scale range. To support the broader community, the forecasting pipeline is made publicly available as a tool capable of simulating foreground separation, delensing, and parameter sensitivity for arbitrary CMB survey designs.
items.citation: Cynthia Trendafilova, Srinivasan Raghunathan, Benjamin Wallisch et al.. Sensitivity of Next-Generation CMB Surveys to Neutrinos and Other Light Relics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation
items.summary: The paper investigates the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation, a model for phase separation in active matter systems, focusing on both its mathematical well-posedness and the dynamics by which phase-separated domains grow and coarsen over time. The authors analyze the equation under both regular polynomial and singular logarithmic potentials, employing a heteroclinic trajectory method in the phase plane to characterize static kink profiles and spherical droplet states, and developing a theory of activity- and curvature-modified surface tension. This theoretical framework explains a conjectured shift in the coarsening power law for characteristic domain length from the classical exponent corresponding to model B dynamics to a slower exponent induced by activity, with the analysis revealing this shift to be a transient phenomenon preceding saturation at a finite length scale. A finite element numerical scheme is designed and proven to be well-posed and stable for both potential types, with convergence analysis in two and three dimensions establishing local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions, and global-in-time well-posedness established in one dimension under a smallness condition on the activity parameter. Numerical simulations confirm that the scheme correctly reproduces phase separation dynamics and that the predicted power-law shift in coarsening behavior is observed prior to late-time length saturation, consistent with the theoretical predictions.
items.citation: Abramo Agosti, Andrea Giorgini. Numerical analysis and coarsening dynamics of the Active Cahn-Hilliard equation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules
items.summary: This paper reports the experimental observation of weakly-bound ultralong-range Rydberg molecules formed from rubidium atoms in excited Rydberg states combined with a ground-state rubidium atom, specifically investigating the rarely observed Π-symmetry electronic states. The molecules were detected across a range of principal quantum numbers, and their Π-state character was identified through a multiplet structure arising from spin-spin coupling between the Rydberg and valence electrons, analogous to the Zeeman effect. The binding energy was found to decrease rapidly with increasing principal quantum number, scaling with a high inverse power of the effective quantum number, which indicates that lower principal quantum numbers are most favorable for studying these states. Experimental results were compared to Green's function-based theoretical calculations and showed good agreement across most of the studied range, though discrepancies at the lowest principal quantum number studied suggest that the standard Fermi pseudopotential approximation begins to break down at low quantum numbers.
items.citation: Matthew T. Eiles, Aleksandr Zaitsev, Dominik Dorer et al.. Observation of $Π$-symmetry ultralong-range Rydberg molecules. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.summary: This paper investigated the fragmented landscape of open-source tools designed to mitigate risks associated with large language models in enterprise settings, where the rapid move from pilot to production has made manual harm identification difficult to scale. The researchers developed a structured, taxonomy-driven protocol that uses a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation to automatically analyze the source code and documentation of prominent open-source tools and map their capabilities onto a comprehensive AI risk mitigation taxonomy. By aligning tool capabilities to dozens of subcategories spanning technical, operational, governance, legal, and financial risk domains, the study revealed a heavily skewed distribution in which existing tools cluster around technical and operational controls while governance, regulatory, and financial risk categories remain largely unaddressed. The mapping pipeline achieved reasonable classification performance after majority voting, and independent reviewer agreement reached moderate levels, lending confidence to the findings. The authors conclude that effective enterprise AI risk mitigation requires a layered architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes, and they identify specific areas where human oversight remains essential.
items.citation: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj et al.. Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, summarizing how new evidence has shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection has been established as a core screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through multiple classes of rapid nucleic acid amplification tests deployed at or near the point of care. Novel specimen types such as tongue swabs and non-sputum samples including stool and nasopharyngeal material have improved bacteriological confirmation in children and others unable to produce sputum, and targeted next-generation sequencing has been endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Host blood transcriptomic signatures show promising prognostic and triage performance, and proteomic, metabolomic, and other biomarker approaches are advancing through evaluation, yet no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The authors conclude that substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain despite these considerable scientific and policy advances.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped research on artificial intelligence–enhanced point-of-care and rapid diagnostic technologies for infectious diseases in resource-limited settings, examining disease coverage, geographic representation, and validation quality. Following established scoping review methodology, the authors searched five major databases spanning over a decade of literature, screening more than a thousand records and ultimately including over two hundred studies for analysis. The field was found to be growing rapidly, with nearly half of included publications appearing in the most recent period, and the research landscape was dominated by three diseases—COVID-19, malaria, and tuberculosis—while neglected tropical diseases remained markedly underrepresented. Convolutional neural networks were the most commonly employed artificial intelligence approach, and microscopy-based diagnostics were the most frequent modality, yet the vast majority of studies lacked prospective field validation, with only a small fraction having been tested in real-world conditions. The authors conclude that despite impressive growth, the field suffers from critical gaps in validation rigor, disease equity, and geographic breadth, and they call for future work to prioritize field validation, broaden disease focus, and meaningfully engage end-user communities from the outset of study design.
items.venue: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
items.citation: Farquhar H. AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.. Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for simultaneous point-of-care detection of multiple respiratory pathogens. The system combines a polymethyl methacrylate rotating disc pre-loaded with lyophilized CRISPR/Cas13a reagents, a portable fluorescence analyzer, and a novel resin-based nucleic acid purification method, enabling automated multiplexed testing after simple sample loading. The platform can screen six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples in a single run, achieving single-copy analytical sensitivity without cross-reactivity between targets. Clinical validation using retrospective patient throat swab specimens demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity compared to reference methods. The authors conclude that iCARD represents a robust, high-throughput, and accurate tool suitable for decentralized molecular diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.
items.summary: This review paper examines point-of-care testing technologies for infectious diseases, focusing on their role in early disease screening, epidemic surveillance, and public health prevention. The authors systematically surveyed recent innovations across molecular diagnostics, microfluidic systems, biosensing technologies, and artificial intelligence as applied to field-deployable diagnostics. The paper also analyzes the quality assessment frameworks used to evaluate these technologies, considering metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, stability, and practical field applicability. Particular emphasis is placed on deployment strategies for resource-limited settings, including approaches to optimizing technical suitability, resource allocation, and local support infrastructure. The review concludes by identifying current challenges and proposing future development directions intended to guide further research and implementation of infectious disease point-of-care testing.
items.citation: Zhang YX, Ru JF. Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.
items.summary: This paper examines the importance of infectious disease diagnostic competencies in medical education as a foundation for building long-term professional resilience against infectious disease challenges. The authors argue that courses in medical microbiology, virology, and hygiene must develop clinical competence encompassing the One-Health concept, covering epidemiology, prevention, diagnostics, and therapy within the context of pathogen transmissibility. They contend that proficiency in rapid and appropriate infection diagnostics is essential for evidence-based practice, underpinning rational antimicrobial therapy and thereby helping to prevent the emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens. The paper emphasizes that skills such as correct sample collection, test selection, and critical interpretation of microbiological findings cannot be acquired through self-directed learning alone but require structured, practice-oriented, hands-on training. The authors conclude that these core competencies are indispensable for infection prevention, outbreak control, and therapeutic decision-making, and must be prioritized in medical curricula despite the time and resource demands they entail.
items.citation: Brandt C, Becker K, Ciesek S et al.. Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.. GMS infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents the updated clinical practice recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for the management of rheumatoid arthritis using synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. An international task force conducted systematic literature reviews on drug safety and efficacy, then used a structured voting process to revise and consolidate guidance based on evidence accumulated since the prior update. The resulting framework was streamlined to a smaller set of overarching principles and recommendations covering conventional agents such as methotrexate, biologic therapies targeting various immune pathways, and targeted synthetic drugs including Janus kinase inhibitors. The recommendations advise initiating treatment with methotrexate combined with short-term glucocorticoids, escalating to a biologic agent after an inadequate response, and considering Janus kinase inhibitors only after careful evaluation of cardiovascular, malignancy, and thromboembolic risks. Guidance is also provided on sequencing therapies after treatment failure, tapering drugs upon sustained remission with caution against full cessation, and balancing efficacy against safety and cost considerations.
items.citation: Josef S. Smolen, Christopher J. Edwards, Victoria Konzett et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and its dysregulation across a broad spectrum of diseases, with particular emphasis on immune cell biology. The authors synthesize the historical development of lipid metabolism research and detail how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways regulate the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of immune cell types including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review explores multilevel regulatory mechanisms—spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational layers—that govern how lipid metabolites shape both innate and adaptive immune responses. Disease contexts covered include autoimmune conditions, cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, aging, and metabolic disorders, illustrating the breadth of pathological consequences arising from lipid metabolic disruption. The authors conclude by surveying therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, the state of relevant clinical trials, and emerging directions such as lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and effective integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. It also evaluates how artificial intelligence is being applied to enhance signal processing and generate predictive health insights from the data these devices collect. Despite significant progress, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of AI-derived outputs. The authors synthesize developments across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to provide a comprehensive overview of the field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026
