items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for an automated conversational assessment system called the "Socratic Test," designed to address limitations in both traditional written exams and oral examinations. The authors argue that static assessments penalize ambitious attempts and obscure useful diagnostic information, while face-to-face oral exams introduce construct-irrelevant variance through anxiety and power imbalances. The proposed system integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy, and the SOLO Taxonomy within a computer-mediated, multimodal environment to actively probe the boundaries of student understanding in real time. A key feature is the formalization of graduated scaffolding as a means of quantifying the Zone of Proximal Development, paired with an additive, non-compensatory grading architecture that rewards demonstrated mastery rather than penalizing errors. The paper also claims that human-AI alignment within this framework can achieve superior measurement reliability compared to conventional assessment approaches.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform with broad potential across energy, environmental, and healthcare applications. The authors survey its synthesis chemistry, property modification strategies, and structural characteristics, including its tunable band gap, high surface area, and capacity for surface functionalization that enables configurations ranging from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers applications in environmental remediation such as adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, plastics, and pathogens, as well as energy-related uses including hydrogen production, carbon dioxide photoreduction, and battery technologies. Sensing applications, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for detecting biological and organic molecules, are also discussed alongside healthcare platforms. The authors acknowledge that despite its considerable promise, graphene oxide faces practical challenges around scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and they propose potential solutions to support its sustainable advancement toward real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Aptamer-gated luminescence enhancement and red-shift in a MOF: a ratiometric and color-tonality visual biosensor for pathogenic E. coli detection
items.citation: Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen, Payam B. Hassan et al.. Aptamer-gated luminescence enhancement and red-shift in a MOF: a ratiometric and color-tonality visual biosensor for pathogenic E. coli detection. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-enabled traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments in three-dimensional printing, modular architectures, and flexible substrates, alongside progress in biosensor integration for detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have expanded clinical applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also identify persistent challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be widely adopted in routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and healthcare costs. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical evaluation of existing diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review addresses therapeutic strategies spanning empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance, including the potential role of combination therapy. Emerging diagnostic technologies, novel antifungal agents in clinical development, and compounds targeting new fungal pathways are highlighted as promising advances. The paper also looks toward future directions including artificial intelligence applications in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches, with the overall aim of guiding clinicians and researchers in managing this evolving clinical challenge.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology
items.summary: This review examines non-Faradaic impedance biosensors, which detect biological targets by measuring changes in electrical properties without requiring electrochemical reactions, and addresses their historically limited sensitivity. The authors survey three complementary strategies for improving sensor performance: micro- and nanoparticle-based signal amplification, microfluidic integration to improve analyte transport to sensor surfaces, and CMOS on-chip integration for high spatiotemporal resolution. By combining these approaches, recent platforms have achieved detection limits reaching the femtomolar range for proteins and sensitivity down to single bacteria, representing substantial gains over conventional non-Faradaic methods. The review analyzes the individual strengths and limitations of each strategy alongside their synergistic potential, and outlines emerging directions in materials and system integration. The authors propose a roadmap for translating these advances into practical biosensing platforms for healthcare diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and biomedical research.
items.citation: Nam-Seog Kim, Jungkyu Kim. Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional blood culture is slow and often insufficiently sensitive. Researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay coupled with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using a set of ten primers optimized to run at a fixed temperature for forty minutes. The assay achieved femtogram-level analytical sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains, and the complete workflow from nucleic acid extraction to visual readout was finished within approximately one hour. Clinical validation using sterile body fluid specimens from neonates with suspected *E. coli* infection showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR and substantially higher positivity rates than conventional culture. The authors conclude that this method offers a rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective tool for point-of-care *E. coli* detection, especially suited to resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: The paper investigated a biosensor strategy for detecting *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major foodborne pathogen, at trace levels. The researchers designed a system that couples DNAzyme-catalysed amplification with hybridization chain reaction to convert target recognition into branched DNA nanowires bearing PAM sequences, which then activate CRISPR/Cas12a to cleave the nanowires and restore a quenched fluorescence signal. This cascaded target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment approach achieved an exceptionally low detection limit and a linear range spanning several orders of magnitude in bacterial concentration. The biosensor demonstrated straightforward operation and rapid response, and the authors propose that by swapping the recognition and primer sequences, the platform could be adapted for sensitive detection of other foodborne pathogens.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a major foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor. The system simultaneously targets two key genetic markers of the pathogen by exploiting the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins, creating dual fluorescence channels that enable serotype-specific identification within a single reaction tube. Target gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing were all integrated to eliminate complex equipment and reduce contamination risk. The biosensor achieved high sensitivity in controlled testing and was validated using fecal samples from a mouse infection model, with results consistent with standard PCR methods. The authors claim this dual-channel approach improves specificity and serotype discrimination over conventional CRISPR diagnostics, offering a simple, field-deployable tool for food safety, clinical diagnostics, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor platform designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The sensor uses disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which are attached via π-π stacking to preserve the material's electronic properties and high surface area without requiring on-surface chemical reactions. A key technical advance was a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduced sensor preparation time from many hours to just two minutes while maintaining detection performance. The platform achieved amplification-free and label-free detection of the colistin resistance gene with low picomolar sensitivity against bacterial plasmid targets, clearly discriminating complementary from non-complementary sequences, and was readily retargeted to a different resistance gene by simply swapping the probe. The biosensor demonstrated consistent reproducibility across independently fabricated devices, supporting its potential for scalable manufacture and decentralized diagnostic deployment against antimicrobial resistance and pandemic threats.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.
items.summary: This review examined advances in biosensor technologies specifically designed to detect two major foodborne pathogens, *Salmonella* spp. and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which are among the leading causes of foodborne illness and death globally. Rather than broadly surveying biosensing across many pathogens, the authors conducted a pathogen-specific analysis mapping trends in bioreceptor development and transducer selection for these two organisms. A distinctive contribution is the first examination of how artificial intelligence tools can accelerate biosensor design, optimization, and decision-making specifically for detecting these pathogens. The review also critically evaluates which biosensing strategies hold genuine potential for scalability, portability, and routine deployment in food industry settings, thereby addressing the gap between laboratory development and real-world application. The authors present the work as a practical roadmap intended to guide future biosensor research toward field-ready, industry-relevant detection solutions.
items.citation: Gumush SE, Al-Attar R, Sandbecker E et al.. Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.. Food chemistry. Molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated the detection of three bacterial pathogens — *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella typhimurium*, and *Staphylococcus aureus* — using a biosensing platform that combines plasmonic nanomaterials with deep learning-based signal analysis. The researchers fabricated a nanostructured electrochemical biosensor incorporating gold nanoparticle–graphene oxide hybrid nanocomposites to exploit localized surface plasmon resonance and enhance charge-transfer kinetics. Raw voltammetric signals from the sensor were processed by a hybrid deep neural network combining a MobileNet-Transformer architecture for feature extraction with a Gated Recurrent Unit for temporal noise reduction. The integrated system achieved extremely low limits of detection for all three pathogens using only a small sample volume and a rapid assay time, while outperforming baseline convolutional and recurrent neural network models in classification accuracy and discriminative performance. The authors claim this approach offers a scalable, portable, and AI-assisted biosensing solution suitable for food safety, environmental monitoring, and point-of-care diagnostics at performance levels comparable to laboratory benchtop systems.
items.citation: Mansour S, Negm N, Alhashmi AA et al.. Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines the production of dark photons as a dark matter candidate through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation, a mechanism known as stochastic misalignment. The framework is predictive but faces constraints from two sources: structure formation, because the produced dark photons are initially relativistic and thus boosted, and inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which demand small quartic self-couplings of the dark Higgs. By accounting for these constraints, the authors identify a viable parameter space spanning dark photon masses from hundreds of electron volts to around a gigaelectronvolt and very small gauge couplings consistent with the observed dark matter relic abundance. If kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the Standard Model photon is present at a generic level, this parameter space narrows further and becomes accessible to direct detection experiments and diffuse soft gamma-ray searches, while the broader favored region could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of planted noisy k-XOR detection and recovery, as well as strong refutation of random k-XOR, focusing on the precise trade-off between the number of clauses, signal strength, and runtime. The authors analyze the Kikuchi hierarchy, a family of spectral algorithms indexed by a level parameter, which was conjectured to achieve a smooth curve relating clause count to runtime but had previously only been shown to do so up to polylogarithmic factors that degrade the running time exponent. By introducing a normalized variant of the Kikuchi matrix and developing sharp combinatorial counts of closed walks in the associated trace expansion, the authors prove that this normalized hierarchy exactly achieves the conjectured sharp trade-off at every arity of three or greater, eliminating all logarithmic losses. Their algorithms accomplish strong detection, weak and exact recovery, and strong refutation with sum-of-squares certificates, and they also establish matching lower bounds in the same model; additionally, a quantum variant yields a quartic speedup for detection and weak recovery. The results extend to more general planting laws and predicates, and the walk-counting techniques developed also resolve a longstanding conjecture on hypergraph Moore bounds.
items.citation: Alexander Schmidhuber, Matthew B. Hastings. The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented and poorly interoperable fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) systems in HVAC buildings by developing a structured semantic framework. The researchers constructed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology designed to formally represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships using well-defined controlled vocabulary. The ontology explicitly encodes contributing cause–fault–symptom–impact relationships to enable machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and mapping of heterogeneous FDD outputs across diverse data sources and equipment types. FDD-ON was evaluated using publicly available VAV HVAC system datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications. The authors conclude that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable FDD solutions, including digital twin frameworks and artificial intelligence-driven maintenance decision-making systems.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC
items.summary: This paper investigates the prospects for detecting light scalar sgoldstinos — hypothetical particles arising from supersymmetry breaking — at the SND@HL-LHC experiment. The study covers the mass range from the dimuon threshold up to a few GeV, examining effective sgoldstino interactions with Standard Model particles, dominant production mechanisms through meson decays, and existing experimental constraints on the relevant parameter space. The authors analyze the geometry and kinematics of the proposed SND@HL-LHC detector, paying particular attention to the spatial separation of muon–antimuon pairs produced when sgoldstinos decay within the detector volume. Using two representative sets of supersymmetry-breaking parameters, they derive sensitivity estimates for the experiment. A key finding is that the efficiency with which the detector can resolve the two muon tracks must be carefully accounted for when designing or interpreting dimuon signal searches.
items.citation: D. Kalashnikov, E. K. Karkaryan. Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding
items.summary: This paper investigated how to reduce the computational cost of processing source code as images in multimodal large language models, where rendering code visually is appealing but wastes tokens on blank space and irrelevant content. The authors developed CodeShrink, a framework combining three components: a blank-free rendering approach that replaces whitespace-heavy layouts with compact representations, a reinforcement learning-trained agent that selects an optimal compression configuration per input, and an instruction-aware mechanism that prunes visual tokens irrelevant to the current task during inference. The framework was evaluated on code question answering, clone detection, and code completion benchmarks. CodeShrink achieved substantial reductions in visual token usage while matching or surpassing uncompressed text-only baselines and outperforming other text-based and visual compression methods across all tasks. The results demonstrate that combining layout compaction, adaptive configuration selection, and instruction-guided token pruning can make multimodal code understanding substantially more efficient.
items.citation: Wenxin Tang, Jingyu Xiao, Zhenyu Liu et al.. CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain
items.summary: The paper investigates Majorana modes in a quantum spin chain when its parameters are tuned to lie along special parametric curves called disorder lines, where the ground state becomes disentangled and certain correlation functions lose their dependence on spatial separation. Using exact results for the XY spin chain in a transverse field, also known as the Kitaev chain in the Majorana representation, the study examines how Majorana modes behave in this disentangled regime. Single Majorana modes are found to remain localized near the ends of the chain, consistent with behavior away from the disorder lines, but multi-particle Majorana modes with two or more particles penetrate into the bulk without any attenuation — a phenomenon the authors call "unwithered" modes. These bulk-edge effects, arising from the interplay between disentanglement and Majorana physics, are predicted to be experimentally detectable in specially engineered optical chains and lattices.
items.citation: Gennady Y. Chitov. Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain. arXiv. 2026
